532488|2026-03.headline: Divi's Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT rose to ₹963 crores (vs ₹864 crores YoY) and PAT to ₹751 crores, while management guided only to "stable" margins.
532488|2026-03.overview: Divi's reported Q4 FY26 consolidated total income of ₹2,986 crores, PBT of ₹963 crores and PAT of ₹751 crores, including a ₹90 crore forex gain. For FY26, total income rose to ₹11,067 crores from ₹9,712 crores, PAT to ₹2,568 crores from ₹2,191 crores, after a one-time ₹74 crore Labour Code charge. Management said volumes in generics were stable with some pricing pressure, while West Asia-related disruption raised raw material, solvent and freight costs and forced some suppliers to declare force majeure. Management declined to quantify FY27 margins, guiding only to stable margins and double-digit revenue growth.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹2,916 crores in FY25; after ₹74 crore Labour Code exceptional charge

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Volumes stable and healthy through Q4 and FY26 per management, but slight pricing pressure; generic API contracts have variability clauses with reviews as often as every 3 months. FY26 product mix was 45% generics.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis (CS)
segments.commentary: FY26 product mix was 55% CS. Management cited a strong project pipeline across Phase II/III, validation and qualification stages; late life-cycle management volumes may decline as products mature.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Several fragments validated in the quarter with more in pipeline; capabilities include protected amino acids, solid-phase and liquid-phase synthesis, and 3,000-litre SPPS capacity.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Iodine-based contrast media in commercial sales to innovators, supplied in multiple tonnes; Gadolinium compounds still at qualification as customers' products are in Phase II/III.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹946 crores in FY26, up from ₹781 crores in FY25.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth, consistent with its historical stated aim.
Margins expected to 'remain stable' per management; no numerical margin figure given due to current scenario.
Freight-related cost pressures expected to continue in the near term and have been factored into planning.
FY27 capex expected to be roughly constant unless a major CS or new project emerges (CWIP about ₹2,000 crore odd).
Inventory build expected mainly from Q1 FY27 to secure material; no percentage given.
Management expects Kakinada dedicated CS projects to commercialise by 2027, earlier or later, subject to customer regulatory approvals.

Kakinada ₹1,500 crore expansion plan; ₹600 crores already capitalised.
Unit 3 (Kakinada) now supports backward integration; select activities moved from Unit 1 and Unit 2 to free GMP space, with moves timed 2-4 months ahead of customer qualification approvals.
Three dedicated CS projects are in validation and supply stage; commercial volumes depend on customer regulatory approval and volume indication.
Capital allocation to CS and peptides, with long-term supply agreements; management guides toward a 2-year range from capex to revenue, but acknowledged timelines from 6 months to 3 years.
demand_pricing: Generic volumes rose in FY26 from existing portfolio; new molecules from customer launches expected to add volume in coming years as products come off patent.
Generic pricing under competitive pressure; customers understanding of market conditions has supported ongoing price discussions.

Raw material prices rising with West Asia conflict; some suppliers invoked force majeure; Ammonia and methanol sourcing affected. Management says cost increases are being passed through where feasible.
No loss of volumes or supply issues with customers reported in Q4; no revenue loss from logistics issues.
Exports about 89% of sales; Europe and US together about 74% of export revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind on raw material availability, and how is methanol sourcing being managed for H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the conflict affected only about one month of FY26 and there were no production stoppages, but sourcing is difficult across solvents and other materials; availability is being reviewed quarterly, with securing supply for the next 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a margin figure, saying it is difficult to project but expected to remain stable; capex for FY27 expected to be constant unless a major CS project emerges.

qa_highlights.question: Why was constant currency growth only about 6% despite capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Most capex was capitalised late in the year; management said it will now track reported revenue growth instead, citing currency volatility, and attributed slower growth to generic pricing pressure rather than a single product.

qa_highlights.question: What would it take to return to 38% margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said generic pricing pressure and higher material costs (rising again due to the war) are the key drags; a return to 38% depends on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: How long from capex to revenue for the new long-term CS supply agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for about 2 years but timelines range from 6 months to 3 years, depending on customer approvals and regulatory queries.

qa_highlights.question: How do the rupee depreciation and raw material and freight cost pressures net out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency gains help as the company is export-led, but a rupee reversal would also hurt; about 40% of raw material spend is imported, on total raw material spend of ₹4,000-5,000 crores against ₹11,000 crore revenue.

risks_watch: Raw material and solvent availability and cost, including methanol and ammonia, given force majeure declarations and Middle East-linked disruption.
Freight cost increases expected to continue near term.
Generic pricing pressure, with contract reviews possibly every 3 months.
Timing of CS and dedicated project commercialisation depends on customer regulatory approvals; Kakinada dedicated project targeted around 2027 with no firm date.
Gadolinium contrast media remains at Phase II/III qualification stage, so no near-term revenue visible.
Inventory build expected from Q1 FY27, which could weigh on working capital.
Margin visibility limited; management withheld numerical guidance.
532488|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operational continuity and supply reliability, but cautious and guarded on margins and project timelines, repeatedly declining to quantify FY27 margins, capex timing or customer volumes.
key_quotes: Despite these external challenges, the availability of critical raw materials and solvents remained broadly manageable.
So we wouldn't see so much of an effect of what is happening on the yearly results, neither on the quarterly results because it's only one-third.
We are hopeful by 2027 it will be commercialized or earlier or maybe later.

tone.note: Management was confident on supply continuity, no production stoppages and double-digit growth, but cautious on FY27 margins, capex timing and CS project timelines (6 months to 3 years); analysts pushed on margin outlook, the 38% margin path, and why constant-currency growth was only about 6%.

532488|2026-06.headline: Divi's Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to ₹891 crores (from ₹557 crores), with Custom Synthesis at 60% of revenue and management guiding to double-digit growth.
532488|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was ₹3,144 crores versus ₹2,529 crores a year earlier, and consolidated PAT was ₹902 crores versus ₹545 crores. Standalone revenue grew 10% in constant currency, with Custom Synthesis at 60% and Generics at 40% of revenue. Gross margin and inventory build were the main swing factors: the company stocked solvents and raw materials on a rolling three-month basis at higher cost and also built validation-batch inventory, and management said margins should be read on a full-year basis. Management declined to quantify commercial ramp-up timelines for the three capex projects, citing CDAs and regulatory timing.

financial_highlights.change: vs net gain of ₹39 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Change in inventory (as cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: vs ₹50-100 crores run rate per analysts

segments.name: Custom Synthesis
segments.commentary: Contributed 60% of standalone revenue in Q1 FY27. Three major capex projects are in validation and about 70% of their combined ~₹2,000 crore cost has been capitalised. Management said the company has about 18 to 20 projects commercialised or being commercialised.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Contributed 40% of standalone revenue. Volumes were stable and pricing reflected competitive conditions; management said about 4 DMFs have been filed, with Brivaracetam and Ticagrelor under customer qualification and commercial volumes expected in 3 to 6 months after qualification.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹298 crores versus ₹250 crores a year earlier, and about ₹240 crores in Q4 FY26 per analyst. Portfolio is over 100 offerings, and the company is expanding capabilities and capacity.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and said it would show double-digit growth 'no matter what'; it did not give a specific gross or EBITDA margin figure.
Management said full-year gross margin is about 60% and EBITDA margin is similar to last year, but Q1 gross margin was about 68% and the company does not expect that level to persist.

Commercial volumes from the validated capex projects depend on customer qualification and agency approvals; no firm timing was given beyond the 'later part of the current financial year' referenced in analyst questions.
Iodine-based contrast media: long-term contracts being signed with two customers; one has started commercialisation and the second is expected to start in the next few months.
Gadolinium contrast media remains in Phase II/III customer qualification, with the customer awaiting regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Three major capex projects are nearing completion with validations ongoing; about ₹2,000 crores in total and about 70% capitalised so far.
Capitalised assets during Q1 were ₹451 crores; capital work in progress was ₹2,034 crores as of June 30, 2026.
Utilisation across Units 1, 2 and 3 is about 80% to 85% (CFO said ~85% across all three units).

Unit 3 at Kakinada is being used for pre-chemistry and backward-integrated work; the company is filling it with pre-chemistry products while regulatory qualification of the plant, which could take 1 to 2 years, is pursued.
Peptides: expanding solid-phase and liquid-phase peptide synthesis, including acquiring several additional 3,000-litre SPPS units.
demand_pricing: Solvent costs rose sharply, with some solvents nearly doubling or tripling in price due to West Asia disruption; the company passed through some costs and raised prices slightly where possible.
Management attributed generic price increases to raw material cost pass-through rather than a durable end of pricing pressure.
Freight rates remained elevated, and ocean and air logistics faced port congestion, blank sailings and longer transit times.
Exports were about 90% of standalone revenue; Europe and North America were 75% of exports.
Management declined to name competitors and said Divi's differentiates through full backward integration from raw materials, in-house resins and protected amino acids.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical ramp from validation quantities to commercial quantities for dedicated capex projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing CDAs and product-specific variability. Commercial volumes start only after validation, customer qualification and agency approval.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory build (≈₹500 crores change in inventory) normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is holding a rolling three-month stock of materials at higher cost to avoid production or shipment stoppages, and validation batches also add to inventory. Management said the inventory level depends on Middle East macro conditions and would fall if costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year margins compare with last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year gross margin is about 60% and EBITDA margin is similar to last year, with lumpiness by quarter. Q1 gross margin was about 68% and the next quarter may be higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is solvent pricing softening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices were flat for a few weeks and then rose again depending on Middle East news. Supply is not always easily available, so the company is holding inventory three months ahead rather than just-in-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Gadolinium contrast media project?
qa_highlights.answer: It is still in customer Phase II and III qualification and is on a slow track while the customer awaits regulatory approval. Validation has not yet been completed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in the gross margin line this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management said there was no inventory gain recorded in Q1.

risks_watch: Solvent and raw material cost volatility tied to West Asia; prices can rise again within weeks, and the 3-month inventory policy ties up working capital (inventory ₹4,413 crores).
Timing of regulatory approvals (FDA and other agencies) for the three capex projects and the Brivaracetam/Ticagrelor DMFs; approvals drive the Custom Synthesis mix shift.
Gross margin normalisation after Q1's approximately 68% level, and the inventory-change swing from roughly ₹50-100 crores run rate to about ₹500 crores.
Net forex loss of ₹7 crores in Q1 versus a gain of ₹39 crores a year earlier; INR movements affect reported margins.
Freight and logistics disruption affecting export schedules, and the need to watch validation-to-commercial conversion for the Kakinada Unit 3 site.

So whatever you're seeing right now is a market correction based on the raw material prices that have taken a substantial hit.
We would say, if you want to look at a revenue projection, we are looking at double-digit growth.

532488|2026-09.headline: Divis Labs Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 32% YoY to Rs 3,770 crore and PAT rose 64% to Rs 1,127 crore.
532488|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income was Rs 3,770 crore (up ~32% YoY) with PBT of Rs 1,505 crore (up 65%) and PAT of Rs 1,127 crore (up ~64%). For H1, total income reached Rs 6,907 crore (vs Rs 5,389 crore) and PAT Rs 2,029 crore (vs Rs 1,234 crore). Management said demand and volumes were healthy, though pricing pressure persists in some categories and input and logistics costs are elevated due to Middle East disruption. Management reiterated guidance of double-digit revenue growth but declined to quantify validation-batch contribution, peptide capacity or margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why has cost containment helped gross margin while volumes grew about 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wider supplier cost inflation, but attributed the material cost ratio drop from 40% to 32% to a higher CDMO mix and backward integration at Unit 1 and Kakinada.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not comment on specific products or customers, and that the product could have gone generic.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO before tax was about Rs 9.59 crore for H1; management attributed it to the large capex cycle, with about Rs 870 crore of work in progress and advances to suppliers.

qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 2,000 crore plus or minus 20% per year, based on RFPs; segment-wise split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid-phase is a well-established capability, and that pilot-scale capacity can be scaled as needed; no major liquid-phase expansion was described.

532493|2026-03.headline: FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores in line with guidance; order book INR2,141 crores standalone and FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%.
532493|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores, in line with the start-of-year guidance, with operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores a year earlier. Q4 billing was INR490 crores (up 16% YoY) and Q4 fresh orders were about INR530 crores, taking the standalone order book to INR2,141 crores at 31 March 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% and guided to roughly INR1,600 crores-plus of orders in FY27, with a board-approved in-principle demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business. The call leaned heavily on a long-range "near-triple turnover in 4.5-5.5 years" narrative, with proprietary IP products and the Su-30 upgrade positioned as upside rather than included in the numbers.

532497|2026-09.headline: Radico Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA margin 20.4%, with P&A volume up 36% and FY27 P&A volume guidance raised to 30%.
532497|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with IMFL volume above 10 million cases (+7% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA of Rs 356 crore at a 20.4% margin (+462 bps YoY). Prestige & Above (P&A) volume hit a record 5.28 million cases, up 36%, while the Regular category declined about 15% after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and Maharashtra and Karnataka policy changes. Gross margin was 48.0%, up 440 bps YoY but down 109 bps QoQ, with packaging inflation costing about Rs 27 crore. The company upgraded FY27 P&A volume growth guidance to 30% and kept EBITDA margin guidance at around 20%. Leadership changes: Dilip Banthiya joined the Board as Executive Director and CFO, and Saket Somani was elevated to Deputy CFO.

segments.name: Regular

segments.commentary: IMFL EBITDA margin is about 24%+ in Q2; non-IMFL margin is about 9.5-10%.

segments.name: Vodka
segments.commentary: Vodka reached 6.3% of IMFL in Q2, up from 3.7% in 2025 and 4.5% in 2026. Flavoured vodka is about 75% of Radico's vodka; vodka is about 30% of Radico's volume.

532504|2026-03.headline: Navin Fluorine Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR938 crore with EBITDA margin of 34.2%; FY26 PAT more than doubled to INR664 crore.

segments.name: Advanced materials (incubating within HPP)
segments.commentary: Not separately reported. Chemours liquid cooling project targeted for completion by end Q2 FY27; Chemours reportedly sold about $1 million of two-phase cooling liquid in the quarter (per analyst). DRDO TDF partnership announced.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in the 32-33% range (plus/minus 1%) on a normalised basis over the next one to two years, supported by HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity.
CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million reiterated; FY29 asset turn of 3x on INR288 crore cGMP4 capex stated as the near-term view.
Gross margin dipped about 100 bps QoQ from Q4 FY26 on raw material costs; management said price pass-through will lag.
Advanced materials adoption capex (INR90 crore) to be done in two phases, first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 for commercial-scale qualification; not included in any return projections.
Growth visibility beyond FY28 depends on the current capex cycle (cGMP Phase 1, adoption capacity, Chemours).
capex_capacity: New advanced materials adoption capex of INR90 crore, internally funded, to be set up at Surat; creates two core platforms and augments analytical equipment.
CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2 capex of INR125 crore (part of INR288 crore approved Feb 2024), operationalisation expected Q4 FY27; Phase 1 operational in Q3 FY26. Dedicated to European CDMO partner.

HFC capacity addition of up to 15,000 MT of R32 on track for Q3 FY27; company currently has about 9,000-10,000 MT and total would be about 25,000 MT. Revenue band of INR600-825 crore cited from original capex approval.
MPP debottlenecking at Dahej on track for completion by Q3 FY27; management cited 2x asset turn.
AHF capacity of 60,000 MT between Surat and Dahej seen as adequate for the next 4-5 years; AHF commissioned in the subsidiary NFASL.
Renewable project of INR15.73 crore (14.9 MW hybrid) expected to supply more than 60% of energy needs once operational.
demand_pricing: R32: management expects a 35-45% contracted share of capacity over five years; a couple of contracts signed and more at a late stage.
R32 long-term demand said to double over a decade while quota-driven supply shrinks by half; Indian oversupply expected for about five years with exports to global market.
Specialty chemicals: volume recovering, but pricing pressure persists in LatAm; 13-14 new molecules launched last year and 5 new molecules being participated in, of which 3 are patented.
HFO supply to Honeywell: asset commercialised July 2022; original seven-year term with a three-year extension at Honeywell's option, so runway beyond FY29.
Management stated that raw material cost inflation is rising amid global war tensions and supply chain risk.

qa_highlights.question: Advanced materials: end-use applications, and growth beyond FY28 given current capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to make advanced materials a material business unit by end of decade, modelled on today's CDMO. Focus on data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defence; the adoption capex is phased, with first phase complete around mid-Q4 FY27 to start commercial-scale qualification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR90 crore adoption capex a pilot or commercial scale, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said five products are already lab-approved and this capex takes them to commercial-scale qualification; not a pilot. No asset turn is assumed in numbers for the INR90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: R32 pricing and India capacity additions versus quota start in Jan 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give pricing; said it will stay the lowest-cost R32 producer through its integrated HF chain and renewable power. Expects India oversupply for about five years and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary (NFASL) margin fall about 12 pp QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campaign mix differs quarter to quarter, and AHF transfers from Dahej to Surat are at arm's-length, so value shows up at Navin Fluorine (NFIL) level; group margin remains solid.

qa_highlights.question: CDMO: is the new capacity dedicated, and is the MSA for an extra molecule with the same customer?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity dedicated to European CDMO partner; an MSA for an extra molecule in the same supply chain takes Navin to API minus 1. Also working on an early-phase molecule with the same customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $100 million CDMO target for FY27 still on track, and is INR900 crore cGMP capex math right?
qa_highlights.answer: $100 million target reiterated as on track. Management confirmed the 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29, and that Phase 1 and Phase 2 combined are about INR900 crore is not exactly right; the INR288 crore figure is the approved base (3x = about INR900 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: HFC contracts, AHF utilisation, and the reason for the margin mix change YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of R32 contracts signed, with more near conclusion; balanced approach kept. Margin mix explained by HF price highs in Q1 FY26 and rising RM costs now; gross margin down about 100 bps QoQ, offset by fixed-cost productivity.

risks_watch: R32 pricing and contracted share: management targets 35-45% of capacity under five-year contracts, with a couple signed and more near conclusion; watch for contract signings and any price disclosure, since pricing was not given.

Gross margin pressure: gross margin fell about 100 bps QoQ on raw material inflation, with price pass-through expected to lag; watch whether the 32-33% EBITDA range (plus/minus 1%) holds as the HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity come on line.

Advanced materials execution: INR90 crore adoption capex is phased, with first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 and commercialisation of about five lab-approved products; no asset turn assumed, so timing and qualification outcomes are key.

CDMO readouts: 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months after one readout did not go well; $100 million FY27 target and 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29 depend on these.
Subsidiary NFASL margin swing: standalone-to-consolidated EBITDA margin gap was about 12 pp QoQ, attributed to campaign mix and arm's-length AHF transfers; watch for downstream capacity at NFASL.
Specialty chemicals (agchem) LatAm pricing pressure persists; management said EBITDA will not return to the old ~30% level, and campaign orders for 4-5 molecules are expected this year.
key_quotes: The revenue of the quarter grew 44% Y -o-Y to INR1,044 crores and EBITDA stood at INR357 crores, up 73% year-on-year and PAT at INR243 crores, registering a growth of 108% year-on-year.
I don't think this is a case of being equal.
Yes, the $100 million is very much on track.
So as we get into more HF you would see that overall, the margin will remain at a group level quite solid.
So, for Navin, the operating leverage on 32 is going to be fantastic.
532504|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, capex pipeline and the 32-33% margin range, but cautious and evasive on R32 pricing, the DRDO order economics, AHF split and CDMO molecule-level details, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Management leaned on "wait and see" framing for Chemours scale-up and on the 15-month window.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Up to 15,000 MT R32 HFC capacity (taking total from about 9,000-10,000 MT to about 25,000 MT) is on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, Chemours liquid cooling completes end Q2 FY27, and Dahej MPP debottlenecking completes by Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY27 revenue up 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore with HPP up 33%, specialty chemicals up 48% and CDMO up 82%; CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million is reiterated as on track and 4-5 agchem campaign orders are planned this year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already announced; phase 1 around mid-Q4 FY27

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.why: A couple of R32 contracts are signed and more are at a late stage, targeting 35-45% contracted share of the expanded capacity over five years, though no pricing was disclosed.

rows.label: Advanced materials as a material business by end of decade

rows.label: CDMO FDA readouts for 3-4 molecules
rows.why: Pipeline of 30-40 molecules with about 10 late stage; 3-4 expected FDA readouts after one readout did not go well, and these underpin the $100 million FY27 CDMO target and 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29.

532504|2026-09.headline: Navin Fluorine Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,191 crores, with EBITDA margin at 34.2%.
532504|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was INR1,191 crores (+57% YoY), operating EBITDA INR407 crores (+66%) at a 34.2% margin, and PAT INR269 crores (+81%). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR2,236 crores (+51%), EBITDA INR765 crores (+69%, margin up 367 bps to 34.2%) and PAT INR513 crores (+93%), with EPS of INR100. Management attributed growth to ref gas pricing, AHF volumes, the Solstice HFO contract, specialty campaigns and CDMO qualifications. The HFO contract with Solstice was extended to December 2032 with about USD180 million of additional revenue potential, though the implied annual run rate is lower than the prior one, which management attributed to pricing mechanics.

financial_highlights.change: +93% YoY vs INR320 crores in H1 FY26

segments.name: HPP (Hydrofluoropolymers / ref gases, AHF, HFO)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew sequentially on better realisations in ref gas and higher AHF volumes after the new AHF plant came into play; HFC realisations improved QoQ. The Solstice HFO contract extension runs to December 2032, with about USD180 million of added revenue potential over four years.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Run rate has been stated at about INR350 crores for the last three quarters. MPP-1 and MPP-2 are expected to far exceed PAR by end FY27; the MPP debottlenecking at Dahej was commissioned in September 2026. Nectar is expected at 60-65% of PAR in FY27, with the balance in FY28.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Management says the USD100 million order-book visibility target is within striking distance and is on time for FY27. The cGMP-4 Phase 2 capex of about INR125 crores is due by end Q4 FY27 and is fully dedicated to Fermion. Phase 1 plus Phase 2 is guided to a peak annual revenue potential of INR900-1,000 crores by FY28-FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to stay in the range of the H1 FY27 level of about 34%; the 30% long-term guidance was not changed.
Capex frame of INR700-1,000 crores a year; FY27 is tracking to the lower end at about INR700 crores.
R32 capacity expected to commission shortly, with incremental growth this quarter and full ramp-up in the next quarter.
Chemours advanced cooling project expected to commission in Q3 FY27; about 15 months after commissioning is needed to gauge adoption and final capex.
Advanced Materials expected to contribute about 10-15% of the expanded revenue pie by 2030, under a 20-25% growth frame.
Advanced material adoption capacity expected to commission by Q2 FY28; HFC capacity expansion on track for commissioning shortly.
capex_capacity: Debottlenecking of MPP capacity at Dahej commissioned in September 2026; growth from it is not yet in the numbers.
HFC capacity expansion progressing as planned; R32 capex on track for commissioning shortly.
Chemours project progressing towards commissioning in Q3 FY27; purchase orders already in hand.
cGMP-4 Phase 2 (about INR125 crores) to be operational by end Q4 FY27; ETP and warehouse infrastructure exist for up to Phase 5/6, so cGMP-5 could follow quickly.
TDF project with DRDO progressing per schedule; renewable energy investments expected to cover more than 60% of energy requirements.
demand_pricing: Ref gas pricing improved on a sequential basis; management says teams placed product above the market average.
HF merchant sales are running well above the earlier plan, with some material going to international markets and high-purity HF.
Cost pressures are visible in sulfur, gas and fluorspar; management says the 34% margin cannot come from pricing alone and relies on efficiency gains and forex tailwinds.
HFO demand is expected to rise with construction and chiller applications; the Solstice contract volumes are based on minimum customer quantities.
Specialty order visibility is strong for H2 FY27 and beyond; five new molecules have campaign orders running to end-FY27 and beyond.
Management said global HFO capacity is about 10% of global ref gas demand in tonnage, so HFO is priced at a premium to ref gases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the QoQ growth across all three segments, and what drives growth from the Q2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: HPP grew on better ref gas pricing and AHF volumes, with QoQ growth also from the Solstice HFO business. Specialty gained from campaign efficiency in MPP plants, and CDMO from Fermion and new qualifications. Future growth comes from Dahej debottlenecking, R32 ramp-up and CDMO scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the Solstice extension imply a lower annual run rate (about USD45 million versus about USD58 million)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is a pass-through pricing mechanism, so a simple average is misleading. It extends the same asset base to an 11-year contract from 7 years, with larger expected volumes; the pricing can change once capex is recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Will HFO commercialisation be delayed by supplying Honeywell beyond 2030?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said there are about 40 HFO varieties, and products outside the conflicting application can be pursued through partnership or product models.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chemours commissioning delay affecting qualification?
qa_highlights.answer: The delay was a deliberate choice to pick the right process route for the initial capacity, not a partner-side issue. Orders are already in place for future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO target beyond USD100 million and what are the timelines for cGMP-5?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 and Phase 2 together have a peak revenue potential of about 3x capex, or INR900-1,000 crores by FY28-FY29. cGMP-5 would be triggered when GMP utilisation reaches 70-80%, and one molecule has approval in China and is on a fast track for FDA approval.

qa_highlights.question: How should capex and surplus cash be allocated?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex frame is INR700-1,000 crores a year, with FY27 at about INR700 crores and the lower end of the range. Working capital is held at 70-75 days, EBITDA conversion is 60-65%, and new capex will be announced after stage-gate approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chemours 10x scale-up trigger and the OEM adoption signal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to size the final capex, which will be clearer after about 15 months of adoption data post-commissioning. Chemours has qualified with a French OEM, 2CRSi, under a joint development agreement, and purchase orders are in hand.

risks_watch: Solstice HFO contract run rate of about USD45 million a year versus about USD58 million previously; the pricing mechanism and post-patent HFO price erosion remain unclear.
Input cost inflation (sulfur, gas, fluorspar, HF) and geopolitical volatility, which management says are not over.
Chemours project commissioning in Q3 FY27 and the roughly 15-month adoption window before final capex is known.
AHF plant utilisation is still ramping and management declined to give a utilisation figure.
Whether the 34% margin holds in FY27 and whether the 30% long-term margin guidance is revisited.
Specialty run rate of INR350 crores versus the Dahej debottlenecking benefit that is not yet in the numbers; R32 full ramp-up expected in the next quarter.
Management declined to discuss the DRDO economics beyond schedule and the dual-use pharma route.
532504|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and execution, with specific timelines for commissioning. Guarded and evasive on forward margins, the HFO pricing post-patent, and AHF utilisation, where management repeatedly said averages are misleading and declined to give numbers.
key_quotes: The way to look at this is that on a same asset base, you're going to extend both the volumes, the revenues and also the period.
I will not sit here and let you believe that I have full knowledge of the future.
So the delay is a conscious choice rather than anything else between the partners.

532505|2026-03.headline: UCO Bank FY26 net profit rose 13.21% to Rs 2,768 crore; gross NPA fell to 2.17%, and FY27 guidance was held at 12-14% credit growth.
532505|2026-03.overview: UCO Bank reported strong FY26 results, with gross advances up 19.44% YoY against 12-15% guidance and deposits up 11.59%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.17% (down 52 bps), net NPA at 0.27%, and PCR at 97.79%. Management held FY27 guidance broadly unchanged despite analyst concern over the West Asia conflict, and said it holds about Rs 1,900 crore of provisioning buffers. Treasury was negative in Q4 due to MTM losses on AFS and HFT books.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 24%+ YoY, with retail up 26%+, agriculture up 26% and MSME up 19%. RAM share of book was 65%, against a 61-63% target.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Housing loans grew about 19% and car loans about 71%. Retail gold loans stood at about Rs 5,400 crore, and the 'others' bucket grew about 40% YoY, mainly on gold loans.

segments.name: Agriculture gold loans
segments.commentary: Agri gold loan book is about Rs 12,200 crore, so total gold loans are about Rs 18,000 crore at an estimated 8.5-9% yield.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore MTM hit on the AFS book. Management cited a Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit against Rs 557 crore, which it said it would clarify offline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 10-12%, credit growth 12-14% (unchanged on deposits, credit range held at 12-14%).
FY27 CASA 37-38%; RAM share raised to 62-65%; CD ratio 80-82%.
FY27 credit cost below 0.75%; global NIM 2.8-2.9%.
FY27 gross NPA below 2%, net NPA below 0.2%, slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recovery and upgradation target Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.
ROA of 0.87% in FY26; management expects 0.95-1% by end of FY27.
FY27 IT budget above Rs 1,000 crore, following Rs 899 crore spend in FY26.
capex_capacity: Network: 3,412 domestic branches plus 2 overseas branches (Hong Kong, Singapore) and 1 representative office in Iran; 110 branches added in FY26; 61% of domestic branches in rural and semi-urban areas.
IT spend rose from Rs 576 crore (FY24) to Rs 642 crore (FY25) and Rs 899 crore (FY26).
Completed: CBDC app on iOS and Android, Murex treasury, Kolkata data centre consolidation, API gateway, ALM TPM automation, MuleHunter integration.

Planned for FY27: omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, RPA, forex and prepaid cards, document management, e-notes, identity access management, Kolkata DR, centralised forex processing, and a CASA back office.
QIP approved by the Board, but management will seek shareholder approval at the AGM first and will not launch it this quarter.
demand_pricing: Corporate pipeline of about Rs 14,000 crore, but disbursement is held back by pricing; management said it will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins.
Demand is coming from renewables, data centres, smart metering and road projects.
AAA-rated exposure is about 33% of the book (unchanged YoY); AA exposure fell to 26% from 29%.
About 65% of the loan book is linked to the repo rate; retail and MSME make up over Rs 1.1 lakh crore of the book.
CD ratio rose to 80.21% from the 75-77% target, which led the bank to push deposit mobilisation, with a focus on retail term deposits, savings and current accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance (credit growth of 12-14%) a sign that the West Asia conflict is weighing on the bank, and is SMA 1 rising stress for MSMEs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance is conservative and has been 12-14% for three years while actual credit growth was 16% in FY24, 17.72% in FY25 and 19.44% in FY26. It attributed the rise in SMA 1 (to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore) to the February 28-day effect rather than stress, and said total SMA 0-2 is 0.45% of standard advances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall to Rs 182 crore from Rs 278 crore QoQ, and what buffers exist against ECL and the Labour Code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop reflects a Rs 260 crore PLI provision in FY25, of which only about Rs 100 crore was paid in FY26, leaving about Rs 160 crore provided. It said it holds an ECL provision of Rs 1,038 crore, a Rs 341 crore contingency provision, and a Rs 530 crore COVID provision, for about Rs 1,900 crore of total buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Given the share price and the Rs 1,900 crore buffer, will the bank raise capital this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to raise capital this quarter. It will seek AGM approval first and then launch the QIP at an opportune time when markets support it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-to-income drop driven by, and what is the outlook for ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fee income growth of 32% QoQ and 25% YoY, and tighter control of controllable costs, with recoveries from written-off accounts at about Rs 1,300 crore in FY26 against Rs 2,400-2,500 crore a year earlier. It expects ROA to reach 0.95-1% by end of FY27, from 0.87% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on MSMEs, and what share is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen a major impact, with MSME slippages flat QoQ and no sharp rise in SMA. About 40% of advances are covered under CGTMSE.

qa_highlights.question: Why was treasury negative and what is the AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore AFS MTM hit as yields rose above 7%. Yields have since eased to 6.95-6.98%, and AFS reserves stood at negative Rs 140 crore at March 2026.

risks_watch: Corporate loan growth could stay subdued while pricing discipline holds back disbursements from the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.
The West Asia conflict may weigh on MSMEs; watch SMA 1 and SMA 2 buckets and MSME slippages in Q1 FY27.
Bond yields and treasury MTM could swing again; FY26 AFS reserves were negative Rs 140 crore.
Employee costs could rise when the Rs 160 crore residual PLI provision is paid, and the Labour Code effect is not yet quantified.
Deposit growth may lag credit growth (11.59% vs 19.44%), which keeps CD ratio pressure on margins; watch whether bulk deposits rise.
Management did not clarify the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure on the call and said it would respond offline.
532505|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on headline delivery, with management repeatedly stressing that FY26 results beat guidance. Defensive on the FY27 guidance and SMA questions, where it attributed changes to the February day-count effect and to the bank's conservative pricing, not to stress.
key_quotes: So, there is no such thing that because of this temporary crisis, we have shifted our guidance downwards.
We do not want credit growth in the Corporate segment at the cost of margins.
February impacts every financial year. SMA 2 is 60 days, but February has 28 days, while January and March have 31 days.
So, all three put together today, we are holding around Rs.1,900 crore of additional provision as a buffer towards our ECL framework.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Fee income rose 32% to Rs 516 crore and cost-to-income fell 581 bps to 52.66%, and ROA is targeted at 0.95-1% from 0.87%; against that, global NIM guidance is 2.8-2.9% and CD ratio is rising to 80.21%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network stands at 3,412 domestic branches after 110 added in FY26, with no further branch additions guided; the FY27 spend is on IT and back-office, not new physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% and deposit growth of 10-12% imply continued expansion from a 19.44% advance growth base in FY26, backed by RAM growth of 24%+ and a Rs 14,000 crore corporate pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex discussion is limited to IT (FY27 budget above Rs 1,000 crore vs Rs 899 crore in FY26) and no utilisation figure or new plant was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit grew 19.44% in FY26 against 12-14% FY27 guidance, and management called the guide conservative, but corporate disbursements are held back by pricing on a Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% sits well below the 19.44% delivered in FY26, and the Rs 160 crore residual PLI payment and unquantified Labour Code effect could pressure employee costs; the risk is more that guidance is conservative than that it is cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management has a dated FY27 plan for omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, forex and prepaid cards, and e-notes, following completed CBDC app and Murex treasury projects.

rows.label: Corporate loan pricing discipline
rows.why: Management will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins, so the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline converts only if pricing clears, which caps credit growth near the 12-14% guide.

rows.label: Asset quality and recovery target
rows.why: Gross NPA is at 2.17% against a sub-2% FY27 target, and the recovery and upgradation target is Rs 2,000-2,500 crore against about Rs 1,300 crore recovered from written-off accounts in FY26.

rows.label: QIP after AGM approval
rows.why: The Board has approved a QIP, but the launch needs AGM approval and waits for market conditions; there is no plan to raise this quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, ROA path and recoveries, but defensive on the FY27 guidance and the SMA 1 rise to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore, and it left the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure to be clarified offline.

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
Was 54.06% last year and 52.66% in March; management expects normalised ~50%

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 27.32% YoY. Home loans grew about 20% and vehicle loans about 65% YoY off a low base; management expects roughly 30% vehicle loan growth and 20-25% home loan growth.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.79% YoY; management expects 19-20% growth to continue. ECLGS sanctions stand at Rs 2,150 crore with Rs 1,700 crore disbursed.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 25.27% YoY and make up 64.5% of the book, within the 62-65% guidance; management aims to hold around 65%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 17%, driven by working-capital limit drawdowns. The bank holds no IBPC exposure and is curtailing low-yield PSU and government lending.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guidance kept at 12-14%, though management says it aims to exceed this; review after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.
NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%, with management aiming to stay slightly above 2.9%; yield on advances expected to hold.
Cost-to-income expected at or around 50% or below for FY27, despite Q1's 37.49%.
ROA of 0.68% annualised in Q1; management sees it near 1% by year-end as the DTA charge is a one-time item.
Credit cost to stay below the 0.75% guidance; deposit repricing largely complete, so cost of funds expected to stay stable.
Expected Credit Loss (ECL): about 60% of the estimated transition requirement already provided as buffer; remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts.
capex_capacity: Around 400 branches in West Bengal under five zonal offices; pan-India network of 3,421 branches.
GIFT City branch to open in the next month; all approvals in place and IT implementation in progress.
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service said to launch 'very soon'.
GST smart product to rise from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore ticket size; pre-qualified personal loan journey to be extended to the call centre.
Digital balance sheet of about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June, up from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 31 STP journeys live; about 70% of fixed deposits now booked digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail loan rates held steady, as they are linked to the repo rate; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026 from 8.75%.
Corporate pricing held steady; management sees demand shifting to loans as bond yields are limited.
Yield on advances was stable, moving only about 3 bps QoQ.
Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management did not quantify the split and sees it as market expansion.
Management reports no stress in any sector; corporate pipelines in infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, steel and cement.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give full-year guidance on cost of funds, cost of deposits, cost-to-income, RAM and corporate advances, ROE and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell to 4.36% as deposit repricing completed; expected to stay stable. NIM 3.05% vs 2.8-2.9% guidance, aim to stay above 2.9%; yield on advances moved about 3 bps. Cost-to-income 37.49% in Q1 but flattered by about Rs 800 crore from few TWO accounts; FY27 target around or below 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank shifting away from IBPC and low-yield government lending, and where is the rebalancing?
qa_highlights.answer: No IBPC exposure now. Growth comes from RAM (above 25%), with retail 27.3%, agri 30%, MSME 19%. Corporate grew about 17%; PSU and government lending being curtailed but is already very limited.

qa_highlights.question: What upside does UCO get from West Bengal's investment climate, given its Kolkata head office?
qa_highlights.answer: About 400 branches in West Bengal across five zonal offices; opportunities seen in steel, railway-related and infrastructure projects. Pan-India network of 3,421 branches.

qa_highlights.question: What would ROA have been under the old tax regime, and what are NIM, ROA and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; the shift to the new regime is statutory. Management said ROA could have been above 1% excluding the Rs 1,237 crore charge, a rough estimate. ROA of 0.68% now, seen near 1% by year-end; NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is competition coming from (PSU, private, NBFC)?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management would not quantify the split and views the market as expanding. Digital balance sheet about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June vs Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 70% of FDs booked digitally.

qa_highlights.question: Should the 12-14% credit growth guidance be raised given 21% actual growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept at 12-14% for now; the bank aims to grow above industry and will review only after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS sanction and disbursement, and is any MSME stress visible?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS sanctions about Rs 2,150 crore, of which Rs 1,700 crore disbursed, under 50% of eligible customers' loans. SMA-1 book (Rs 1 crore and above) fell to Rs 1,009 crore (0.36%) from Rs 1,125 crore (0.43%) in March; slippage 0.63%.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provision is already held versus the requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Assessment done on the 1 April transition date; about 60% of the requirement already provided as buffer over and above mandatory provisions. Remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before ECL starts.

qa_highlights.question: Retail loan pricing trends and corporate pricing; was there JP Associates interest recovery in TWO income?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail rates held as they are repo-linked; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026. Corporate pricing held, with demand shifting to loans as bond yields limited. No interest recovery from JP Associates in interest income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ, why did fee income from loan processing fall, and what drove other commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits rose slightly due to reclassification of deposits and borrowings; overall cost of funds still lower. Advance-related fees fell as renewal charges are now recognised on actual basis; other commission rose on PSLC sale of about Rs 2,000 crore earning Rs 55 crore.

risks_watch: Q1 profit is flattered by about Rs 800 crore of TWO recoveries from a few accounts that management does not expect to recur; cost-to-income of 37.49% will normalise upward.
Credit growth running about 21% against 12-14% guidance; guidance review only after Q2 FY27, so the gap may widen or force a revision.
ECL transition: remaining 40% of the requirement to be provided over 4-5 quarters, a future provisioning drag.
Deposit cost rose QoQ due to reclassification; watch whether cost of funds stays at 4.36% after deposit repricing.
Retail vehicle loan growth of about 65% off a low base; management expects about 30% going forward. Concentration in RAM at 64.5% against a 62-65% band.
Corporate book growth driven by working-capital limit drawdowns; sustainability of demand and yield on the corporate book to watch.
ECLGS and MSME stress: management sees none, but the ECLGS 5.0 disbursement pace and SMA-1 trend need monitoring.
key_quotes: So, our cost of funds has come down to 4.36%.
We will review the guidance after the 2 nd Quarter numbers, because in the midterm, we can review.
As of now, we have not seen any risk from any sector.
So we can't quantify as to how much competition I am getting from the private or from the public sector.

532505|2026-09.headline: UCO Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 26.77% YoY to Rs 786 crore; advances grew 24.70%, well above the 12-14% guidance.
532505|2026-09.overview: UCO Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 786 crore, up 26.77% YoY from Rs 620 crore, with operating profit of Rs 1,872 crore (up 16.04%). Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Gross NPA fell 60 bps YoY to 1.96% and net NPA to 0.18%, both within guidance. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -60 bps YoY; NNPA -25 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 30.23% YoY; housing loan growth above 20% YoY with average home-loan ticket up from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 29.59% YoY; agri slippages rose to Rs 205 crore in Q2 from Rs 73 crore in Q1, but were below Rs 238 crore a year ago.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 20.32% YoY; management sees scope for more growth here.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; sanctioned but undisbursed corporate pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore.

segments.name: RAM portfolio
segments.commentary: RAM portfolio is Rs 1,68,736 crore, up 26.92% YoY, and its share of advances has crossed 65% against the 62-65% guidance.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Hong Kong and Singapore branches are operating; GIFT City IBU opened in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guidance of 12-14% for FY27 was kept; management said it aims to grow above guidance but will not revise it mid-year.
Deposit growth guidance of 10-12% was exceeded (actual 14%+).
GNPA guidance is below 2% by 31 March 2027; already at 1.96%.
Net NPA guidance is below 0.25% for the year; already at 0.18%.
Global NIM guidance of 2.80-2.90% was exceeded (3.00%); management expects to sustain NIM above guidance with repo pass-through.
Credit cost guidance is below 0.75% for FY27; Q2 is 0.65%.
Cost-to-income expected to be around 50% for the full year and possibly below 50% next year.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027 estimated at about Rs 3,200 crore+ requirement; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 3,439 after adding 27 branches in the quarter; business per branch Rs 185 crore vs Rs 161 crore a year ago.
Business per employee Rs 30 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.
GIFT City IBU opened in Q2; three international branches (Hong Kong, Singapore, GIFT City).
Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.
Seven processes automated via RPA; digital marketing solution onboarded; customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches.
Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.
demand_pricing: Advances growth came from all segments; RAM share has crossed 65%, and management expects it to hold around 65% with corporate growth also continuing.
Corporate sanctioned pipeline of about Rs 10,000 crore is undisbursed; disbursement depends on corporates' acceptance of lending rates and capex plans.
About 66% of advances are linked to external benchmark (repo/EBLR); a 25 bps repo hike was passed on immediately to these loans.
Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.
Gold loan yield is about 9% (slightly below) and unchanged QoQ.
Housing loan growth above 20% YoY from both volume and ticket size; second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are small.
Domestic yield on advances 8.11%; global yield 7.79%; cost of funds 4.44%, up slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries from written-off accounts fell to Rs 301 crore from Rs 1,018 crore; is this a normalised rate, and what is the treasury outlook given rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the June quarter included a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery from one large account; excluding it, June recovery was about Rs 233 crore, so Rs 301 crore is the normalised run-rate. On treasury, management said yield hardening pressures profitability, but ~66% of advances are repo/EBLR-linked, so NII gains should offset treasury losses; FVTPL book is small.

qa_highlights.question: Slippages rose from Rs 428 crore to Rs 538 crore and SMA-1 rose from Rs 228 crore to Rs 437 crore; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were Rs 549 crore in the quarter per management; the rise is mainly half-yearly crop-loan agriculture marking in September. SMA-1 and SMA-2 (Rs 1 crore and above) stood at 0.42% vs 0.77% a year ago, with a QoQ uptick described as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates be raised, and with what lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate need to raise deposit rates; current term deposit rates maintained. Any hike would apply only to new deposits and renewals, decided later based on deposit requirement.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in corporate stance, and will the bank raise its credit growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; RAM share crossed 65% (guidance 62-65%) and is expected to hold around 65%. Corporate sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore, dependent on lending rates and capex. Guidance of 12-14% kept; management aims to exceed it but will not revise mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition estimate for 1 April 2027 and has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition requirement estimated at about Rs 2,500 crore in one answer and Rs 3,200 crore-plus in another; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions, including COVID provisions of Rs 530 crore, extra provisions of Rs 341 crore and about Rs 1,600 crore ECL-specific. Estimate not materially changed from three months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan yield and how is it trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan yield is around 9%, slightly below; no change QoQ as no rate changes were made. Any EBLR-linked gold loans will reprice with the repo hike.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating expenses rise by about Rs 160 crore, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is normal, reflecting IT investment, physical infrastructure and network expansion, plus a lag in opex growth in earlier quarters; expected to stay in a similar range, depending on transaction volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income outlook for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 0.65% vs guidance below 0.75%, with ECL provisioning of Rs 570 crore in the quarter and accelerated NPA provisioning to bring NNPA to 0.18%. Cost-to-income was 50.39% (about 45% excluding the June one-off effect); expected around 50% for FY27 and possibly below 50% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Second-hand car loan growth and yield, and housing ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are a small share of car loans; management will work out numbers. Average home-loan ticket rose from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh, with growth from both volume and ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Is NII growth enough to offset treasury stress, and what NIM is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said repo-linked NII growth (about 66% of advances) would more than offset treasury stress, and that FVTPL exposure is small. Global NIM was 3.00% and domestic 3.19%, against guidance of 2.80-2.90%; management expects to sustain NIM above guidance.

risks_watch: Treasury losses from hardening yields; FVTPL book is small but MTM impact depends on the yield path and any further RBI repo action.
Asset quality: quarterly slippage of Rs 549 crore (0.85%), with agri slippage Rs 205 crore and SMA-1/2 up QoQ to Rs 437 crore; watch whether the September agri marking reverses or persists in March.
Recovery from written-off accounts normalising at about Rs 300 crore per quarter, down from the Rs 1,018 crore a year ago, as large accounts are largely resolved.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027: requirement of about Rs 2,500-3,200 crore plus, with Rs 2,500 crore already provided; any further top-up depends on profitability.
Deposit mobilisation: CASA ratio slipped to 36.77% and deposit rates are unchanged, while advances growth of 24.70% far exceeds 10-12% deposit guidance.
Corporate growth conversion: Rs 10,000 crore sanctioned corporate pipeline remains undisbursed and depends on lending rates and capex; watch the RAM-share cap near 65%.
key_quotes: So, this is the normal recovery, and this quarter we don’t have any such big recovery account, which was a one-off in the last quarter.
So, overall, the asset quality has been maintained.
We are ready to take up the growth, whatever the credit growth we can take up in all the sectors.
But, yes, as we move ahead in the year, we will see and we will try to grow more than that, of course.

532508|2026-03.headline: Jindal Stainless Q4FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 37% YoY to INR1,455 crore; FY27 volume guided at 7-9% with EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 only.
532508|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 deliveries were 0.64 million tons, flat YoY, while consolidated EBITDA rose about 37% YoY and 3% QoQ to INR1,455 crore and PAT rose about 41% YoY to INR834 crore. For FY26, volumes grew 8% to 2.57 million tons, EBITDA rose 19% to INR5,560 crore and PAT rose 27% to INR3,185 crore. Net debt fell to INR3,040 crore (0.55x net debt/EBITDA). Management flagged a sharp, sudden rise in gas and utility costs from the Middle East conflict (up around 2.5x-3x), a temporary QCO suspension, and CBAM uncertainty, and gave FY27 volume guidance but EBITDA/ton guidance only until H1.

financial_highlights.change: reduced further; net debt/EBITDA 0.55x, net debt/equity 0.15

financial_highlights.value: INR1 interim + INR3 final per share (face value INR2), ~INR330 crore total

segments.name: Stainless steel (India and Indonesia)
segments.commentary: Consolidated, with EBITDA/ton guidance covering the whole stainless business including Indonesia and Rathi. Domestic share about 92%, export share 8% of FY26 sales.

segments.name: RKEF nickel (Indonesia)
segments.commentary: Management said recent EBITDA has been around $3,000/ton of nickel versus a prior guided range of $500-1,500/ton, but flagged it is volatile and tied to Indonesian ore pricing formulas.

segments.name: Rathi (rebar subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Operated at about 80-85% utilisation in FY26; stainless rebar was about 25% of Q4 volume. Company stated Rathi is EBITDA positive, with no separate figures given.

segments.name: Jindal Stainless Steelway (fabrication subsidiary)
segments.commentary: First fabrication facility in Patalganga started operations, initial investment about INR125 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 7-9% (management also said 'at least 8-10%' early in the call, later clarified as 7-9%).
FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 FY27 only; to be reviewed after six months depending on the situation.
FY27 capex guidance around INR2,600 crore; FY28 capex to be given later.
Sales volume target of 3.5 million tons per annum by FY29, described as double-digit CAGR over three years.
CRAP capacity to reach 2.67 million tons per annum by FY28, including the 0.17 mtpa CRAP line at Jajpur and additional INR900 crore for cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur.
Indonesia melt shop (1.2 mtpa) ramp-up expected to reach 70-80% of capacity during FY27.
capex_capacity: Indonesia 1.2 mtpa stainless melt shop commissioned ahead of schedule; total melting capacity now 4.2 mtpa, of which 3 mtpa in India.
Jajpur 1.1 mtpa HRAP line upcoming commissioning; 0.17 mtpa CRAP line also at Jajpur.
Additional INR900 crore to augment cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur.
Maharashtra greenfield: land acquisition under way, most of this year expected to go into land acquisition; downstream to be built first, then upstream. Clear plan needs a few more months.
Partial commissioning of a 315 MW solar/wind hybrid project with Oyster Renewable Energy in Q4.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand cited as resilient across automotive, ornamental and industrial pipe and tube, railway, metro, lift and elevator, and white goods; metro and passenger coach demand strong, with stainless demand expected to rise 2-3x over 3-4 years.
Export volumes rose QoQ in Q4 despite subdued global trade; focus on Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Germany; Americas remain key.

Management said cost increases were only partly passed on to customers, depending on the product and competitor pricing; imports from competitors without the same cost increases were cited as a constraint.
Gas and utility costs (propane, LPG, natural gas, ammonia, acid) rose about 2.5-3x. Management declined to quantify gas consumption.
QCO suspended for six months; management said this encourages substandard imports and dampens MSME capacity plans. Antidumping verifiers to be appointed in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume and EBITDA/ton guidance be given for FY27 given Middle East headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 volume growth of 7-9% and EBITDA/ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1, with a review after six months; availability of gas is no longer the constraint in May, but cost is much higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export share falling, and what is the FY27 export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports were 8% of sales versus 9% in FY25. Management expects to hold 8-10% of exports in the FY27 volume growth, with disruption from the war and CBAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Maharashtra capex and the FY27/FY28 capex number?
qa_highlights.answer: Land acquisition is under way; FY27 capex guidance is about INR2,600 crore; FY28 figure deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How should RKEF and Indonesia be valued and treated in EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: RKEF EBITDA recently around $3,000/ton of nickel versus the earlier $500-1,500 range. The slabs are planned to be brought to India; Indonesia is a line-by-line consolidated subsidiary with minority share shown separately. Indonesia is included in the INR18,000-20,000 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mitigation plans for gas shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Jajpur has started using natural gas for part of its needs and plans to scale up; coal gasification/syngas and green hydrogen (600 mm cube plant at Jajpur, running June-July) are being pursued; Hisar and Ghaziabad are also being worked on.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 400 series share falling, and does it affect EBITDA/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: 400 series was 18% in FY26 versus 17% in FY25, with Q4 at 19-20%. Management said it is pursuing 400 series growth and only adds volumes that improve EBITDA/ton.

risks_watch: Gas and utility cost inflation from the West Asia conflict; H1 EBITDA/ton guidance may be revised at H1.
QCO suspension for six months and imports of substandard material; antidumping process timeline.
Indonesian nickel and mining policy changes; RKEF EBITDA volatile with nickel prices.
CBAM implementation in the EU; verifiers yet to be appointed.
Ramp-up of Indonesia melt shop and balancing of slab imports against Jajpur HRAP/CRAP timing.
Declining share of 400 series relative to FY25 levels in FY26 mix (headline 17% to 18%, Q4 at 19-20%).

So we are confident of balancing our needs as the market demands.

So, FY27 guidance, volume guidance, we have already provided, which is 7% to 9%, and that takes care of all these uncertainties.

532508|2026-06.headline: Jindal Stainless Q1 FY27: revenue up 10.5% YoY and PAT up 7.7%, but finished-goods volume fell 7.3% on gas shortages; FY27 volume guidance held.

Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 10.5%, 1.4% and 7.7% YoY, with management prioritising value-added mix and thinner grades. Consolidated net debt fell to INR 2,950 crore (net debt/EBITDA 0.53x). Management kept FY27 volume guidance (8-10% growth) and the INR 18,000-20,000/t H1 EBITDA guidance, deferring any revision to the next quarter. Indonesia melt shop (1.2 MTPA) has started ramping up; the Jindal Stainless Indonesia structure changed from subsidiary to associate effective 1 July 2026.

532509|2026-03.headline: Suprajit Q4 FY26: quarterly revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore, Q4 consolidated PBT ~INR 97 crore (almost double YoY); FY27 guide: double-digit growth, consolidated EBITDA margin 12-13.5%.
532509|2026-03.overview: Management reported that Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore on a quarterly run rate, with consolidated PBT of about INR 97 crore, almost double last year. Full-year revenue grew about 17% and EBITDA about 19-20%, helped by the SCS (ex-SES) turnaround, which turned EBITDA positive in Q4 at about +2% after roughly -20% in Q1. Standalone and ex-SCS growth was more modest (standalone revenue +7.1%, ex-SCS consolidated revenue +8.7%). Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth and a 12-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin, with GCM (including SCS) margins rising from about 6% to 10-12%.

Surplus cash in mutual funds, March 2026

segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA margin crossed double digits for the first time at 11% for FY26. Mexico consolidated into Matamoros and Brownsville made main US warehouse; SAL India and Shanghai Lone Star each grew about 20%.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 9%, dampened by YoY price concessions passed to customers; management says EBITDA margin was robust and unchanged for the year. Margin optics were weighed by STC and corporate overheads being allocated to DCD.

qa_highlights.answer: Unrecovered Mexico duties of $1-2 million will be a permanent material cost. The $6 million Section 301 claim is excluded from guidance; resolution expected in 3-6 months.

532514|2026-09.headline: IGL posted negative EBITDA of INR31 crore in Q2 FY27 as spot LNG share rose to 15%, even as average daily gas sales crossed 10 million SCMD.
532514|2026-09.overview: Volumes grew about 8% YoY with CNG and PNG both up, and average daily gas sales hit 10.06 million SCMD, a first for the company. Gross turnover was about INR5,600 crore (up roughly 26% QoQ as stated), but input gas costs rose sharply as term LNG was curtailed under force majeure and spot RLNG filled the gap. The company recorded EBITDA of negative INR31 crore, PBT of INR9.5 crore and PAT of about INR24 crore. Management said pricing is a lever but is being held back to protect CNG volume growth, and capex is being maintained at about INR1,700-1,800 crore for FY27.

FY27 capex is guided at about INR 9,000 crore, mainly the petchem project, and the dividend is to be maintained.

532522|2026-06.headline: Petronet Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 33% to INR 1,133 crore despite company LNG volumes falling to 207 TBTU, aided by trading and inventory gains.

Volumes fell: company LNG processed was 207 TBTU versus 220 TBTU a year earlier, and company utilisation was 58% versus 76%. Management attributed the profit resilience to trading gains of INR 301 crore and inventory gains of INR 193 crore, as Qatar supplies remained under force majeure and tolling cargoes from other sources replaced most of the gap. Dahej's nameplate capacity was raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026, which lowers reported utilisation.

Management said the biosimilars and generics integration was completed in under 100 days and the major capex phase is substantially complete, shifting focus to utilisation, margins and deleveraging. Net debt has fallen to about $1.1 billion from more than $1.5 billion in March 2025, and interest cost savings of about Rs70-75 crore per quarter are now in the P&L.
