532523|2026-06.headline: Biocon Q1 FY27 group revenue up 10% YoY with EBITDA of INR902 crore (21% margin); biosimilars and generics grew while Syngene fell 16%.
532523|2026-06.overview: Group operating revenue rose 10% YoY in Q1 FY27, with biopharmaceuticals up 17% and services down 16%. Group EBITDA was INR902 crore at a 21% margin, and reported net profit before exceptionals was INR145 crore (up 245% YoY) as interest cost fell 23% YoY to INR213 crore. Biosimilars grew 16% to INR2,855 crore, while generics grew 21% to INR760 crore with EBITDA margin recovering to 7%. Management said the second half should be stronger, driven by new launches (Aflibercept in the US, denosumab in Europe) and insulin capacity from the Malaysia second drug product line. Working capital and net debt rose sequentially on inventory build ahead of the H2 ramp.

segments.name: Biosimilars
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,855 crore (+16% YoY), EBITDA INR728 crore (25% margin, +10% YoY); R&D at 7% of revenue. North America drove growth; management guides to meaningful acceleration in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR760 crore (+21% YoY); EBITDA INR56 crore at 7% margin. Improvement attributed to product mix, cost take-out, operating leverage and lower R&D; liraglutide contributed only single-digit share this quarter.

segments.name: Services (Syngene)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR736 crore (-16% YoY) on lower offtake from a key biologics client and a forex hedge loss; EBITDA margin 12%. Guidance: H1 revenue decline, single-digit rupee revenue decline for FY27, margins back to mid-20s.

guidance_outlook: Biosimilars: momentum to build through the year with meaningful acceleration in H2 FY27; management expects biosimilar EBITDA margin in the mid-20s, with a 27% FY26 figure normalised to roughly 24-25%.
Generics: new launches expected to scale in subsequent quarters; operating synergies to be quantified from H2 FY27; margin expansion remains a priority with no specific guidance.
Syngene: FY27 is a transition year, with single-digit rupee revenue degrowth for the full year and EBITDA margins back to mid-20s; return to profitable growth expected from FY28.
Management aims to launch at least one new product in the US or Europe each year through the end of the decade.
Management said it will not increase US manufacturing capex; it will use partnerships and existing US facilities.
capex_capacity: Malaysia insulin facility: EMA approval received for second drug product line; supplies started, with pick-up expected from Q2 FY27.
Working capital build in Q1 is mostly inventory, made to scale up for H2 biosimilars and generics; biosimilar inventory days (DIO) normalised to about 280-290 from over 400 previously.
Depreciation rising as new launch amortisation and newly capitalised facilities come on stream; no specific cost drag quantified for new US and other units.
demand_pricing: Aflibercept (Yesafili) launched in the US in August 2026, with active contracts being tied up; management expects a strong start building into H2.
Five focus growth products: Aflibercept, denosumab (Bosaya/Aukelso), aspart (Kirsty), ustekinumab and bevacizumab; July-September is the payor negotiation window for the next calendar year.
Insulin glargine US market share grew over the last couple of quarters; insulin aspart (Kirsty) moving from closed-door supply to commercial channels in the US.
Management flagged price erosion and competitive pressure as real in biosimilars, offset by integrated cost structure.
Generics: no change in competitive intensity cited; API:formulation mix about 60:40 this quarter versus historical two-thirds:one-third.

qa_highlights.question: What is the generics base business growth ex-liraglutide, and is competitive intensity rising given lower R&D and only a 2% EBITDA gain QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said there is no notable competitive intensity change; liraglutide is still single-digit contribution and not fully reflected. Opex fell sharply across the three companies from Q4 to Q1 and YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Should biosimilar margins rise versus last year's 27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said to normalise FY26's 27% to about 24-25% because of a Q3 North America product mix; management guides to mid-20s with ramp-up, and did not guide beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that Syngene's decline drags on Biocon's profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said Biopharma is about 83% of the business and Services about 17%, so Syngene's temporary decline should not drive group performance; she also noted the structured equity debt element has been retired.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt and working capital rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said the increase is mainly inventory built for H2 scale-up in biosimilars and generics, and that net debt rose on working capital rather than new term loans. Finance cost is down 23% YoY and free cash flow goes first to debt reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of US tariffs and is Biocon expanding US manufacturing capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Matt Erick said the reported tariff remark is not current law, since generics and biosimilars are exempt and legislation would be needed. Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said there will be no new US capex; Biocon will use partnerships and existing US facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What is Biocon's stake in Bicara and any plan to monetise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said Bicara is no longer significant, the holding is small, and monetisation is not being contemplated at present.

risks_watch: Syngene: H1 revenue decline from reduced demand from a key biologics client; watch for H2 recovery to mid-20s margin.
Generics margin sustainability (7% EBITDA) as liraglutide and new launches ramp, and whether R&D prioritisation affects growth.
Biosimilar price erosion and competition in the US (Aflibercept ramp, insulin aspart commercial transition) and the H2 acceleration being delivered.
Net debt and working capital: whether inventory build converts to sales and whether debt reduces as promised.
Policy risk: the US tariff announcement, which management says is not law today but is being monitored.

key_quotes: Q1 performance was broadly in line with our expectations, and we expect momentum to build progressively through the year with meaningful acceleration in the second half of FY'27.

532524|2026-03.headline: PTC India Q4 FY26 standalone volume rose 24% YoY to 23.6 BU, but PAT fell 85% to ₹75.7 crore on the prior-year PEL sale gain.
532524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone trading volume rose 24% YoY to 23.6 billion units, and FY26 volume grew 12% to 92.8 BU. Reported profit fell sharply because Q4 FY25 included the PEL (PTC Energy) sale gain of about ₹521 crore; excluding it, standalone PAT rose 18% to ₹75.74 crore for the quarter and was flat at ₹397 crore for the year. Management said the DISCOM liquidity surplus cut rebate and surcharge income (rebate fell from ₹121 crore to ₹97 crore), so operating income held near ₹450 crore for the year. The board has lifted its pause on the PFS divestment, with the route and advisers still to be decided by a board committee.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 down from ₹17.6; FY26 down from ₹28.88
Around ₹2,400 crore as of call date (approx.)

segments.name: Short-term / exchange trading
segments.commentary: Now about 56% of business by management's account, up from the 50:50 target mix, driving most of the Q4 volume growth. Competes with more than 70 licensed traders.

segments.name: Cross-border and long-term trading
segments.commentary: Management describes a niche edge here with only about 4-6 credible competitors. Cross-border is one of three cited moats alongside balance sheet and relationships.

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: 68 lakh certificates delivered in FY26 to cover balance renewable obligations. The company also trades power for Himachal Pradesh from 14 hydro projects.

segments.name: Consultancy and new initiatives
segments.commentary: Includes PM KUSUM smart meter and rooftop solar work, an ADB project for Laos, Thailand and Cambodia, and BESS power trading. Green power supply to GAIL Vijaipur green hydrogen (10 MW) is also in place.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth expected to track or slightly exceed national power demand growth of about 5% a year.
Trading margins guided flat, with movement of only plus or minus a few basis points; growth to come from volume rather than margin.
Medium- and short-term contracts expected to take a larger share; long-term contracts may shrink to 10-12 years from 25.
PFS divestment process restarted after the board lifted its pause; a board committee will decide the structure over the next few months, with material developments to be disclosed.
NLC India JV: about 2,000 MW initial hydro/renewable portfolio, subject to DIPAM-level government approval.
Teesta Urja: cofferdam phase to supply about 40-50% of capacity by September or October 2026; full dam completion targeted for 2029.
capex_capacity: Net cash about ₹2,800 crore at 31 March 2026, around ₹2,400 crore on the call date, per management.
Cash is held for working capital needs (the business is cyclical), a strategic 'war chest' for small, value-adding investments, and returns to shareholders.
NLC India JV: MoU for about 2,000 MW initially; may go higher or lower depending on government permissions.
Teesta Urja hydro: cofferdam phase first, full dam later.
PFS divestment proceeds would be reinvested in trading-adjacent opportunities; management said no fixed return benchmark will be applied.
demand_pricing: Management reported record peak demand of about 260 GW the previous day; electricity demand is growing about 5% a year.
Renewables reached about 26% of energy consumed, against a 29% government target for the year.
Competition is intense on exchange and short-term trades, with over 70 licensed traders. Margins are under pressure; management says trading margin growth is difficult.
Customer base is more than 800 consumers. Data centres and green hydrogen are emerging demand segments.
Rebate and surcharge income fell as DISCOM payments became timely, reducing income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT contribution from the PEL sale and how will it affect future earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: The PEL sale produced a PBT gain of about ₹521 crore in the prior year, and PAT from PEL was about ₹33 crore in FY25. FY26 numbers have no PEL profit and are a good base for trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth do you expect over the next 2-3 years, and is PFS divestment still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is expected at about 5%, slightly above national growth. The board's pause on PFS divestment has been lifted, and a board committee will decide the structure over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition, and does it pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is strong on exchange trades (over 70 traders) and limited in long-term and cross-border trades (about 4-6 players). Growth will come from volume, not margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance be deployed, and what is the return hurdle?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is kept for cyclical working capital, strategic investments that add value to the core business, and returns to shareholders. Management said it would not hold the company to a fixed ROCE or IRR benchmark that delays value realisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline across long-, medium- and short-term contracts, and how are spreads moving?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term contracts are harder to win, with more focus on medium- and short-term deals. Spreads are not expected to rise much or fall much, with margin changes of plus or minus a few basis points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NLC JV plans, capex and timing, and what is net cash and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: NLC JV targets about 2,000 MW initially, awaiting DIPAM approval, with no timeline. Net cash is about ₹2,800 crore at March-end and about ₹2,400 crore now. Management said distressed assets were largely resolved and remaining ones are expected to be resolved in the near term.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from competition, with management saying margins will stay roughly flat in the next 2-3 years.
Reliance on short-term exchange trades, which raises volume volatility and reduces contract visibility.
Lower rebate and surcharge income as DISCOM payments improve; this has already cut income.
PFS divestment timing, route and value, with no investment banker yet announced.
Capital allocation of a large cash balance (about ₹2,400-2,800 crore) without a stated return target.
Asset quality of the remaining financing book, which management would not detail.
NLC JV and Teesta Urja timelines depend on government approvals and construction schedules.

532524|2026-06.headline: PTC India Q1 FY27 standalone PBT fell 32% to Rs 96 crore on 12% higher trading volume of 25.78 BU, as lower surcharge and rebate income offset gains.
532524|2026-06.overview: Trading volume rose 12% to 25.78 billion units at a stated margin of 3.35 paise per unit, and total operating income rose 2% to Rs 113 crore. Standalone PBT fell 32% to Rs 96 crore and PAT fell 33% to Rs 71 crore, which management attributed to lower net surcharge and rebate income as Discoms' liquidity improved. Consolidated PBT fell 48% to Rs 151 crore, also reflecting a Rs 82 crore impairment reversal in the year-ago quarter. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 23 per share, which it described as one-time, linked to the PTC Energy (PEL) asset sale to ONGC.

segments.name: Power trading
segments.commentary: Volume up 12% to 25.78 BU, with 60% from exchange-traded products and the rest bilateral short, medium and long-term. Management said the volume growth came mainly from exchange trade.

segments.name: Consultancy / C&I services
segments.commentary: Management said the business is steadily growing and is a stable piece, but declined to give projections. No figures were disclosed.

segments.name: Power exchange associates
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 total income Rs 13.98 crore and PAT about Rs 5.16 crore, as disclosed in response to a question.

segments.name: PTC Financial Services (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management described performance as less than spectacular. Its PBT decline also drove part of the consolidated fall, and the company is now looking to divest it, with SBI Capital engaged as transaction advisor.

guidance_outlook: Management expects power demand to grow 4%-6% annually, with short-term volatility from weather.

Long-term capacity additions: management said no new long-term contracts are expected in FY27 or FY28 because of regulatory constraints. Growth will come from battery storage and time-of-day/seasonal trades.
NTPC Green 1,200 MW long-term solar PPA is expected to come online around FY29.
Teesta Urja (1.2 GW) is under construction; a cofferdam-stage power start is expected around December 2026, with about 40%-50% generation initially.
Interim dividend of Rs 23 per share is a one-time measure and should not be expected annually.
PFS disinvestment: management expects to say more to the market closer to the end of FY27; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Long-term PPA of 1,200 MW signed with NTPC Green for solar power procurement, expected online around FY29.
Teesta Urja 1.2 GW hydro project under construction after the cloudburst-related washout, with staged commissioning.
NLC India JV: DPE approval received; Board has approved investment of up to Rs 500 crore, to be deployed over time.
Battery storage: management said it is in discussions and evaluating whether to own storage assets or contract for storage services, with no tie-up announced.
demand_pricing: Standalone PBT decline was driven by lower net surcharge and rebate income, which management attributed to improved Discom liquidity and Discoms paying on time to capture rebates.
Long-term volume decline YoY was attributed to lower hydro generation under long-term agreements.
Management said pricing is competitive and that some contracts are taken as marketing calls. Trading margins are expected to depend on portfolio mix, with exchange markets providing lower margins.

Management said trading on spot and exchange markets is only about 8,000-9,000 MW against peak demand of about 260,000 MW, and that policy changes such as merchant capacity mandates could deepen the market.
Contracts for difference (SECI pilot) and the futures market were cited as policy developments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the long-term PPA book expires in the next one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing is likely to expire in the next three years. It did not give the average remaining tenor and promised data by email.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term capacity decline YoY, and will it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline was due to lower hydro generation under long-term agreements. Management said no new long-term contracts are expected in FY27 or FY28 due to regulatory constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rebate income decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Discoms are now paying early and capturing rebates themselves, while PTC pays generators early and then recovers from Discoms later, so PTC's net rebate income fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a Rs 17.4 crore provision booked (Note 8)?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a generator's claim from a legal dispute over a contract. The adjudicating authority ruled that PTC pay first and recover later. The provision was made on auditor consultation, with no clear visibility on recovery from the counterparty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash position and who are the top debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone net cash was Rs 2,451 crore at 30 June, before the interim dividend. Top debtors: Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore), Haryana (about Rs 500 crore), Rajasthan (about Rs 400 crore), and Tamil Nadu (about Rs 300 crore). Management said PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, as back-to-back pass-through items inflate gross debtors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for PFS and how much stake will PTC keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a transaction advisor (SBI Capital) is appointed and the process is under way. No stake or timeline was committed, and the structure depends on advisor input.

qa_highlights.question: Will CERC's HPX rule affect PTC?
qa_highlights.answer: The CERC rule caps shareholding at 5% for trading members. PTC holds more than 22% of HPX, so it cannot be a trading member unless it reduces its stake below 5%, which management said depends on several factors.

risks_watch: Lower net surcharge and rebate income: management attributes it to improved Discom liquidity and early Discom payments, and called the cyclicality uncertain; no split of surcharge between long-term and short-term sources was given, with data promised by email.

Receivables: gross debtors of Rs 4,469 crore at 30 June, with Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore) and Haryana (about Rs 500 crore) as the largest; management says PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, but back-to-back items inflate the figure.
Rs 17.4 crore provision (Note 8) for a generator's legal claim; recovery from the counterparty is not assured and may lead to further litigation.
Long-term book and volumes: long-term volume fell YoY on lower hydro generation; no new long-term contracts expected in FY27 or FY28; average remaining PPA tenor not disclosed.
Timing risk on new capacity: Teesta Urja (1.2 GW) first power around December 2026 at 40%-50% initially; NTPC Green 1,200 MW PPA around FY29; battery storage still in discussion with no tie-up.

PFS disinvestment: transaction advisor (SBI Capital) appointed; no stake, structure or timeline committed beyond 'closer to end of FY27'. HPX: PTC holds more than 22% and cannot be a trading member unless it cuts below 5%.

Nothing is likely to expire in next three years.
But as far as the PTC exposure is concerned, so that is not more than, I will say not more than 60 days wherein PTC has taken an exposure and that is pending.
So, we are not expecting to add any long-term contracts in that duration.

532524|2026-09.headline: PTC India Q2 FY27 standalone PAT fell 15% to Rs 113 crore on 24% higher volume, as net surcharge income dropped from Rs 42 crore to Rs 26 crore.
532524|2026-09.overview: Trading volume rose 24% YoY to 32.5 billion units in Q2 and 18% to 58.2 billion units in H1, led by exchange and medium-term trades. Operating income was flat-to-down (Rs 134 crore vs Rs 137 crore), while PBT fell 15% to Rs 152 crore as net surcharge and treasury income declined after a special dividend reduced cash balances. Consolidated PAT fell 28% to Rs 159 crore, with a Rs 51 crore impairment provision at PTC Financial Services (PFS) a major drag. Management said PFS stake sale is in process with a transaction advisor appointed, but gave no timeline.

segments.name: Power trading (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume 32.5 bn units (+24%); H1 58.2 bn units (+18%), with 60% of H1 volume on exchanges. Q2 trading margins: short-term 0.69 paise/unit, medium-term 3.17, cross-border 6.98, long-term 7.98.

segments.name: Cross-border trade
segments.commentary: Flows to Bangladesh stable with regular payments; Bhutan 1,200 MW winter supply contract signed; Nepal import/export commenced. Lower cross-border income reduced operating income in Q2 as margin is higher than exchange trades.

segments.name: HPX (Hindustan Power Exchange, 22.5% stake)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 18.13 crore vs Rs 9.89 crore YoY; H1 revenue Rs 32.11 crore vs Rs 22.18 crore.

segments.name: PTC Financial Services (PFS)
segments.commentary: Q2 impairment provision of Rs 51 crore vs a Rs 57 crore reversal in Q2 FY26; management cited a roughly Rs 40 crore reduction in PFS PAT, which flowed into consolidated numbers.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given for Q3 or full year; management said there is no dramatic change in the current situation.

PFS stake sale: transaction advisor appointed, information dossiers being prepared, nodal officers appointed in PFS; no deadline or dates announced, citing regulatory approvals (RBI, SEBI if required).
Management expects power prices to stay firm in peak hours; intraday price range cited from under Rs 1 to Rs 10 per unit; storage additions expected over the next 12-18 months.
Minerals exchange: planned launch with initial focus on five minerals including iron ore; investment described as modest and funded from cash; partnerships under evaluation.
Dividend: company practice is to declare dividends once a year; no interim dividend expected soon.
Joint venture with NLC: board has met and a business plan is being formulated; near-term (1-2 years) business activity expected to be limited due to connectivity lead times of 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Solar PPA of 1,200 MW signed with NTPC Renewable Energy in the last quarter.
Floated a 500 MW / 2,000 MWh tender for long-term renewable-linked power procurement.
Bhutan winter supply contract of 1,200 MW signed.
Contracted supply to NG delayed by NG itself; safeguards in contract mean no commercial impact, but power has not yet been delivered.
Minerals exchange and NLC JV are early-stage; no capacity or capex figures disclosed.
demand_pricing: Total generation grew 10.64% in H1 while PTC trading volume grew over 18%, which management cited as evidence of market share gains.
Net surcharge income fell from Rs 42 crore to about Rs 26 crore YoY, as DISCOMs paid on time and PTC reduced outstanding dues from a large state utility.
Treasury income fell after a special dividend paid out of the PEL divestment proceeds reduced cash.
Rebate income is netted within sale and purchase account, not shown separately in P&L; management said it depends on DISCOM liquidity.
Gas-based power costs have risen sharply due to Middle East conflict, affecting trading partners' behaviour and RE project timelines.
Market coupling remains pending regulatory directives; HPX competitiveness depends on it.
Minerals trading competitors cited as MSTC and Mjunction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timeline of the PFS stake sale, and is there a deadline?
qa_highlights.answer: Process is on track with a transaction advisor appointed; no deadline or specific dates given because of regulatory approvals and the aim to realise good value after operational stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PAT fall despite higher operating income, and which expense items rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Net surcharge fell from Rs 42 crore to about Rs 26 crore and treasury income fell after the special dividend; establishment costs rose about Rs 2 crore on a base of about Rs 10 crore due to staff transfer from PEL.

qa_highlights.question: What are the trading margins by category?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 margins: short-term 0.69 paise/unit, medium-term 3.17, cross-border 6.98, long-term 7.98; overall about 2.89 paise/unit.

qa_highlights.question: How is rebate income generated and where is it reported?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebate is earned when a DISCOM does not avail rebate while PTC pays generators early; it is netted within sale and purchase account, not a separate P&L line.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost double QoQ despite large cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Includes working capital interest (about Rs 14 crore in H1, Rs 7 crore in Q2) and surcharge expenses paid back-to-back against surcharge income booked in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PTC entering mineral trading and what are the regulatory and competitive issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Synergy with existing 500-600 C&I clients and mining customers; regulator is Indian Bureau of Mines; competitors are MSTC and Mjunction; partnerships being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Can HPX trade given the 5% exchange-trader cap while PTC holds 22.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC does not trade on HPX; trading would require cutting its stake from 22.5% to 5%, a decision still under evaluation.

risks_watch: PFS stake sale: no timeline, and shareholder concerns about the process being delayed or halted; PFS stock trades near 50% of book value per a shareholder question.
Consolidated earnings are exposed to PFS provisions (Rs 51 crore impairment in Q2).
Lower surcharge and treasury income and reliance on rebate income, which depends on DISCOM liquidity.
Recoverability of a previously written-off amount depends on judicial process with no timeline.
Market coupling regulatory directives still awaited; HPX volume outlook depends on it.
Minerals exchange and NLC JV: execution timing uncertain, with connectivity lead times of 3-4 years.
532524|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on volume growth and cash strength but defensive on PFS divestment, repeatedly declining to give dates or timelines and rejecting shareholder suspicions. Profit decline was attributed to PFS provisions and lower surcharge and treasury income, which management framed as improved receivables management.
key_quotes: Our risk management is far more composed and should that lead to some reduction in the rebate income, still it is much more sustainable than anything else.
The revenue and the trading margin is only a by-product of that, but for some quarters it may go down, for some quarters it may go up.
To divest like a slump sale is not a wise thing. It will not be good for the PTC shareholders also.
There is absolutely no intent on the part of the management to stop in between or create this smoke screen.

532525|2026-03.headline: Bank of Maharashtra FY26: net profit INR7,019 crore (+27% YoY), full-year NIM 3.91%, ROA 1.86%, all guidance met; FY27 ROA guidance 1.80%.
532525|2026-03.overview: Management reported that all FY26 guidance metrics were met, several with headroom, with total business up 17% and advances up 22% YoY. Gross NPA fell 29 bps to 1.45% and net NPA to 0.13%, while operating profit rose 16% to INR10,826 crore. Management created an INR200 crore "global geopolitical uncertainties" provision in Q4 as a buffer against the West Asia crisis, and said stress is not yet visible in MSME. Non-interest income was weak (2.51% growth) due to a one-time INR290 crore MTM hit from the RRB amalgamation. FY27 guidance was issued across 18-19 parameters, with ROA lifted to 1.80%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew 32% YoY; home loans +29%, vehicle loans +56%, gold loans +53% to INR24,000 crore, of which about INR5,000 crore is co-lent with NBFCs. Retail slippages in Q4 were about INR100 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew 22% YoY, with RAM split 63:37 (retail/agri/MSME vs corporate). Corporate reported no slippages in Q4; INR72,000 crore sanctioned in FY26 with INR34,500 crore undisbursed.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 11% YoY (about INR6,000 crore added per management); MSME NPA fell to 1.54%. Q4 MSME slippages were about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri grew 13% YoY; agri NPA was 7.72% (about INR3,100 crore). Q4 agri slippages were about INR300 crore.

segments.name: GIFT City IBU
segments.commentary: Overseas advances rose to INR6,142 crore from INR3,517 crore (2% of book). Management said the IBU turned profitable in March after covering all overheads; 650 million USD booked against a 1 billion USD 12-month aspiration.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: AFS reserve swung from +INR175 crore in Q3 to -INR362 crore at 31 March; FVTPL MTM gain of about INR40-45 crore booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total business growth 16-17%; advances 18%; deposits 14-15%; CASA around 50%.
RAM growth 18% with RAM corporate mix at 60:40 (+/-2%); non-interest income growth 10%; NII growth 15%.
FY27 NIM guidance 3.75%; cost to income below 40%; ROA 1.80%; ROE 20% or more.
GNPA within 2%, NNPA within 0.25%, slippage below 1%, credit cost around 1%, PCR around 98%, CRAR maintained at 18%.
Management expects FY27 tax at about 10% of PBT (OP tax rate 13-14%), with PBT-basis tax about 18-20%, after unabsorbed losses of about INR1,200-1,300 crore were used up in Q1.
Debt waiver: about INR2,000 crore expected (INR917 crore overdue + INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts), with approval expected Q2 to Q3 FY27; agri NPA could fall to about 5.33%.
capex_capacity: Project 321: 321 new branches in the first 3-year phase, 183 functional to date; Board has approved 1,000 branches over 5 years.
GIFT City IBU: first business booked September 2025; retail products planned for H2 FY27.
PLI for Scale 4 and above not yet released; 100% provision made, release pending discussions.
demand_pricing: Management expects West Asia crisis impact to show from Q2 FY27 rather than Q1, with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk; no MSME stress seen as of March.
Q4 SMA-1 was INR241 crore and SMA-2 INR56 crore as of 31 March (per analyst).
Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises, but gave no specific pricing action.
Pool/assignment book of about INR14,000 crore is largely lent to AA/AAA NBFCs; security cover is low as it is pool-based.
Gold co-lending slowed after RBI's CLM1 guidelines from 1 January 2026; fresh underwriting resumed in early March, with 9 NBFC co-lending partners signed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the West Asia war affect corporate and MSME accounts from April onward, and what stress is visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no stress was visible in March and MSME NPA fell to 1.54%, but impact is expected from Q2 FY27 and depends on how long the crisis lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the special provision fall to INR1,010 crore from INR1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the COVID buffer was released, and a new INR200 crore global geopolitical uncertainties provision was built in Q4, with no regulatory prescription behind it.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time non-interest income drag?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR290 crore MTM provision was taken on investments in the RRB (Vidharbha Konkan Gramin Bank) that was amalgamated into a single Maharashtra RRB, with the bank as sponsor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net worth fall QoQ and gold loans drop about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth fell due to AFS reserve movement and dividends (interim 10% plus final 12%, about INR1,692 crore total). Gold loans dropped because fresh underwriting paused during the shift from CLM2 to CLM1 co-lending; underwriting resumed in early March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is on the normal tax rate from Q2 FY26, with OP tax at 13-14%. FY27 PBT-basis tax is expected around 18-20%, and the call gave a 10% figure for the tax on PBT in the same answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split of Q4 slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail about INR100 crore, agri about INR300 crore, MSME about INR400 crore, and corporate nil.

risks_watch: West Asia / crude-driven stress in MSME and corporate books from Q2 FY27; a 1.2% to 2% geopolitical provision top-up is open.
Timing and size of the state KCC debt waiver (about INR2,000 crore); the scheme is not yet approved.
Tax-rate normalisation to about 25% creates an earnings headwind; management guided FY27 PBT-basis tax at 18-20%, but the figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Non-interest income growth (2.51% in FY26) versus 10% target; a fee-income push is planned for FY27.
Gold co-lending volume recovery after CLM1 transition; the book fell about 17% QoQ.
Pending PLI payout for Scale 4 and above, and the NCLT recovery pipeline (about INR7,500 crore in NCLT).
532525|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance, with management calling the targets "sacrosanct". Cautious and somewhat evasive on the West Asia impact, saying the full effect cannot yet be gauged and that the crisis is not over.
key_quotes: we have been able to meet all the guidance and at some of the places with a decent margin above the guidance that was shared in the beginning of the year.
These are sacrosanct numbers for us. We will be achieving itself.
So we can only hope that the crisis resolves and what damage must have happened, the impact, how fast it can be replaced is also needs to be seen.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 NIM was 3.91% against FY27 NIM guidance of 3.75%, so management is guiding a ~16 bps compression, and credit cost is guided around 1% against a much lower FY26 run-rate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: over 5 years, with 183 of 321 Project 321 branches already f
rows.why: Board approved 1,000 branches over 5 years and 321 in the first 3-year phase, with 183 functional to date (57%), so branch rollout continues through the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance is advances +18%, deposits +14-15%, total business +16-17%, against FY26 advances +22% and total business +17%, backed by 9 NBFC co-lending partners and gold co-lending restarting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; utilisation is not disclosed for a bank, and branch expansion is already approved under Project 321.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 delivered ROA 1.86% against 1.75% guidance and NIM 3.91% against 3.75%, but FY27 guidance was set at roughly the same bar, with ROA raised only 5 bps to 1.80%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects the West Asia crisis to hit from Q2 FY27 with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk, a geopolitical provision top-up of 1.2-2% is open, and tax normalises to about 18-20% on PBT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: GIFT City IBU plans retail products for H2 FY27 after turning profitable in March with USD650 million booked against a USD1 billion 12-month aspiration.

rows.label: Risk-based repricing if stress rises
rows.why: Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises but gave no specific action, with Q4 slippages of about INR800 crore across retail, agri and MSME (corporate nil).

rows.label: State KCC debt waiver of about INR2,000 crore
rows.why: The waiver covers INR917 crore overdue plus INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts, with approval expected Q2-Q3 FY27, and agri NPA could fall to about 5.33% from 7.72%.

rows.label: PLI payout for Scale 4 and above
rows.why: 100% provision is already made, but release is pending discussions, so any release would be an upside to other income with no date given.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance (targets called sacrosanct) but cautious and somewhat evasive on West Asia impact, which it said cannot yet be gauged; analysts pressed on tax-rate inconsistency, the 10% vs 18-20% PBT tax figures, and the gold book's 17% QoQ drop.

532525|2026-06.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q1 FY27: net profit up 27% YoY to INR2,020 crore, advances up 27%, NIM 3.85%, all guidance parameters beaten.
532525|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) with total business up 19% YoY, advances up 27% and deposits up 13%, against guidance of 16-17%, 18% and 14% respectively. Operating profit rose 21% YoY to INR3,117 crore and net profit rose 27% to INR2,020 crore. Asset quality held: gross NPA flat QoQ at 1.45%, net NPA 0.13%, credit cost 0.99%. Management kept its FY27 guidance unchanged despite the faster growth, and flagged the NIM (3.85%, down 10 bps YoY) and the rising cost of deposits QoQ as the points to watch.

financial_highlights.value: INR1,04,000 crore added in past year

financial_highlights.change: Guidance 14%; no CDs raised in Q1
vs INR33 crore in March quarter; includes one-time SR of INR104 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY; retail gross NPA 0.34% per management, with home loan sanctions in the past 12 months 80% from CIBIL 750+ borrowers.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 30% YoY; agri gross NPA 7.58%, down from about 9% a couple of quarters back.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 23% YoY; MSME gross NPA 1.60%, and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 30% YoY, up from 17-18% in the prior four quarters; RAM:corporate mix at 63:37.

segments.name: IBU (GIFT City)
segments.commentary: IBU book about INR8,200 crore, contributing about 3 points of the 27% advances growth; sanctions of $965 million; global yield 8.57% vs domestic 8.66%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth guidance kept at 18%, despite Q1 growth of 27%; management said it would not revisit the number.
NIM guidance of 3.75% maintained; management said no further rate cuts are now expected and a rate hike may come.
Cost-to-income guided below 40%; Q1 running at about 36-38%.
Credit cost guided below 1%; Q1 at 0.99%.
Gross NPA guided below 2% and net NPA below 0.25%; Q1 at 1.45% and 0.13%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore planned this FY, with Board, shareholder and RBI approvals in place; awaiting government approval.
Tax rate guided at 12-13% on operating-profit basis and 16-17% on PBT basis.
Debt waiver scheme (under formulation): eligible portfolio about INR3,500 crore; expected to be settled within FY27; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions.
ECL: about INR125 crore per quarter of provisioning needed through March 2031, to be charged against net worth per RBI's final guidelines rather than P&L.
capex_capacity: Opening about 200 new branches a year under a 5-year expansion plan; new branches are staffed from day one.
Staff strength about INR17,500 crore (figure as stated) vs about INR13,000 crore two years ago; recruitment to continue.
Mobile banking app active registered users up from 2.75 lakh (old version) to over 14 lakh.
Around 40% of branches are in rural areas.
LCR average 118% vs terminal LCR 114%; management targets a 115-120% band.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 13% with no CDs raised in Q1; PSB average deposit growth 11% and private banks 14%, per management.
Domestic CD ratio 86%; 81.99% after including about INR19,000 crore of refinance (blended cost 6-6.5%).
Repo-linked share of loan book 53%, MCLR-linked 44%; MCLR was raised in the last two ALCO reviews and will reset gradually over the next year.
5-year FCNR deposit offered at 6.60%, positioned against the best PSB offers.
ECLGS: eligible portfolio INR6,700 crore, sanctions INR4,500 crore (65%), disbursed INR3,560 crore (82% of sanctions); MSME INR2,700 crore, corporate INR400 crore.
Retail term deposit growth 16% vs total deposits 13%; management attributes the QoQ rise in deposit cost to special retail TD schemes.
Gold loans about INR13,000 crore, up 75% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII (14.5%) lag advances growth (27%), and would management revisit the 18% loan growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept NII guidance of 15% and NIM of 3.75%, citing a branch-level profitability dashboard and tighter pricing. It said it would keep the 18% advances guidance, with IBU contributing 3 points of the 27% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did current account balances fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it not a major concern: the decline is about 2,500-3,000 bps of the current account book, and CASA still grew 9% YoY, adding INR14,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Agri provisions and debt waiver impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligible portfolio INR3,500 crore; government receivable INR2,750 crore; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions. Settlement expected within FY27, plus INR50,000 per farmer incentive into SB accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate is about 12-13% on an operating-profit basis and 16-17% on a PBT basis, aided by rural advances (about 40% of branches rural), bad-debt write-off benefits and DTA.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of 8-9% vs balance sheet growth above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost growth is driven by staffing new branches from day one; cost-to-income is 36-38% and guided below 40%. Branches opened three or more years ago have all turned profitable, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did treasury profit jump to INR266 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury included a one-time SR of INR104 crore, with part of the payment possibly coming in later quarters; no treasury profit targets are set.

qa_highlights.question: SMA-2 jump from INR56 crore to INR208 crore; is MSME stress rising?
qa_highlights.answer: A single government entity account of INR87 crore moved into SMA-2 and is expected to regularise. SMA-1+2 stands at 1.34%, down 5 bps YoY.

risks_watch: Cost of deposits rose 5 bps QoQ to 4.38% and retail term deposits are growing faster than total deposits; watch the QoQ trend.
Thin CASA growth in Q1 (current account balances fell sharply QoQ) and reliance on refinance (about INR19,000 crore) and possible CDs as deposit growth lags loan growth.
Agri gross NPA at 7.58% and the debt-waiver haircut timing; the Rs 87 crore government account in SMA-2 needs to regularise.
Agri and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ (MSME 1.60%); watch for stress from geopolitical conditions (West Asia).
NIM pressure from MCLR resets, with the yield on advances down 71 bps YoY to 8.57% globally; the rate-hike benefit depends on repo-linked share at 53%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore pending government approval; treasury gains include a one-time item of INR104 crore.
ECL provisioning of about INR125 crore per quarter through March 2031 against net worth.
532525|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on keeping guidance unchanged. Management was evasive on the NII-versus-loan-growth gap and the cost-of-deposit trajectory, answering both with qualitative points rather than numbers.
key_quotes: We are committed to the guidance numbers that we have shared.
Gross NPA is maintained at the March level 1.45% against our guidance of maintaining it below 2%.
So refinance, again, why we decided not to go for high-cost bulk deposits, the blended cost that we have experienced while we go for refinance is in the range of 6% to 6.5%.
The mantra is very clear. It has to be a profitable growth and no compromise on the quality.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 27% YoY (INR65,000 crore added) against FY27 guidance of 18%, and deposits grew 13% vs 14% guidance; IBU contributes about 3 points of growth and gold loans are up 75% YoY to about INR13,000 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex utilisation figure disclosed; the INR5,000 crore equity raise (Board, shareholder and RBI approvals in place, awaiting government nod) funds growth but is not a capex plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept the 18% advances guidance despite Q1 growth of 27% and said it will not revisit the number; NII guidance kept at 15% after NII grew only 14.5%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Deposit growth (13%) trails loan growth (27%), with no CDs raised in Q1 and CASA balances down QoQ, and agri gross NPA at 7.58% plus a debt-waiver haircut of INR450-500 crore (already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions) add risk to the guided ratios.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch discussed; only a 5-year FCNR deposit at 6.60% was mentioned as an existing offer.

rows.label: Equity raise of INR5,000 crore this FY
rows.why: Board, shareholder and RBI approvals are in place and only government approval is pending, against advances growing 27% and CRAR at 18.64%.

rows.label: Debt waiver scheme settlement
rows.why: Eligible portfolio about INR3,500 crore with maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions, so the P&L hit is largely absorbed.

rows.label: ECL provisioning charged to net worth
rows.why: About INR125 crore per quarter of provisioning is charged against net worth per RBI's final guidelines rather than the P&L.

tone.note: Management was confident on loan growth, asset quality and keeping guidance unchanged, but evasive on the NII-versus-loan-growth gap and the cost-of-deposit trajectory; analysts pressed on those points.

532525|2026-09.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27: business up 25% YoY, advances up 30%, ROE 26.98%, GNPA down 47 bps to 1.25%.
532525|2026-09.overview: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics were met in Q2, with business crossing INR7 lakh crore and advances growing 30% YoY (23% ex-IBU). Operating profit rose 31% and net profit 41% YoY, lifting ROE 440 bps to 26.98% and NIM 12 bps to 3.97%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.25% and NNPA at 0.12%, helped by write-off recoveries and lower NPA provisions, while INR500 crore of ECL provisions was booked in the standard asset line. Cost of deposits fell 4 bps YoY to 4.38%, though management acknowledged a QoQ rise tied to FCNR(B) and OFCB raises of about $1.65 billion.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of deposits / cost of funds

segments.name: Advances / large credit
segments.commentary: Large credit up 38% YoY to INR36,000 crore, of which INR18,000 crore from GIFT City IBU and INR18,000 crore domestic (19% growth). Domestic credit ex-IBU grew 23%, with RAM, retail, agri and MSME each above 20%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 22% YoY, or 19% ex-FCNR(B); CASA up 12% YoY with INR19,000 crore CASA added over the last FY.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book INR44,000 crore, up 34% YoY (about INR11,000 crore). Agri gold loans INR18,600 crore vs INR6,500 crore in Sep-25; agri stress down 35 bps to 3.51%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan outstanding INR33,000 crore; MSME gold loan about INR2,000 crore. Retail gold declined QoQ as loans were reclassified to agri/MSME under RBI norms.

guidance_outlook: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics across growth, profitability, asset quality and capital were met in H1.
Domestic credit guidance is 18%; management sees no challenge sustaining above 18% with INR23,000 crore pipeline and INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Recovery target from written-off accounts of INR1,300-1,500 crore annually for the next 4-5 years; FY27 recovery so far INR1,023 crore.
ECL: total assessed requirement INR2,500 crore over 4 years; INR750 crore already provided (INR250 crore earlier plus INR500 crore in Q2), which management says covers more than 1 year.
Maharashtra debt-waiver government receivable (about INR2,700 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore): about INR1,200 crore received to 30 Sep; SLBC timeline for balance is 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 200 branches planned annually; 77 branches made functional in H1 FY27.
Employee strength raised to 17,500 from about 13,000 two years earlier, driven by branch expansion and specialist hiring (treasury, IBU, IT).
IT budget: INR900 crore in FY25 and INR985 crore in FY26, with a large share on cyber security.
Pipeline sector mix: infra power about 18%, roads/HAM about 12%, renewables about 10%, metals and others about 10%; data centres cited as a niche growth area.
demand_pricing: Credit growth ex-IBU of 23% YoY; IBU book INR18,500 crore funded partly by about $560 million of FCNR(B) leverage. The FCNR(B) special window has closed.
Repricing: management raised rates on several MCLR-linked state PSU facilities (several thousand crore, about 25 bps on some) in Q1, contributing to NIM gains.
Global yield on advances 8.86%, domestic 9.02%; IBU yield not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan pricing tiers: agri lowest, MSME about 50 bps higher, non-priority retail highest.
EBLR-linked loans are 47% of the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning: standard/restructured provisions rose to INR603 crore from INR76 crore; what is the ECL preparedness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPA provisions fell from INR580 crore a year ago to INR120 crore this quarter, helped by recoveries. Standard-asset provisions rose to INR603 crore including INR500 crore of ECL; total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years, with INR750 crore already provided.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth sustain after the FCNR window closes, and will write-off recoveries continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IBU leverage was about $560 million from FCNR(B) and the window is closed; domestic growth is 23% and the INR23,000 crore pipeline supports growth above the 18% guidance. Write-off recovery target is INR1,300-1,500 crore a year for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR(B) is fixed at 6.51%, OFCB at 6.11%, and 1-year CDs at about 7.75-7.9%. About $1.65 billion was raised via FCNR(B) and OFCB against a $1.5 billion plan, with 5-year fixed-cost borrowings and a 3x oversubscribed MTN issue; YoY cost of deposits fell 4 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 30 bps QoQ rise in yield on advances despite IBU mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to repricing of MCLR-linked state PSU accounts (about 25 bps on several thousand crore), a one-off write-off recovery impact of about 2-3 bps on NIM, and a 3-4 bps ITR refund. Only INR30 crore of the INR125 crore recovery has gone to interest income so far.

qa_highlights.question: Drought exposure and restructuring under SLBC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no visible agri stress; special SLBC restructuring applies at 33-50% crop loss (1-year moratorium, up to 3-year tenor) and above 50% loss (5-year tenor including 1-year moratorium). Farmer applications open till February 2027; past experience suggests 10-15% take-up, with about 5% provisioning on the restructured amount.

qa_highlights.question: Agri gold and retail gold trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri gold loans rose to INR18,600 crore from INR6,500 crore YoY. Retail gold declined QoQ because loans were reclassified to MSME/agri under RBI norms; total gold outstanding INR33,000 crore and MSME gold about INR2,000 crore.

risks_watch: Drought and El Nino: Maharashtra drought could trigger SLBC restructuring; management estimates 10-15% take-up and says no visible stress yet.
ECL transition: INR2,500 crore total assessed; management said the number may fall; surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore (COVID, global uncertainties INR200 crore) can be used.
Cost of deposits: QoQ increase from high-cost FCNR(B)/OFCB/CD raises; FY28 impact on margin depends on deployment.
Maharashtra debt-waiver balance of about INR1,500 crore receivable; management does not count on it and timing depends on state process (deadline 31 March 2027).
Pace of IBU growth after the FCNR(B) window closed; IBU yield not disclosed.
Cyber and DPDP compliance; management deferred detailed answer.

qa_highlights.answer: The figure covers forgings and castings together. Management expects 85-90% casting utilisation over the year, with margins of about 15-16% and Rs 400-500 crore of additional revenue. Management declined to put a figure on the incremental revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 debt and capex plans?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and revenue growth in FY27?

qa_highlights.answer: Production starts by Q1 FY27 and about 40,000 wheels are expected in FY27 under the railway offtake guarantee, for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore. Pricing is still being reset for two years of inflation.
