FY27 group capex expected at about Rs 550 crore, with about Rs 160 crore in H2 mainly machining, plus Rs 15-20 crore JV investment in H2 and the balance next year.
FY28 debt reduction aim of Rs 300-400 crore; finance cost savings of about Rs 40 crore per annum from repaying Rs 500 crore at about 8% interest.
FY27 ROCE expected at 12-15% by year end; 20% ROCE set as an aspiration for next year.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by 30-40 bps QoQ; management aims to return to previous peak margins without a timeline.
Management expects a strong H2 FY27 and a strong market for the next six months; no FY28 guidance until full-year results.
Rs 8 crore to Rs 9 crore net shipping cost impact in Q2 expected to persist if freight stays at current levels.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about Rs 390 crore plus Rs 40 crore JV investment; FY27 capex now guided at about Rs 550 crore versus Rs 350 crore guided in Q1.

Railway wheels JV: first-phase 140,000 wheels and second-phase 140,000 wheels; project cost Rs 2,180 crore; Rs 56 crore approval sought for phase 2; remaining JV equity about Rs 50-55 crore to be paid over next year.
Aluminium forging capacity about 3,000 tonnes; aluminium and cold forging utilisation above 50%.
Casting business at about 88% utilisation per analyst; management says capacity is sufficient for the new orders, with any capex planned for next year.
Wheels JV: 80% of capacity targeted in Q4 FY27 for 4,000-5,000 wheels per month.
demand_pricing: Q2 orders Rs 673 crore: 48% domestic, 52% export; Rs 447 crore casting, of which Rs 272 crore North American LV casting for a new customer and new product.
Geographic mix: North America about 58% and Europe about 41% of export revenue, versus Europe about 28% two years ago.
Lead time from order to delivery averages 6 months; exports 9-12 months and domestic 3-4 months.

Steel price pass-through is achieved in domestic market; North American and European contracts did not pass through the Indian steel increase, and Rs 6-7 crore raw material negative carry was absorbed in Q2.
Management expects another domestic steel price hike possibly in January and says it is prepared to pass it on.
Management said shipping rates have largely settled at peak, with no incremental increase seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Rs 447 crore casting orders be executed and is there capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: North American LV casting needs 6-9 months of validation after sample development; domestic casting starts within 12-14 weeks of development. Management said there is enough capacity for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY27 capex risen and how much is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about Rs 550 crore for FY27 across the group, mainly machining and value-add capacity; JV capex of about Rs 50-55 crore is pending over the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt at year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt at March 2026 was Rs 2,173 crore; year-end FY27 gross debt is expected at about Rs 1,670-1,700 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Power and shipping cost trends and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Power cost fell on lower surcharges; other expenses rose on shipping costs, which will ease only when freight falls. Management expects 30-50 bps margin expansion every quarter and aims to return to previous peak margins without a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No inventory gain; there was a negative carry of about Rs 6-7 crore on raw material price increases in exports.

qa_highlights.question: Europe revenue appears flat YoY; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was reallocated to North America, which recovered sharply; the Europe dip is marginal and expected to be recovered next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Shipping cost impact in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Net unrecovered shipping cost impact was about Rs 8-9 crore in Q2; part of the increase has been passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital rose about Rs 140 crore on volume growth, with receivable and inventory days near March levels; shipping delays kept shipments in inventory, and management expects improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company give FY28 or FY29 revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify FY28 growth or revise margin trajectory; Lalit Khetan confirmed an aspiration of Rs 8,000 crore revenue for FY29 but said timing would be updated later. Management said guidance will come after full-year results.

risks_watch: Shipping costs and geopolitical tensions: Rs 8-9 crore quarterly unrecovered freight, and management said some cost will be borne if freight stays high.
Working capital: net working capital up about Rs 140 crore in H1 on higher receivables and inventory from delayed export shipments.
Railway wheels JV: commercial production and RDSO/railway inspection timing, plus funding and the Rs 56 crore phase-2 approval; JV first-year depreciation and interest impact not quantified.
Consolidated margin dilution as casting (lower margin than forgings) scales; management said this may keep consolidated margins somewhat muted.
Europe export revenue flat YoY in Q2, with FTA ratification timing uncertain and no inquiries yet from UK FTA.
532527|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, order flow and near-term utilisation, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to give FY28 guidance, margin timelines or customer-level detail, and gave only six-month visibility.
key_quotes: We believe that high utilization of our existing capaci ty and improved product mix and continued operating discipline will support growth and profitability in the coming quarters.
And I think we are seeing a huge order inflow with new RFQs and new inquiries, I think flooding our system.
Europe FTA is still to be approved by the European Union.
We would like to not comment on what is going to happen in FY28.

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.

segments.name: Digital Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296.8 crore, up 16.1% YoY; EBIT margin 19.3%. TNQTech is integrated here, per management.

segments.name: Digital Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 153.1 crore, up 6.1% YoY; EBIT margin 8.9%. Carries the company's AI R&D spend of about INR 40-50 crore a year, which management says depresses the margin.

segments.name: Digital Experiences
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 64 crore, down 5.3% YoY; EBIT margin 11.7%. Management said several good-sized deals were signed this year and the practice is seeing an upswing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of high single digits, maintained despite market softness.
Full-year EBITDA margin expected to rise about 0.5 percentage point, to close to 20%; management later said 19-20% at year end.
AI R&D spend to stay at about the same level (INR 40-50 crore) in FY27; FY28 budget not yet decided.

Management cited a roughly 3-year target of about INR 3,000 crore revenue, versus about INR 2,000 crore now, to be a mix of organic and inorganic growth; it was described as starting in the current year.
Annual salary increments effective April 2026 are already reflected in Q1 numbers.
M&A dialogue is ongoing but no deal has matured to disclosure stage.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were discussed.

AI platforms cited as growth drivers: KAiBRE and KAiSDLC for legacy modernisation, KAi underwriting for insurance, agentic claims processing, and SuperCX for contact-centre and front-office automation.
Legacy modernisation projects reportedly compress timelines from about three years to about six months; first underwriting-product revenue has been booked with one customer.
demand_pricing: Customers are choosing Datamatics for AI capability; recent wins include SBI Life Insurance (TruAI underwriting), a US pet and veterinary provider (AI voice agent) and a US consumer products company (KAiBRE/KAiSDLC).
About 60% of deals won this fiscal were AI-led or largely AI-driven, per management.
Deal sizes are rising but are increasingly shorter (3-9 month) AI projects rather than multi-year annuity contracts; management said margins are not shrinking.
Competition is increasingly from well-funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and captive tech teams, not from larger listed IT peers.
Top 5, 10 and 20 clients contribute 30%, 41% and 54% of revenue. Education and Publishing is 29%, technology and consulting 20%, BFSI 19%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AI R&D spend, and is there any plan for buybacks or M&A with the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: AI R&D stays at about INR 40-50 crore this year. Cash of INR 710 crore predates the INR 200 crore TNQTech payout, and management is in M&A dialogue but nothing has matured; no buyback was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth consistent with the full-year guidance, given the strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained high single-digit FY27 growth guidance and cited market softness from the war and uncertainty. The CFO clarified that 43% growth refers to PAT, while revenue grew 9.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Digital Technologies grown slowly with margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to traction in KAi underwriting, KAiSDLC and KAiBRE, with legacy modernisation projects starting. It said the segment carries the AI investment, so removing it would give a much healthier margin.

qa_highlights.question: How has the competitive landscape changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not compete much with large listed IT players. Competition comes from funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and in-house tech teams.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Key risks are customers automating in-house instead of outsourcing, captive/GCC setups, and geopolitical softness.

qa_highlights.question: What is the five-year blueprint and what are the revenue drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about INR 3,000 crore over roughly three years from about INR 2,000 crore now, with organic growth from AI platforms and bolt-on acquisitions.

risks_watch: Customer insourcing to automation and GCC/captive setups could reduce outsourcing budgets, per management.
Geopolitical uncertainty (the war) is cited as softening demand; management said it needs to settle.
Shift toward shorter AI projects (3-9 months) rather than multi-year annuity deals could affect revenue visibility.
Digital Experiences declined 5.3% YoY and Digital Technologies margin is 8.9%; watch for recovery.
Whether AI R&D spend (INR 40-50 crore) remains flat next year is undecided.
532528|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on AI-led deal wins, margins and the INR 3,000 crore ambition, but cautious on near-term demand, which management said remains soft due to the war. Management was vague on TNQTech's standalone contribution and on the FY28 AI spend.
key_quotes: So, we have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that.
We are seeing strong market validation of our AI-first strategy.
So, a project that will take three years can be probably done in six months now.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments (net of debt)
financial_highlights.change: As of 30 June 2026, before INR 200 crore TNQTech payout in Q1

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin rose 343 bps YoY to 19.7% and management guides FY27 EBITDA margin up about 0.5 pp to 19-20%, with EBIT margin up 319 bps to 15.3% in Q1, though AI R&D spend of INR 40-50 cr is held flat.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management held high single-digit FY27 revenue growth (about 9% midpoint) with Q1 revenue up 9.9% to INR 513.9 cr, but cited war-related softness and no volume or order-book numbers were given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only maintained high single-digit revenue growth and 19-20% EBITDA margin guidance while citing market softness from the war, so no raise was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged geopolitical softness, customer insourcing to GCCs and captive teams, and a shift to shorter 3-9 month AI projects, which could pressure the high single-digit growth guide given Digital Experiences fell 5.3%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI platforms KAiBRE, KAiSDLC, KAi underwriting and SuperCX are already in market with first underwriting revenue booked, and about 60% of FY27 deals won are AI-led.

rows.label: INR 3,000 cr revenue ambition over ~3 years from ~INR 2,000 cr
rows.why: Management described it as starting this year, mixing organic AI platform growth with bolt-on acquisitions, but no deal has matured and no revenue phasing was given.

rows.label: M&A dialogue with INR 710 cr net cash (pre INR 200 cr TNQTech payout)
rows.why: Management is in M&A dialogue but no deal has reached disclosure stage, and cash of INR 710 cr is before the INR 200 cr TNQTech payout made in Q1.

rows.label: Digital Experiences recovery
rows.why: Revenue fell 5.3% YoY to INR 64 cr with EBIT margin of 11.7%, but management said several good-sized deals were signed and the practice is seeing an upswing.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI-led deal wins, the 19-20% margin and the INR 3,000 cr ambition, but cautious on near-term demand softness from the war; analysts pushed on the 43% PAT vs 9.9% revenue gap, Digital Technologies margin pressure, and the FY28 AI R&D spend.

532531|2026-03.headline: Strides FY26 revenue rose 6.4% to INR48,587 mn and EBITDA 15% to INR925 crore at 19% margin; Q4 US revenue weak at $70 mn as flu season failed to materialise.
532531|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6.4% YoY to INR48,587 mn, held back by a weak second-half US flu season and donor-funding pressure in access markets; management says underlying growth was about 10% excluding access markets. Ex-US revenue grew 21% and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, while EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 19% for the year. Q4 EBITDA rose 10% YoY to INR240 crore (18.1% margin), with about INR20 crore of logistics and air-freight cost pressure. Operational PAT crossed INR500 crore for the first time at INR518 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR5 per share.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue $284 mn and Q4 $70 mn, hit by a weak second-half flu season; 6 launches in the year, 9 products exited, and some molecules faced higher competition, with leading positions in 37 of 70 products. Controlled substances from the Chestnut Ridge ANDA acquisition are in their first full year, with 4 products launched and quota allocations below expectations.

segments.name: Ex-US (total)
segments.commentary: Grew 21% in FY26 and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, with a 3-year CAGR of about 19%. Quarterly ex-US revenue rose from about $40 mn in Q1 FY24 to about $70 mn in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Other regulated markets (ORM)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue rose from about $31 mn in Q1 FY24 to a $52 mn exit run rate in Q4 FY26, with traction in Europe, UK, Australia and the Nordics.

segments.name: Africa / growth markets
segments.commentary: Focus is shifting toward branded business, with Francophone Africa growing faster than the underlying market. The Sandoz product acquisition (announced Feb 2026) is expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and to lift the branded portfolio more than 1.5x.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration: EBITDA margin upwards of 20% and gross margin in the 58%-60% range; Q&A reiterated a 18%-20% margin range for the near term.
US aspiration of $375-400 mn by FY28, described as a full-year FY28 target rather than an exit run rate; management said about 8 quarters remain.
Sequential growth expected from Q4 to Q1 FY27; Q4 sequential growth stated at 11% (14% excluding institutional business).
US growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27; FY26 seasonality was roughly 50:50 H1:H2 versus the usual 45:55.

Sandoz portfolio expected to contribute from H2 FY27; R&D spend to be $20-25 mn a year over the next 2 years; tangible and intangible investment run rate about INR300 crore; nasal sprays, patches and films expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment INR418 crore: INR236 crore tangible (including nasal spray capacity, ex-US capacity and a UK office) and INR182 crore intangible (global product rights and SAP HANA ERP upgrade).
Tangible capex is nearly complete beyond maintenance; a run rate of about INR300 crore across tangible and intangible is expected, including possible acquisitions of global rights.
Capacity sufficient for the next 2 years; no major additional capacity needed in the next 1-2 years apart from growth capex.
Chestnut Ridge facility (acquired from Endo) is capable of manufacturing nasal sprays and controlled substances; second nasal spray filed in May 2026, with commercialisation about 12 months away.
Patches and thin films: filing expected in 12-18 months.
demand_pricing: US flu-season demand did not recover in H2 as it had in prior years, and wholesaler discipline also contributed.
Marginal US pricing pressure, offset by COGS improvements; gross margin held in the 58%-60% range for 8 quarters.
Intense competition in a few molecules led to market-share rationalisation; management prioritises profitability over volume.
Q4 logistics and air-freight costs of about INR20 crore hurt margins; price increases are being negotiated with customers.
Access markets are facing donor-funding challenges, which management describes as tactical.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in the US, including discontinuations and delayed launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the missing flu season, controlled-substance quota timing, and a policy of not launching until market conditions are attractive. It said 150 products are in the portfolio and launches will continue through FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are controlled substances and nasal sprays structurally higher-margin, and how big is the controlled substances opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said controlled substances are an in-US-for-US strategy and margins will be similar to the current profile, not dramatically different. It declined to give revenue potential, saying the company needs more DEA quota first, and the company has gone back to the DEA for additional quota.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 SG&A and freight spike persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A will stay around the current range, with Q4 freight costs elevated. It said a discount factor should be applied to Q4 when modelling.

qa_highlights.question: What are the nasal spray and new modality timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: One or two nasal products could launch earlier, but bulk revenue is expected in FY28-FY29. Patches and thin films filings are expected in 12-18 months, with about 5-6 additional third-party nasal programmes added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sandoz deal's impact and the R&D outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The Sandoz deal is expected to close in H2 FY27 (October-March). R&D spend is expected to be $20-25 mn over the next 2 years.

risks_watch: US growth depends on a recovery in H2 FY27 and on the controlled-substance quota outcome from the DEA; no timeline was given.
Gross margin needs to stay in the 58%-60% range amid logistics, fuel, raw material and FX cost pressure.
Working capital: cash-to-cash cycle is 124 days, with inventory up 21 days and payables stretched in Q4, which management expects to normalise.
Competition in several US molecules and a 2-year wait before new nasal spray and modality revenue.
Access markets exposed to donor-funding challenges; Sandoz integration timing.
532531|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on ex-US growth, profitability and balance sheet, but cautious and evasive on US timing, quota and controlled-substance sizing. Management repeatedly deferred US recovery to H2 FY27 and declined to quantify the controlled-substance revenue potential.
key_quotes: Ex-U.S. markets have emerged as the most important highlight of our performance.
We are reporting an operational PAT of INR518 crores crossing the INR500 crores mark for the first time.
We have not taken any exit run rate and all that.
I have clearly said that margins will be between the 18% to 20% range.

financial_highlights.value: 21% growth; ex-US about 46% of FY26 revenue and close to 50% in Q4
INR518 crore; EBITDA to operational PAT conversion 56%
INR575 crore; reported EPS INR60.3; operational EPS INR56.2
financial_highlights.change: Reported PAT +40% YoY; includes gain on sale of investment property in Q3

financial_highlights.value: INR136 crore, margin 10.3%; operational EPS INR14.7

financial_highlights.change: From 1.9x last year; constant-currency net debt down INR197 crore

financial_highlights.value: About 40.6% of sales; employee cost 19%, other operating cost 21.5%

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated an 18%-20% EBITDA margin range for the near term after FY26 margin rose 140 bps to 19%, with gross margin held at 58%-60% for 8 quarters; Q4 margin was 18.1% with about INR20 crore of freight cost pressure, and price increases are being negotiated.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said capacity is sufficient for the next 2 years and tangible capex is nearly complete beyond maintenance, with FY26 tangible capex of INR236 crore already commissioned, so no major new capacity is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: US revenue fell to $70 mn in Q4 FY26 on a weak flu season, but management guides to sequential growth from Q4 to Q1 FY27 (Q4 sequential growth 11%) and a US pick-up from H2 FY27; ex-US grew 21% in FY26 and is near 50% of Q4 revenue.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is guided at a run rate of about INR300 crore across tangible and intangible, with tangible nearly complete beyond maintenance and capacity sufficient for 2 years, so no new major capex is signalled beyond growth capex and possible global rights acquisitions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue grew only 6.4% (about 10% ex-access markets) and US is weak at $70 mn in Q4, with management deferring the US recovery to H2 FY27 and not raising guidance; the US $375-400 mn FY28 aspiration was held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: US growth depends on an H2 FY27 recovery and a DEA controlled-substance quota outcome with no timeline, and Q4 freight costs of about INR20 crore persist; access markets face donor-funding pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said launches will continue through FY28 across 150 products, with 6 US launches in FY26 and 4 controlled-substance products launched; one or two nasal products could launch earlier, though bulk nasal revenue is expected in FY28-FY29 and the second nasal spray is about 12 months from commercialisation.

rows.label: Sandoz product acquisition contribution
rows.why: Sandoz deal (announced Feb 2026) expected to close Oct-Mar and lift the branded Africa portfolio more than 1.5x, with contribution from H2 FY27.

rows.label: Net debt to EBITDA improvement
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA fell to 1.55x from 1.9x last year and management is confident of further improvement, with constant-currency net debt down INR197 crore.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation
rows.why: Cash-to-cash cycle rose 7 days to 124 days with inventory up 21 days and payables stretched in Q4; management expects this to normalise but gave no timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on ex-US growth, margins (18-20%) and balance sheet, but cautious and evasive on US timing, DEA quota and controlled-substance revenue sizing, deferring recovery to H2 FY27.

532531|2026-06.headline: Strides Q1 FY27 revenue grew 13% YoY with EBITDA margin at 18.2%, while US revenue was flat at ₹6,282m and Ex-US grew 17% to ₹5,875m.
532531|2026-06.overview: Strides reported 13% YoY topline growth and 5.4% YoY EBITDA growth to ₹229.8 crore at an 18.2% margin, absorbing about ₹13.1 crore of geopolitical freight and operating costs. Reported PAT rose 56.7% to ₹165.5 crore, helped by a ₹53.4 crore net gain from divesting majority stake in Pivot Path. Ex-US revenue grew 17% YoY but fell sequentially from $70m in Q4 FY26 to $63m on supply-chain shipment delays that management calls timing, not demand. US revenue was flat at ₹6,282m ($68m) amid competition in newer launches, and management guided that H2 FY27 will be stronger.

financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY; down from $70m in Q4 FY26
+60 bps YoY; absolute gross margin ₹770.2 crore, +14% YoY
+5.4% YoY; margin -130 bps YoY, vs 18.1% in Q4 FY26
+56.7% YoY; includes ₹53.4 crore net gain from Pivot Path divestment
+7 days YoY; inventory +24 days, payables +15 days
Down ₹11.9 crore QoQ; from 1.55x at FY26 end

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹6,282m ($68m), stable despite competition in recently launched products; 72 commercialised products, 2 launched in the quarter; top-3 positions in 37 products contributing ~70% of US revenue. Chestnut Ridge (US) supplies nearly one-third of US revenue.

segments.name: Ex-US
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹5,875m ($63m), +17% YoY but down from $70m in Q4 FY26 due to supply-chain shipment delays; management expects ~$7m spillover to be recovered in coming quarters. Africa grew strongly via Brands business; UK prescription and Europe/Nordic Branded and OTC performed well.

segments.name: Pivot Path (GCC)
segments.commentary: Majority stake divested, generating ₹74.2 crore gross gain (₹53.4 crore net of tax); Strides retains 20% stake per analyst question.

guidance_outlook: US revenue growth expected to improve in H2 FY27 on new approvals and launches; first two quarters described as soft.
About 10 product launches targeted from now until 31 March 2027.

Ambition of $375m North America business by FY28 retained; management says ~$80-90m must be added from levers including OTC, controlled substances, 100-plus unlaunched products, specialty channels and partnerships.
Ex-US expected to grow faster than company average; Sandoz acquisition expected to close in Q2 FY27 (subject to permissions) and contribute from H2.
Gross margin to stay within 58-60% range; objective of superior EBITDA margins over medium term.
Capex of ₹2.5-3.0 billion per year (maintenance, R&D and hard capex); no greenfield plans at present.
Net debt-neutral targeted in 2-3 years, per management.
capex_capacity: Annual capex envelope ₹2.5-3.0 billion covering maintenance capex, R&D and hard capex, focused on existing factories and high-impact line items.
No greenfield capex being considered currently.
Chestnut Ridge, US facility supplies about one-third of US revenue; controlled substances, nasal sprays, transdermal patches and films are being built around this platform.

Bengaluru plant received a USFDA inspection in May 2026 with observations; response submitted, and management expects USFDA feedback by end-August or September 2026; no current supply impact anticipated.
demand_pricing: US: increased competition in certain products launched over the last few quarters; management says growth strategy prioritises profitability over volume.

US controlled substances: about 5% of group revenue; 4 products demonstrated over ~20 months; quota allocations occur twice yearly (June and December); June-cycle outcome not yet received, December response expected.

Nasal spray: first filing in advanced review, approval expected in H2 FY27 (Q3/Q4 timeframe); second filed about a month ago with 12-15 month review; 5-6 nasal spray programmes planned, plus transdermal and film programmes.
Proposed US tariffs on generic pharmaceuticals from August 2028 flagged; implementation framework still unclear.
Freight and supply-chain disruption from Middle East conflict; inflationary pressure across operating costs; manufacturing costs drove ₹29.0 crore YoY increase in other operating costs (ex-freight).

qa_highlights.question: Why is US soft and how is FY28 $375m target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two quarters will be soft with launches weighted to H2; five levers (controlled substances, new channels, new geographies/partnerships, launches, OTC) are expected to drive growth over the next 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify revenue lost to freight-related supply delays in US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify US loss; said the impact was elongated supply and that Ex-US shipment delays were temporary and expected to be caught up during the year.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt-free path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current net debt is about ₹1,420 crore excluding OneSource investment valued at about ₹320 crore; management expects broad neutrality in 2-3 years, noting ~₹300 crore debt reduction last year offset by rupee depreciation (INR82 to ~INR95-97/USD).

qa_highlights.question: Weighted cost of debt and debt mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of debt is about 7.6%, with major debt in India and the US; interest cost has fallen for 7-8 consecutive quarters. Management said CARE rating covers only a subset of loans.

qa_highlights.question: Controlled substance quota status?
qa_highlights.answer: Quota allocations happen twice a year based on past sales; controlled substances are about 5% of revenue; June cycle did not yield success, with a response expected in the next month.

qa_highlights.question: Product launches in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10 launches planned from now to 31 March 2027, with bulk of launches in H2 and profitability thresholds applied.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for next two years?

532539|2026-06.headline: Uno Minda Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 5,557 crores; EBITDA margin 10.3%, with FY27 guidance of 11% ±50 bps held.
532539|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations hit a record INR 5,557 crores, up 26% YoY against INR 4,420 crores excluding prior-period income. EBITDA excluding prior-year exceptional income grew 21% to INR 572 crores, but margin was 10.3% as commodity and gas inflation, a ~40 bps mathematical pass-through dilution and minimum wage hikes weighed on it. Management kept the annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps, biased to the upper end. PAT attributable to shareholders rose 24% to INR 296 crores, and the company added seating, sunroof and lighting orders while the Inovance JV awaits China approval.

segments.name: Switching systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,335 crores, +20% YoY, 24% of consolidated turnover. 4-wheeler switches under Uno Mindarika grew 24% to INR 525 crores; Manesar to Farrukhnagar shift on track for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,153 crores, +14% YoY, ~21% of revenue. New domestic 4-wheeler lighting nomination from a global OEM; INR 450 crores annual peak value order in 2W lighting; Indonesia 4W lighting plant secured a second customer with SOP in Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Casting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,090 crores, +32% YoY, ~20% of revenue and the fastest-growing vertical. 2W alloy wheel INR 284 crores, 4W alloy wheel INR 56 crores, aluminium die casting INR 248 crores (+66%).

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 408 crores, +28% YoY, ~7% of revenue. Exports INR 72 crores; INR 390 crores annual peak export orders from 3 new customers; INR 320 crores greenfield 4W seating plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, operations by Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 542 crores, +78% YoY, ~10% of revenue. Alternate fuels INR 184 crores, Uno Minda EV Systems INR 186 crores, Uno Minda Automation INR 123 crores, EV controller business INR 37 crores. Like-for-like EV EV Systems plus controller revenue INR 218 crores, +24%.

segments.name: Other (reconfigured)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,029 crores, +21% YoY, ~19% of revenue. Sensors and ADAS INR 250 crores, acoustics INR 225 crores, blow moulding INR 125 crores, non-EV controllers INR 80 crores; sunroof order book crossed INR 500 crores.

segments.name: Aftermarket and SPD
segments.commentary: Aftermarket revenue INR 336 crores (~6%); OEM spare parts division INR 254 crores; combined INR 590 crores, ~11% of consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps, with a bias towards the higher end, reaffirmed despite Q1 headwinds.

FY27 capex stays at about INR 1,750 crores. Total announced project capex is about INR 3,800 crores, of which about INR 1,400 crores is spent; the remaining ~INR 2,000 crores to be spent over 18-24 months.
Gross margin may stay under pressure from commodity pass-through dilution (~40 bps) and lower-margin electronics business, but EBITDA margin should offset this.
Management expects healthy automotive growth through the rest of FY27 and aims to keep outperforming industry volumes.
Export targets: double and triple export value in absolute terms, with export growth needing to outpace domestic growth to raise its share.
Inovance JV: no holdup on plant construction or supplies as of now; more clarity expected in about one quarter.
capex_capacity: Kharkhoda 4W alloy wheel: new 60,000-unit line to be fully ramped up from Q2 FY27; a further 30,000-unit line to commission in H2 FY27.
Bawal 2W alloy wheel: 4 of 6 lines expected live in H2 FY27, adding about 1 million units annual capacity and entering HPDC alloy wheels.
Sunroof plant commissioning by end FY27; ramp in FY27 with full sales from FY28-FY29. Order book above INR 500 crores.
4W seating greenfield plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (INR 320 crores): commencement by Q2 FY28; capex of INR 3.2 billion can generate more than 2x its investment in revenue.
Lighting: consolidation of North India 2W lighting plants into Kharkhoda from H2 FY27; Indonesia lighting plant transition to new facility by end FY27.
Inovance JV plants: Khed City plant construction on schedule; CSN plant to start construction in the next couple of months.
demand_pricing: Indian automotive production in Q1 FY27 was a record 96.9 lakh units (+22% YoY); PV production 14.5 lakh (+17%); 2W 72.5 lakh (+23%); CV 2.9 lakh (+15%).
EV penetration in PV reached 6.8% (84,000 units, +54%); electric 2W registrations crossed 5 lakh in a quarter; electric 3W penetration above 60%.
Customers are passing through commodity costs, with some OEMs moving to monthly price adjustments on one or two commodities and some announcing price hikes.
Seating kit value estimated at INR 30,000-40,000 per car; management says it could become one of the group's largest kit-value products.
Competition in Indian seating is intense; the Tachi-S partnership is cited as a technology edge.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete in 4W seating (segments, market size) and how will H2 growth hold up against a high base, including Inovance SOPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has one 4W seating nomination with more models in talks and will not name vehicles before launch; kit value is INR 30,000-40,000 per car. As of now there is no holdup to Inovance products or plant work, and the H2 growth is supported by Kharkhoda phase 2, 2W alloy wheels and the Mindarika move.

qa_highlights.question: Is green mobility near group profitability, and what is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Some green mobility businesses already earn above group profitability while newer ones are below it; new businesses are expected to reach target profitability in their third full year of production. FY27 capex remains about INR 1,750 crores; FY28 guidance will be given with the annual outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will margins recover toward 11%, and can wage and commodity costs be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: The ~40 bps commodity dilution persists for the rest of FY27 if prices stay high. Management expects to absorb much of the wage increase through automation and productivity and to recover commodities on a quarterly or half-yearly basis, with some customers moving to monthly indexation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Casting uses the WDV method, so new capacity starts from a lower base and Q1 depreciation tends to be lower than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the 4W seating capex and the timing of export and sunroof ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 3.2 billion seating capex can generate more than 2x revenue. Export orders run on a 2-year cycle, with impact from end FY28 and full run-rate in FY29; the sunroof ramp starts around March-April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the China Inovance JV and is e-axle import at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Press Note 3 approval is in hand, but China approval is pending after recent regulatory tightening; Inovance is seeking clarification. There is no current restriction on e-axle imports, and more clarity is expected in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook and the gross margin trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose to INR 228 crores from INR 141 crores, and new business of about INR 400 crores is in the pipeline. Gross margin is diluted by commodity pass-through (~0.4%) and lower-margin electronics, but EBITDA margin is expected to hold given better asset turns.

risks_watch: Inovance JV: China approval pending after tighter technology-partnership rules; possible delay to JV-linked e-drive and EV product launches.
Commodity and gas inflation could persist through FY27, keeping margins under the 11% target until pass-throughs catch up.
JV and associate profit was flat at INR 48 crores, and management expects recovery from Q2 as commodity prices are passed through.
Execution on the INR 2,000 crore capex balance over the next 18-24 months, plus ramp-up of new plants (Bawal, Kharkhoda, sunroof, Sambhajinagar seating).
Green mobility traction-motor volumes are small (2 OEMs), so the segment's profitability path is still unproven.

532540|2026-03.headline: TCS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, third straight sequential gain, with $12B TCV and 25.3% operating margin.
532540|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹70,698 crore (up 5.4% QoQ in INR, $7.621B up 1.5% QoQ, 1.2% QoQ in constant currency), the third consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Q4 TCV was $12B including three mega deals, and client additions were seen across all revenue bands after about two years. Full-year FY26 revenue declined 2.4% in constant currency to $30.017B, while operating margin reached 25%, a four-year high. Management said the restructuring programme is complete, and the company announced annual increments effective April 1 with top performers getting double-digit increases.

financial_highlights.change: +5.4% QoQ INR; +1.5% QoQ USD; +1.2% QoQ CC

Management expects a regular Q1 and Q2 with a stronger first half, which is the planning assumption.
Wage increments effective April 1 are expected to cost 150-200 bps of margin, similar to the past cycle.
Management expects SG&A to rise both in absolute terms and as a percentage of revenue due to Build-Partner-Acquire investments.
Margins are to be kept within a tighter range, with a longer-term aim of moving toward 26%; rupee depreciation helps but is not guaranteed.
Management expects AI revenue to be net accretive to growth in FY27, aiming to arrest the degrowth in traditional services first.
Combined one-off charges for FY26 were ₹1,300 crore; no one-offs were called out in Q4.

FY26 TCV of $40.7B with 5 mega deals; Q4 deal mix was about 50-55% renewals and 40-45% new programmes.
Client additions: 66 accounts above $100M (+4 QoQ), 139 in the $50M+ band (+3), 1,397 in the $1M+ band (+14); every revenue band added clients after about two years.
Pricing: realisations improved, contributing about 40 bps to Q4 margin; management said TCS does not lose deals on pricing.
Clients are shifting from experimentation to industrialised AI, with vendor consolidation and cost optimisation a major theme.
Geopolitical impact so far is limited to the Middle East and travel and transportation; no broad client caution reported outside BFSI-specific caution.
Management said AI deals are 12-16 week rapid builds, and that agentic AI in business process services is gaining traction.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 international growth return to the 3-4% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan declined to give a number but said the company is quite positive on FY27 and on international growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is elevated SG&A the new normal, or will it return below 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Seksaria said investments in partnerships, recruitment, training and new businesses will keep SG&A elevated, both in absolute terms and as a share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are restructuring costs still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs were called out in Q4; the combined FY26 one-off was ₹1,300 crore. Krithivasan said the restructuring programme is complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected margin impact of wage hikes next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Seksaria said the impact should be similar to the past annual increment cycle, which was 150-200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth being sacrificed for margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan said margin is not hurting growth; the margin allows competitive pricing and funds investments such as acquisitions and HyperVault.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI revenue be net accretive to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan said AI is expected to be net accretive in the first year, with the aim of arresting the degrowth in traditional services.

532540|2026-06.headline: TCS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to ₹72,275 crore, but operating margin fell 130 bps QoQ to 24% on wage hikes.
532540|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹72,275 crore, up 2.2% QoQ and 13.9% YoY in rupee terms, and the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. In dollar terms revenue was $7,624 million, flat QoQ and up 2.7% YoY; constant currency growth was 0.4% QoQ and 3.2% YoY. TCV was $9.5 billion, including an $800 million mega deal with SKF. Operating margin fell to 24% (down 130 bps QoQ), with a 170 bps hit from annual salary increments partly offset by 40 bps of currency benefit and efficiencies. Management said clients deferred some projects amid geopolitical uncertainty and expects demand to improve sometime in Q2.

segments.name: Technology, Software and Services

segments.name: Manufacturing

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare

segments.name: Consumer Business Group
segments.commentary: Pressured by inflation and geopolitics affecting discretionary spend; airlines in North America and non-essential retail under stress.

segments.name: CMI and ERU
segments.commentary: CMI saw modest growth amid industry headwinds; ERU declined slightly, with management positive on AI infrastructure, electrification and renewables.

segments.name: Regional Markets

532540|2026-09.headline: TCS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 0.5% QoQ in constant currency to ₹73,188 crore; operating margin held at 24% amid higher subcontracting and investments.
532540|2026-09.overview: Constant-currency revenue grew 0.5% QoQ and 2.8% YoY, with international up 1.2% QoQ and India up 6% QoQ, though Regional Markets fell on an India project deferral. Growth broadened across BFSI, Manufacturing and Technology & Services, while Consumer and ERU declined. Operating margin was stable at 24% and net margin 19%, with management prioritising investment (higher bench, subcontractors, partnerships, M&A) over near-term margin expansion. Annualised AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion, over 10% of revenue, and TCV was $9.6 billion excluding Porsche and Best Buy deals.

financial_highlights.value: US$9.6 billion (excludes Porsche and Best Buy deals)

financial_highlights.change: AI revenue grew ~19% per analyst question, not disputed

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Largest large vertical and biggest growth contributor: +2.5% QoQ and +3.9% YoY in constant currency, broad-based across banking, capital markets and insurance.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: +3.1% QoQ and +4.2% YoY; demand improving in factory automation, engineering productivity, and industrial AI.

segments.name: Technology and Services
segments.commentary: +3.1% QoQ and +4.8% YoY, driven by enterprise software, cloud modernisation and digital transformation; traditional app and infra portfolios seeing agentic AI adoption.

segments.name: Consumer Business
segments.commentary: -0.7% QoQ and -1% YoY; retail and consumer products hit by inflation, energy costs and insourcing, though QoQ decline improved versus prior quarter.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: +0.3% QoQ, stable demand from compliance, clinical/research platforms and AI-enabled drug discovery.

segments.name: Communications and Media
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ; media and digital platforms offset by continued telecom pressure.

segments.name: Energy, Resources and Utilities
segments.commentary: -0.5% QoQ; management sees medium-term structural recovery.

segments.name: Regional Markets / India
segments.commentary: India revenue grew 6% QoQ, while Regional Markets grew 3.6% YoY; management cited a project deferral in India (not hardware pass-through) that reduced Regional Markets revenue, expected to return in medium term.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance; management expects medium-term growth momentum to continue based on TCV, pipeline and client conversations.
Long-term EBIT margin aspiration unchanged at 26%-28%; near-term priority remains investment, so management says it will 'inch up' from 24% rather than commit to 25% exit.
H2 headwinds flagged: MHP acquisition dilution of about 50 bps (timing-dependent), normal furlough seasonality and continued ecosystem investments.
Q3 furlough expected to be similar to prior years; BSNL deal expected to provide cushion for next couple of quarters.
North America expected to recover and become healthy soon; Consumer expected to improve medium term, with Q3 seasonally important.
Data center business: capacity to be built after contracts are signed; revenue expected 18-24 months after start.
capex_capacity: Higher bench and subcontractor usage to meet near-term new-age skill demand; hiring lags deployment for new skills.
Acquisition of MHP (Porsche-linked mobility engineering) subject to regulatory approvals; Best Buy GCC engagement announced.

Expanding into data center services, GCC and mid-market offerings, ServiceNow, Public Services and Sovereign Cloud.
demand_pricing: Demand environment not materially changed QoQ; discretionary programs without near-term value remain under scrutiny.
Three AI demand patterns: AI-native outcome solutions, AI-led enterprise systems transformation, and autonomous GBS; AI governance and secure platforms becoming a top need.
Pricing: management said AI revenue is priced better, revenue per employee slightly lower, and overall portfolio pricing broadly stable.
Subcontracting rose across India and overseas; only partly linked to visa fee hike.
Win rates improved; growth attributed partly to vendor consolidation in traditional services.

qa_highlights.question: Will the international growth momentum continue in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not comment on the next quarter but is confident of medium-term growth based on TCV, pipeline and client conversations.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the India revenue decline and client-count drop?
qa_highlights.answer: A project deferral in India caused the decline, expected to return in later quarters; the client drop below the $100 million band was a single account pushed below the threshold by currency movement.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin levers toward 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir Seksaria cited subcontracting cost reduction, investments starting to deliver, productivity, utilisation and non-employee expense control; long-term aspiration stays at 26%-28%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline QoQ, and what is the margin path to exit FY27 at 25%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin decline reflects higher subcontractor and third-party expenses; H2 headwinds include ~50 bps MHP dilution, so management will only aim to inch margins up.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI revenues margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: The $3.1 billion annualised AI revenue comes in at a much higher margin than the company average.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40% YoY growth in delivery-related costs an upfront investment that will pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir said it is a combination of investment in capacity ahead of growth and partnership costs; subcontracting is an optimisation lever, and fees to external consultants carry incremental delivery cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America lagging, and how will Consumer and ERU play out in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects North America to recover soon based on TCV and client conversations; Consumer expected to improve medium term, ERU to recover structurally over medium term.

risks_watch: Margin: investments and subcontracting keep gross margin under pressure; MHP dilution ~50 bps in H2 and BSNL timing uncertain.
Regional Markets volatility from lumpy deliveries; India deferral revenue expected back but no date given.
AI deflation from productivity gains may offset AI-led growth in BFSI and Hi-Tech; management would not call it complete.
Consumer and ERU continue to decline; telecom remains under pressure.
Discretionary spend and North America recovery timing remain uncertain.
Bench and hiring ahead of demand; conversion of new-skill capacity into revenue needs to show in coming quarters.

532548|2026-03.headline: Century Plyboards posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,492 crores (+24.5% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex at 13.6%.
532548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores, up 10.5% QoQ and 24.5% YoY, with consolidated EBITDA margin excluding forex losses at 13.6% versus 12.6% in Q3 and 12.1% a year ago. For FY26, revenue grew 19.2% and EBITDA ex-forex rose to INR 702 crores (13.0% margin) from INR 502 crores (11.1%), with PAT up 44% to INR 268 crores. Management has taken a 7% plywood price increase in April and an industry-wide 15% increase in MDF/particle board amid chemical and resin cost inflation, but gave no FY27 segment guidance, citing fluid geopolitical conditions. Capex is focused on plywood (Hoshiarpur, UP, Orissa land), with no frozen capex for MDF or particle board.

financial_highlights.change: +10.5% QoQ, +24.5% YoY; highest ever quarterly revenue
vs 12.6% in Q3 FY26 and 12.1% in Q4 FY25
from INR 502 crores in FY25; margin 13.0% vs 11.1%

financial_highlights.value: Growth 11.4% QoQ, 17.9% YoY; EBITDA margin ex-forex 16.1%

financial_highlights.change: Revenue +8.9% QoQ, +31% YoY; margin down ~1 pt QoQ

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% QoQ and +17.9% YoY with 16.1% EBITDA margin ex-forex; FY26 revenue +15.6%, EBITDA margin 15.2%. Capacity utilisation near 99% in Q4 per Nikita Bansal; current capacity 4,06,000 CBM as of March 2026.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +8.3% QoQ and +16.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 10.3%; FY26 revenue +13.9% with margin 8.5% vs 5.2% in FY25. Badvel thick-laminate plant utilisation 47%; overall utilisation 84% on 87.7 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +8.9% QoQ and +31% YoY, EBITDA margin ex-forex 11.3% after ~1 pt QoQ erosion from chemical-related disruptions and one-off ATL spend; FY26 revenue +25.5%, margin 12.7% vs 10.1%. Utilisation ~80-85%; Badvel shut down in Q4 to add 20% capacity; South plant brownfield adds 60,000-70,000 CBM in Q1 FY27 (total to ~6 lakh CBM).

segments.name: Particle Board
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +3.9% QoQ and +108.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 7.2%; FY26 revenue +38.2% but FY26 EBITDA margin only 1.2%. Old multi-daylight plant shut and to be scrapped; new continuous line capacity 2,40,000 CBM, Chennai plant cost cited at ~INR 550 crores.

segments.name: Century Ports
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiary commenced commercial operations at KPD-1 West, Kolkata, in Q4 FY26; management expects it to be cash positive from Q1 FY27. Management said no cost saving accrues to Century Ply; it remains a separate profit centre.

guidance_outlook: No segment-wise FY27 guidance given; management said the situation is too fluid, with a stated intent to provide guidance at the next call.
Management expects ROE and ROCE to improve further as it sweats assets built over the last 3 years.
MDF steady-state EBITDA margin targeted in the high teens, timeline not specified.
Plywood planning assumes muted 10-12% volume growth and 80% utilisation for expansion planning.
Long-term debt not expected to exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA; working capital debt expected to rise with growth.
Laminates expected to outgrow the industry by 3-4 percentage points.
capex_capacity: Plywood: Hoshiarpur plant (48,000 CBM) due in October 2026 (second half FY27); brownfield expansion at Kandla, Chennai and Guwahati adds ~20% (Chennai ~25,000-30,000 CBM by July 2026).

Plywood: UP plant capex expected to start late FY27 (Feb-March 2027 or Q1 FY28), commissioning in about 15-16 months after land is ready, targeted around Q1 FY29; Orissa land procurement underway (MoU covers plywood or MDF/particle board, nothing finalised).
MDF: South plant brownfield expansion adds 60,000-70,000 CBM per year, completion targeted by end of Q1 FY27; no further MDF capacity firmed up.
Particle board: new 2,40,000 CBM continuous line running; old plant to be scrapped with no plan to revive.

Capex for FY27-28 is predominantly plywood-directed; no frozen capex for MDF or particle board. Management cited ~INR 2,000 crores of total capex over the next 4-5 years as an analyst estimate, not confirmed by management.
Century Ports absorbed roughly INR 260-270 crores of spend over three years, per analyst.
demand_pricing: Plywood: 7% price increase taken in April 2026, with further hikes contingent on the chemical and timber trend; management described it as wait-and-watch.
MDF and particle board: industry-wide price increase of about 15% in Q4 FY26, which management said barely covers the chemical-driven cost rise; some peers have made selective rollbacks.
Vishu Goel said MDF and plywood price increases of 10-12% were largely in Q1 and predominantly cover chemical cost increases.
Timber prices reported as broadly stable; management described a marginal correction, not 10%.
Plywood secondary demand stable post price increase, per management; MDF demand described as stable with normal April-May correction from Q4 exuberance.
March 2026 channel stocking was cited as a partial driver of MDF Q4 volume growth; management said April was not slow.
Plywood Sainik MR (around 8% of revenue last quarter) is being moved in-house after Hoshiarpur comes online, to reach 100% in-house production.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of MDF's ~39% YoY growth, utilisation and price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas cited year-end stocking, network expansion in the South and secondary-channel demand; utilisation 80-85% of rated capacity, with a practical max of 85-90%. Industry price increase of 15% barely covers chemical cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 segment guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said the situation is too fluid to guide now; management expects to be in a better position at the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity plans for plywood FY27-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikita Bansal said utilisation is near 99% in Q4 and capacity rises ~30% in FY27 (about 20% brownfield plus Hoshiarpur in October); a new plant is needed in FY28-29, with UP and Orissa land being procured.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the new particle board plant cost lower than earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said the old multi-daylight plant (~INR 70 crores) was archaic and is being scrapped. The new continuous line cost about INR 550 crores, not INR 700 crores as the analyst cited.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for MDF after Q4 erosion?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said Q4 margin fell ~1 pt QoQ from chemical disruptions and one-off ATL spend; steady state is a high-teens EBITDA margin, with no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels, forex exposure and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Julasaria said long-term debt will not exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA, working capital debt will rise with growth, and forex exposure is within INR 600 crores, mostly mark-to-market on long-term debt for imported machinery. Management is not increasing forex exposure.

risks_watch: Chemical (phenol, melamine, resin) and imported timber cost inflation tied to geopolitical disruption; management said the 15% price hike barely covers costs and its stickiness is unknown.
Possible price rollbacks by peers in MDF and particle board, which could affect pass-through and margins from Q1 FY27.
MDF margin recovery to high-teens EBITDA depends on chemical stabilisation; no timeline given.
Forex mark-to-market losses on long-term import debt, capped at about INR 600 crores by management.
Execution risk on Hoshiarpur (October 2026), South MDF brownfield (Q1 FY27), and UP and Orissa land timing.
Particle board FY26 EBITDA margin of only 1.2%; ramp-up of the new line is needed.
Plywood Sainik MR in-sourcing could constrain volume growth relative to the capacity addition.

532548|2026-06.headline: Century Plyboards Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue hit record INR1,561 crore (+33.5% YoY) and PAT rose 57% to INR83.3 crore, helped by a 7% plywood price hike.
532548|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly consolidated revenue of INR1,561 crore, up 33.5% YoY, with EBITDA margin excluding forest losses at 13.0% and PAT up 57% YoY to INR83.3 crore. Plywood led, with revenue up 32.4% YoY and EBITDA margin of 16.9%, aided by a ~7% price increase taken in April on chemical input cost pressure. MDF was hit by a planned shutdown for the Andhra Pradesh capacity expansion (700 to 950 CBM/day), causing a sequential revenue decline, though revenue still grew ~29% YoY. Management has stopped giving formal guidance citing volatility, and said capex will be restrained with focus on utilisation and debt reduction.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Revenue +32.4% YoY and +8.9% QoQ with 16.9% EBITDA margin after ~7% April price hike. Management attributes growth to price-led dealer stocking plus strong June and July sales.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue +14.7% YoY, EBITDA margin 10.2% on mix and utilisation. New home press commissioned, export-grade manufacturing planned from end-July 2026. Volume de-grew QoQ on size adjustment, per analyst question.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~29% YoY but down sequentially due to Andhra Pradesh expansion shutdown (700 to 950 CBM/day). Management targets 15%+ EBITDA margin without a date.

segments.name: Particle board
segments.commentary: Revenue +155.7% YoY and +29% QoQ on higher utilisation; margins still early-stage. Management expects ~15% margins next year.

segments.name: Logistics (Khidderpore Docks / CFS)
segments.commentary: Operations stabilised and EBITDA-positive; 9,000+ containers handled in July. Management is evaluating a possible strategic partner at valuation accretive to the company.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance on revenue, volume or margins; management cites volatility from geopolitical developments.
MDF: aim for 15%+ EBITDA margin as soon as possible; growth trajectory to be maintained for FY27.
Particle board: margins to rise quarter-on-quarter with utilisation; ~15% margin targeted next year.
Long-term: ROCE target of 20% for MDF and particle board; long-term debt to be within 1x EBITDA.
Revenue aspiration: INR12,000 crore, implying ~INR4,000 crore incremental revenue; indicative incremental capex ~INR2,500 crore at 1.5-2x asset turnover.
capex_capacity: Hoshiarpur greenfield plywood plant (60,000 CBM per annum) expected to commence in Q3 FY27.
Chennai brownfield plywood capacity: 8,000 CBM/month in Q1, 10,000 in Q2, 12,500 from Q3 FY27.
Andhra Pradesh MDF expanded from 700 to 950 CBM/day during Q1.

Uttar Pradesh plywood plant (~INR200 crore capex) targeted for April 2028 if land is secured by year-end; UP MDF to follow with a lag, timing not finalised. Odisha project still at land-selection stage.

No large capex planned in the near term; third laminate press capex ~INR25 crore; no large MDF or particle board capex planned. Particle board capacity expansion beyond ~240,000 CBM via efficiencies only, not 20%+.
demand_pricing: Industry growing ~5-7%; company estimates its share at 9.5-10% of the industry at end-FY26, targeting 15% in five years (implies 12-15% annual growth).

Price hike: ~7% in plywood (April), ~15% in MDF (part since rolled back as raw material prices moved), ~10% in domestic laminate and slightly lower in exports. Price increases remain above pre-war levels across most segments.
Channel inventory at June-end described as okay; July was a high sales month to date.
Brand spend ~4-4.5% of revenue including schemes. Total Cover assurance programme (10-year, covers furniture-related costs) launched; management states claim ratio of 0.06%.
Management declined to give volume guidance or premium/standard split.

qa_highlights.question: Is plywood growth from industry growth or share gain, and where is market share heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says share was 9.5-10% last year and the goal is 15% in five years. Growth was driven by the 7% price hike, dealer stocking and a strong June. Quarterly share is not tracked.

qa_highlights.question: When will balance sheet and gearing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose on working capital for ~33% growth in a 60-day debt industry. Cash flows go to debt repayment, with no large capex planned. Target is long-term debt within 1x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is it possible to give MDF FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance has been stopped due to volatility. The objective is 15%+ MDF margins and a good growth trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Will particle board capacity increase by minor capex to ~3 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The line was pre-designed in two parts. Efficiency gains are possible but a 20%+ increase is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for UP and Odisha greenfield projects?
qa_highlights.answer: UP land is not yet secured; target is to acquire by year-end, with the plywood plant by April 2028. Odisha is still in government talks with no land selected. UP MDF timing is not finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable ROCE for MDF and particle board, given particle board capex and realisation differences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the analyst's numbers do not match its capacity basis. The target for both segments is 20% ROCE, which it believes is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the logistics business and its structure?

532555|2026-03.headline: NTPC group added a record 9,618 MW in FY26 and standalone Q4 PAT rose 51.4% to INR8,747 crores.

Group PAT rose 15% to INR27,546 crores and NGEL revenue grew 29% in FY26. Management guided to about 9,557 MW of FY27 capacity additions, mostly renewables via JVs and subsidiaries, and flagged a higher FY27 renewable grid-connectivity risk. Management said West Asia tensions have no material operational impact, with about 18 days of coal stock and about 18% of coal needs met from captive mines.

532555|2026-06.headline: NTPC reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 5,343 crore, up 12% YoY, and targets 150 GW by FY32 and 250 GW by FY37.

Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 5,343 crore (up 12% YoY) and said FY26 standalone PAT was a record INR 23,162 crore. Renewable additions lagged target: 4.2 GW in FY26 and 1.9 GW added in FY27 to date, against a FY27 RE target of 7-8 GW. Technical-minimum and curtailment issues for thermal units, and a shift in the tender vs cost-plus debate, were the main analyst focus.

segments.commentary: Group coal capacity 66 GW at March 2026, planned to reach 77 GW, with 17 GW in pipeline (total 91 GW). Under-construction thermal around 16 GW. Sinnar 1,350 MW acquired with Mahagenco, first unit targeted this calendar year.

qa_highlights.question: Can NTPC accelerate RE additions, given FY26 missed target and FY27 target of 7 GW vs about 0.6 GW delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said RE should not be measured in MW alone; storage is needed, and 7 GW with storage is equivalent to about 8 GW. Transmission delays are a key constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How does NTPC plan to handle thermal units falling below technical minimum during peak solar hours?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a regulatory change allowing shutdown below 55% with capacity charges still recovered, co-located BESS of 5 GWh at thermal plants, and advocacy for uniform technical minimum. Smaller flexible units are being designed for cycling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for coal capacity and FY32-37 RE additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal capacity to reach 77 GW by FY32 and 91 GW with pipeline; beyond that, additions depend on RE and demand. Nuclear to reach about 6 GW by FY37.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend payout policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Director (Finance) said payout will hover around 36-40%, with dividend trend maintained through FY37.

qa_highlights.answer: CMD said NTPC focuses on brownfield cost-plus projects with PPAs for healthy and transparent returns. Director (Finance) cited limited equity capacity and stated that competitive bids would compress margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will NTPC add coal gasification and nuclear capacity, and is there a plan for smaller flexible thermal units?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal gasification (SNG) is a significant opportunity; NTPC considers itself a serious contender for the INR 37,000 crore scheme. Smaller flexible units could amount to tens of GW, to be located at load centres and designed for fast start and stop, pending regulatory approval.

Pipalkoti pumped storage may slip a few months past FY28 year-end.

532555|2026-09.headline: NTPC standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR 45,752 crore and PAT 14% to INR 5,320 crore; NGEL revenue up 53%.

NGEL's revenue and EBITDA grew about 53-57% in Q2, but renewable capacity addition is behind plan due to transmission delays, with FY27 group target cut from about 9.5 GW to about 8 GW. Management flagged coal supply tightness (5.2 MMT stock, about 7 days) and is sourcing 13 MMT from alternative sources for H2. A first interim dividend of INR 3 per share was recommended.

segments.commentary: H1 power traded 31 BU vs 24.8 BU (+25%); commissioned 250 MW / 500 MWh BESS as an implementing agency.

532626|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR 932 crores and FY26 PAT rose 113% to INR 139 crores, with copper cathode capex of about INR 200 crores funded from internal accruals.
532626|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 production, sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with FY26 revenue of INR 2,939 crores (+45%) and EBITDA of INR 218 crores (7.4% margin). Operating cash flow was negative in FY26, which management attributed to about INR 265 crores of trade receivables, mainly an export shipment delayed by vessel movement that pushed INR 120-130 crores of collections into early April. Management also disclosed a 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant (Phase 1 of 18,000 tpa targeted for December 2026) and some trading volumes in Q4, which it said were opportunistic.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be funded through internal accruals with no term loan. Total reserves plus equity is about INR 800 crores, borrowings about INR 150 crores (all short-term), and there is no long-term debt.

532626|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR931 crore and PAT 32% to INR36 crore, while lead volumes fell on supply-chain disruption.
532626|2026-06.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY to INR931 crore, INR56 crore and INR36 crore, with EBITDA margin about 6%. Copper volumes more than tripled YoY to record levels and copper EBITDA per ton rose 66% to INR48,488. Lead volumes moderated as shipping delays via the Strait of Hormuz constrained scrap imports, and management chose to prioritise value-added products (85% of lead revenue), giving a record lead EBITDA of INR21,595 per ton. Management says demand is intact and the constraint is supply, not demand.

segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q1 with net profit of about INR15 lakh on about 800 tonnes of volume.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Small production of about 200 metric tonnes in the quarter.

2030 roadmap: over 15% volume growth, 20%+ CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, over 60% revenue from value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Is there demand softness in lead, given exposure to Western and Middle East markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand softness; exports are mainly Southeast Asia. Only supply delays are affecting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 16% YoY and 44% QoQ?

qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance INR20-25 crore; the balance of INR140-150 crore is for the new copper plant.
