rows.label: CRISIL outlook upgraded to A positive
rows.why: CRISIL upgraded outlook to A positive from A stable and reaffirmed the rating, a credit-positive signal alongside copper ramp-up.

tone.note: Management was confident on the copper ramp-up, raised copper EBITDA/t guidance and held the 2030 margin target, but was cautious and vague on lead volumes, deferring a firm view for 1-2 months; analysts pressed on lead volume shortfall, other expense rise of 44% QoQ, and the normalisation of record

532628|2026-09.headline: 3i Infotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4.1% YoY to ₹182 crore; H1 EBITDA margin ~7% with ₹2 crore operating cash flow.
532628|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about ₹182 crore, up roughly 4.1% YoY and 2.3% QoQ, with H1 revenue near ₹360 crore (+4.2%). Q2 EBITDA was ₹13.7 crore (7.5% margin) and PAT ₹6.7 crore; H1 EBITDA was ₹25.2 crore and PAT ₹13.2 crore, though year-ago figures included about ₹27 crore of one-time US ERC credit, so comparisons are not like-for-like. Management reorganised the business into three capability-aligned service lines from October 2026 and said modest growth should accelerate over the next two to three quarters. Legacy matters (e-Mudhra, RailTel arbitration, RBI/FEMA, inter-company balances) remained open.

segments.name: Digital Engineering Services (formerly Application, Automation & Analytics)
segments.commentary: Largest unit at ~74.1% of H1 FY27 revenue; covers application engineering and modernisation, enterprise apps, data and analytics, intelligent automation and quality engineering.

segments.name: Cloud Infrastructure & Security Services (formerly Infrastructure Services)
segments.commentary: ~17.9% of H1 FY27 revenue; focus on hybrid cloud, cybersecurity, digital workplace, enterprise automation and AI operations.

segments.name: Business Process Services
segments.commentary: ~7.8% of H1 FY27 revenue; management flagged headwinds from AI-driven automation and BFSI regulatory tightening in India.

segments.name: Geography: US / India / Middle East / APAC
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue split: US ₹89.4 crore (~49.1%), India ₹63.6 crore (~34.9%), Asia Pacific ₹4.5 crore; Middle East ₹24.5 crore, up 54.3% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: No numeric revenue guidance for H2 FY27 or FY28; management said momentum should continue from H1 levels.
Management expects modest growth to accelerate over the next two to three quarters, with growth focus on AI-led platforms, cybersecurity, cloud and automation.
Wage increase effective 1 October 2026 will raise wage costs from Q3 FY27; management said it will be absorbed without impact on EBITDA or PAT.
e-Mudhra decision on whether to pursue or drop the claim (claim made public at over ₹100 crore) expected within about four weeks; no P&L impact expected from either path.
RailTel arbitration expected to take one to two more quarters before exposure can be assessed; base claim already provided for.
capex_capacity: Setting up a separate subsidiary for AI, analytics and automation CoEs, approved by the Board; partnerships possible later.
Right-of-use assets rose in H1 due to a new 5-year lease for one location.
Rights issue completed October 2025; proceeds used for building CoEs, with part parked in FDs and bonds.
Working capital of over ₹20 crore invested in new contracts in India and Middle East during H1.
Over 150 data and advanced analytics professionals and 350 certified automation and quality engineering specialists; 12 specialised CoEs plus 2 corporate CoEs.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 added 25 new clients across banking, insurance, energy, manufacturing, government, consumer and technology.
Middle East revenue grew 54.3% QoQ to ₹24.5 crore on new business; new geographies Canada and East Africa added last quarter.

DSO rose because about ₹20 crore of receivables from two Middle East and a few Indian opportunities (built up late July to early August 2026) was outstanding at September end; management expects normalisation as collections start in Q3.
Management is building a new GCC sales sub-team, as it currently lacks expertise in the segment.
Management said it has no specific ESG strategy; EnGRC is a small governance, risk and compliance workflow tool.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth is expected in H2 FY27 and FY28, and what are the growth catalysts for Vision 2030?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric outlook given; management said growth would accelerate over two to three quarters, with focus on AI platforms, cybersecurity, cloud and automation. FY26 was a deliberate clean-up of loss-making businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Constant-currency growth, DSO increase, tax provision and FX hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency growth is not currently published but may be added. DSO rise was due to ~₹20 crore of receivables from late-period opportunities. India has large carried-forward losses; US tax provided with auditors. No FX hedging, as US revenue and roughly 70% of costs are in USD.

qa_highlights.question: Legacy issues: are they resolved, and what is the cash exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: RBI/FEMA settlement application still pending with RBI. Inter-company legacy balances in some entities run to ~₹900-1,000 crore, provided for where not recoverable; no top-ups needed in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowings rise while cash is ₹70-75 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Month-end overdrafts against FDs and bonds are used to meet salaries and repaid in the first week of the next month to avoid breaking FDs. Average borrowing is ~20% of the balance-sheet figure. US credit line fluctuates with US profits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the e-Mudhra matter and RailTel arbitration?
qa_highlights.answer: EOW deemed the complaint not criminal, at best civil. Decision on pursuing or dropping the claim (over ₹100 crore) within about four weeks. RailTel arbitration in witness stage; base claim already provided, with possible additional interest or costs not expected to be large.

qa_highlights.question: Which industries are targeted, and how is differentiation achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is BFSI, telecom, IT companies, retail, healthcare and logistics, varying by geography. Differentiation is building industry SME depth; management said it is not a unique differentiator versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the robotics/automation exposure and GCC business share?
qa_highlights.answer: No production robotics; focus is back-end process automation. GCC is a new segment with no major presence yet; a separate sales sub-team is being built.

risks_watch: Revenue growth remains modest (~4%); management has not quantified H2 or FY28 targets.
Open legacy items: RBI/FEMA settlement pending, inter-company balances of ~₹900-1,000 crore, and e-Mudhra and RailTel proceedings.
Wage hike from Q3 FY27 is a cost headwind that management says will be absorbed.
DSO elevated at September 2026 end; collections on ~₹20 crore of receivables are expected from Q3.
Business Process Services faces AI-driven and BFSI regulatory headwinds.
Management did not provide constant-currency growth; no FX hedging in place despite USD-dependent exposure.
532628|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the transformation narrative and near-term momentum, but evasive on forward numbers and on constant-currency growth. Candid about legacy issues being slow to resolve, with several items still pending.
key_quotes: We are done with the base work of building capabilities and execution and now, as we move into the second half of FY27, our focus is on building business momentum, expanding our market presence, and driving sustainable profitable growth.
Now we have started seeing modest growth and expect it to accelerate over the next two to three quarters.
There is no financial implication of this because there was no claim from their side. It was our claim and which we have not accounted for.

financial_highlights.change: Prior year included ~₹27 crore one-time US ERC credit (net of tax)
After >₹20 crore working capital investment in new contracts

532630|2026-03.headline: Gokaldas Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to about 12% (16% ex-tariff impact per management), with FY27 guided to a couple of points of margin improvement.
532630|2026-03.overview: FY26 was disrupted by US reciprocal tariffs that stayed near 50% for much of the year, with AGOA lapse hitting Africa, yet total income rose 4% to INR4,065 crores and the EBITDA margin was held at the prior-year level. Q4 standalone margins improved on volume-driven operating leverage and the post-February normalisation of the penal tariff, with no tariff refunds booked. Management guides to a Y-o-Y margin improvement of a couple of percentage points in FY27 and Africa revenue of about $115-120 million, while BTPL is being merged in and is expected to turn EBITDA positive in H2 FY27. Net debt rose by INR395 crores on capex, BTPL investment and working capital, and management targets a INR75-100 crore working capital reduction in Gokaldas and Atraco.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone operating EBITDA margin Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.value: about 12% (about 16% adding back tariff impact; about 15.5% excluding provision reversals)
financial_highlights.change: Improved Q-o-Q and Y-o-Y, per analyst read of 200-400 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Net discount to customers FY26 (tariff offset)

segments.name: India operations (Gokaldas standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 operations grew 2% Y-o-Y while Indian apparel exports fell 10%; FY26 India operations grew 10% Y-o-Y. Standalone volume was 10.19 million pieces in Q4 (8.6 million ex-Matrix at INR773 realisation) and 33.627 million pieces for FY26 at INR765.

segments.name: Africa (Atraco)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about $80 million; FY27 target $115-120 million, with H1 run-rate about $24-25 million per quarter. Q4 volume 5.63 million pieces at INR405; FY26 16.27 million pieces at INR420. Management expects H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10%.

segments.name: BTPL (Bombay Rayon, fabric)
segments.commentary: Merger initiated subject to NCLT approval, expected in Q3 FY27. Utilisation near 50 lakh meters/month against 70 lakh capacity, expandable to 100 lakh for INR50-60 crores capex. FY27 revenue guided above INR1,000 crores; EBITDA breakeven in H1 and about 6-7% in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Matrix and other Indian subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Had minor setbacks in Q4 as customers shifted business to other regions during the 50% tariff period; management expects reversal in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone Y-o-Y EBITDA margin improvement of a couple of percentage points, conditional on no new tariff disruption; H1 FY27 margins still absorb about 3% sharper pricing given on H1 orders.
Africa FY27 revenue target $115-120 million (worst case $115 million), with H2 FY27 Africa EBITDA margin of 8-10%.
Working capital to be reduced by INR75-100 crores in FY27 across Gokaldas and Atraco, excluding BTPL merger impact.
Medium-term (FY28 steady state, excluding new capacity drag): India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, India:Africa revenue split about 75:25 to 80:20; BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.
Management said FY27 revenue growth would be much more than 10-12% excluding U.K./EU FTA benefits, which are not factored in; it targets at least 15% growth.
Two new premium customers in India (one US, one European) and two in Africa (one US, one European) to contribute revenue from FY27, about 5% of revenue in year one.
capex_capacity: Africa capacity expansion completed in FY26; one factory running 2 shifts on 20-25% of its capacity, with a second-shift opportunity without major capex.

Karnataka (Kolar Gold Fields) half-factory ramp-up expected through Q1-Q2 FY27 to full utilisation; Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) 1,000-machine unit expected at full utilisation by Q3 FY27 (Sept-Oct), adding about INR175 crores revenue at full capacity; Karnataka adds about INR125 crores at steady state.
Two further planned factories (about INR300 crores steady-state revenue) with capex of INR80-100 crores over two years; decision expected in the next quarter or so, with revenue mainly FY28.
Total capacity to reach 104 million pieces including 12 million added (India about 7.5 million, Africa about 4.5 million); India 52 million and Africa 40 million pieces currently, per management.
BTPL: 70 lakh meters/month capacity, expandable to 100 lakh with INR50-60 crores capex; captive fabric consumption by Gokaldas about 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Reciprocal tariff of about 50% (including penal 25%) on India until mid-February 2026; penal tariff withdrawn, then a 10% tariff applied until July 24, 2026. Section 301 tariffs may reset to about 20% for rest of world from late July; Africa not under Section 301 probe (Kenya stays at 10%).
Tariff rebates given during the penal regime were up to about 15% of order value, partly clawed back from the supply chain; sharper pricing of about 3% continues in H1 FY27 and is removed in H2.
AGOA extended to December 2026; US administration reportedly moving to country-by-country deals; Kenya FTA not expected by end-2026.
US retail sales grew 8% and UK 6% in CY25; US retailers pared imports from H2 CY25. Spring 27 orders being booked; customers ordering conservatively.

Input cost inflation from Middle East war (polyester, packaging, fuel, trims, cotton); pass-through being attempted in H2 orders, with partial recovery expected given customer resistance and competitor under-utilisation in SE Asia and China.
Hedging: about 80% of revenue hedged for the next two quarters at INR87-91/USD; 50% for the following two. Rupee depreciation benefit not yet in numbers, expected in H2.
Labour cost inflation in India: Haryana announced 35% wage increase from April 1 and UP 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 12% standalone margin be sustained, and what is the Africa margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Africa H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10% and operating leverage in India; Matrix and other subsidiaries were hit by pivoted orders in Q4 and should recover in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital reduce in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a reduction of INR75-100 crores in Gokaldas and Atraco, with BTPL's working capital to be added on merger; the INR200 crore increase reflected inventory build for Q1 orders (Chinese holidays) and year-end receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to volumes if AGOA lapses again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it refused to share AGOA-related discounts last time and let volume fall; now it has a broader Africa customer base and can offer some AGOA-related support if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Were tariff refunds booked in Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff reversals were factored in; the Q4 gain came from volume-driven operating leverage and no tariff discounts after mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 margin outlook with BTPL included?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state FY28 India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Are the acquired entities meeting internal targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not in FY26 due to tariff disruption; management expects them to perform to plan in FY27.

risks_watch: Section 301 tariff reset from July 24, 2026 and whether India returns to about 20%.
AGOA expiry in December 2026 and timing of renewal; Kenya FTA uncertainty.
Cotton, polyester and fuel cost pass-through versus customer resistance in H2 FY27.
BTPL NCLT merger timing (Q3 FY27) and its loss-making run-rate (-4 to -5% EBITDA in Q4 FY26); integration working capital.
Labour cost inflation in North India (Haryana 35%, UP 25% wage increases).
Rupee hedges at INR87-91/USD could limit currency gains; debt rising with capex and net debt up INR395 crores.
Tax expense elevated at consolidated level because losses at overseas and new Indian subsidiaries get no tax credit.
532630|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the demand and margin recovery narrative, but cautious on H1 FY27 margins, tariff timing and AGOA renewal. Management repeatedly hedged FY28 and FY27 guidance with geopolitical caveats and declined to factor in pending FTAs.
key_quotes: So, overall, I don't see any problem from a demand standpoint.
It looks like the worst is behind us.
Africa is not under Section 301 investigation, giving further comfort.
Certainly, there is no rebate on top of it at all for the year.

rows.why: AGOA extended only to December 2026 and Section 301 may reset India to about 20% from late July; Africa FY26 revenue about $80 million, and management says it can offer AGOA-related support if needed.

532630|2026-06.headline: Gokaldas Q1 FY27: consolidated income up 21% YoY and EBITDA up 17%, with Africa up 45% and India up 16% amid a sector-wide 12% decline.
532630|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong, broad-based quarter, with consolidated income up 21% YoY and consolidated EBITDA up 17% (India EBITDA up 14%). India revenue grew 16% YoY against a 12% fall in Indian apparel exports, partly helped by the lower US tariff regime. Africa grew 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak prior-year base, but Africa EBITDA margin was about 8%, below normal. Cost pressures from wages (Haryana minimum wage up 35% from April 2026), fuel, chemicals, logistics and freight were significant, partly offset by overhead control and a weaker rupee. BTPL (fabric unit) remains loss-making at the operating level, with merger expected in Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Target: double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28

financial_highlights.metric: India wage cost increase in Q1
Other expenses cost hit (utilities and logistics)

financial_highlights.change: Mix-driven; management disputed the volume metric

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 14%, versus a 12% decline in Indian apparel exports. Matrix plus stand-alone India ASP cited at INR 613 with about 1.53 million pieces for the old Gurgaon units. Central India plants running at about 85% utilisation; South India plants full.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Revenue up 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak Q1 FY26 base. EBITDA margin about 8%, with management targeting double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Utilisation at 80-85%; FY27 visibility of USD 112-115 million against a USD 120 million target.

segments.name: BTPL (fabric unit)
segments.commentary: Running at 50-53 lakh meters per month, with Q1 turnover around INR 170 crore and operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%. Targets EBITDA break-even in H1, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Growth: management said 15%-plus growth is 'straightforward' and it should do better; mid-to-high-teens was floated by the analyst, with management not confirming a number. Q2 FY27 revenue expected to resemble Q1; Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked.
Africa FY27 revenue visibility of USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, with a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.
Africa EBITDA margin expected back to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.
ETR guided at 20-22% for FY27 as international operations contribute.
Wage, fuel and logistics cost pressure expected to partly ease in H2 if conditions improve; uncertainty remains. Pass-through pricing being applied to new orders.

Capex: about INR 80 crore mentioned in presentation; Jharkhand and Karnataka greenfield units total about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27), with steady-state revenue of about INR 350 crore from FY29. Bhopal second unit yields revenue from H2 FY27.
Potential 2,000-3,000 extra machines (about INR 200 crore revenue per 1,000 machines) to be decided within 3 months; larger spend in FY28.
capex_capacity: Bhopal second unit ramping up, expected to reach near full utilisation by Q4 FY27; adds about 3.5 million pieces and about INR 175-200 crore steady-state revenue.

Karnataka and Ranchi existing-factory machine additions (about 500-700 machines) are being commissioned in FY27; total of commissioned Bhopal Phase 2, Karnataka and Ranchi adds about INR 275 crore revenue potential.

New Jharkhand and Karnataka facilities: total investment about INR 100 crore, about 3.5 million pieces each, steady-state revenue about INR 350 crore combined; expected on stream H2 FY28, full potential FY29.
Africa: capacity already in place to deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue; second shift used for swing capacity; no significant Africa capex planned until existing options are exhausted.
BTPL capacity about 50 lakh meters per month, expected to grow about 30%; new customer onboarding with operations starting in Q2.
demand_pricing: US and UK end-consumer demand grew strongly through the first six months of CY26, though US growth slowed in June; EU and UK apparel imports declined through the first five months of FY27 per management.
US Section 301 tariff places India on par with competing sourcing countries, while China and Vietnam face 12.5%. India-UK FTA brings parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam in the UK.
Management says European buyers and US buyers are increasing inquiries and business towards India, extending beyond fashion and outerwear into shirts and bottoms; denim inquiries also rising.
Pricing: fabric cost pass-through is standard; some items (poly bags, cartons, fuel) were not priced into Q1 orders set in January and will be priced going forward.
Product mix: ASPs range from about USD 40-50 for high-value products to lower-value items; average realisation in India about INR 613 per piece for Gurgaon units.
UK is about 4-4.5% of total revenue; focus on larger UK players such as Marks & Spencer. Fibre mix about 65% cotton and up to 30% man-made (annual).

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth was only 3.4%, so where does India volume go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume is a misleading metric because Q1 and Q2 are high-value outerwear with 150-250 minutes of content per garment, versus about 22-25 minutes for a shirt; it added there is no YoY volume drop and growth is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Does the strong order book mean the mid-teens growth guide holds, or can growth be mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Spring '27 orders execute in Q3 FY27 and revenue traction for that period and beyond looks similar to Q1; 15%-plus growth was called 'straightforward' and it should do better.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa EBITDA margin recover to double digits from about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28, with H2 the differentiator; it cited AGOA expiring December with a 2-year extension passed by the Senate and awaiting the House and presidential assent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the visibility on shipping delays, and could they delay orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is the worst shipping environment; outbound FOB shipments can wait about 2 weeks for a vessel, and it expects easing over the next two quarters as the war and typhoon issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: How do India incentive cuts (RoSCTL) and the BTPL merger affect margins, and is the Africa margin base higher?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% and management's worst case is a halving to about 1.75%, which it expects to offset; BTPL should reach mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA after merger in Q3. Management said the EBITDA margin would be a bit higher than the analyst's base, and it sees the rupee weakness as a cushion (about 70% of dollars hedged at about INR 89).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 visibility, particularly for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 are booked; Q2 revenue should look like Q1. Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked now and the projection looks good despite US inflation concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Is India gaining share from China and Vietnam after the tariff change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2.5% advantage is not remarkable by itself, but European and US buyers are increasing inquiries for India across shirts, bottoms and denim, not just fashion and outerwear.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 35% minimum wage hike a larger hit, and how is it being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Haryana minimum wage rose 35% from April 2026 but overall wages for the Gurgaon/Manesar units rose only 14-15%; India wage cost increase in Q1 was about INR 20 crore, absorbed in the system. Karnataka increase was about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase and the ETR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose by about INR 5-6 crore on utilities, gas, fuel and chemicals plus inbound and outbound logistics, partly expected to ease in H2; FY27 ETR is guided at 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BTPL Q1 performance and the break-even timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: BTPL had about INR 170 crore fabric turnover in Q1 with operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%; management targets EBITDA break-even in H1 (Q2), EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity plan, including Jharkhand, Karnataka and Bhopal?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharkhand and Karnataka together need about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27) for about INR 350 crore steady-state revenue, coming on stream H2 FY28; Bhopal Phase 2 adds about 3.5 million pieces and INR 175-200 crore revenue. Management also said it may add 2,000-3,000 machines with a decision within 3 months and larger spend in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Africa plan require more capex, and what is the Africa capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant Africa capex is planned until second-shift options are exhausted; capacity in place can deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue. FY27 visibility is USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indian business share, utilisation and product-wise breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Central India plants run about 85% utilisation and South India plants are full; Africa is at 80-85%. Management gave the old Gurgaon units at 1.53 million pieces at INR 613 ASP, while Matrix alone was about 1.5 million pieces at INR 613.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric mix and UK exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton is about 65% or a little higher and man-made fibres up to 30%, on an annual basis per management. UK is about 4-4.5% of revenue, with focus on larger players such as Marks & Spencer.

risks_watch: Africa EBITDA margin (about 8% in Q1) must recover to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28; AGOA expires December 2026 and the extension is still awaiting House and presidential approval.
Shipping and logistics: container shortages, Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, and typhoon-related sailing delays; FOB outbound goods can sit about 2 weeks before boarding.
Wage and cost inflation: Haryana minimum wage up 35%, RoSCTL at about 3.5% with a possible halving to 1.75%, plus fuel, chemicals and poly bag/carton costs not priced into Q1 orders.
BTPL execution: operational EBITDA about -7.5% to -8% in Q1; break-even in Q2, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.
India volume metric disputed (3.4% per analyst), with growth attributed to mix; Q2 revenue expected to be similar to Q1, and Q3/Q4 orders still being booked.

So we can't put an estimate to it.

532633|2026-03.headline: Alldigi Tech FY26 revenue rose 9.6% to INR598.7 crore and EBITDA 25% to INR162 crore, with management guiding to mid-teens revenue growth in FY27.
532633|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR154.7 crore (+5.9% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR43.7 crore (+24.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin for FY26 at 27.1% versus 23.7% in FY25. Tech & Digital (T&D) was the growth engine at +22.3% YoY in Q4, while BPM was flat YoY at INR110.4 crore as management deliberately exited low-margin domestic FTE business. Management said about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin BPM business, and guided to mid-teens revenue growth and a 1-2% margin improvement for FY27. Q4 PAT rose 49.7% YoY to INR28.9 crore, and FY26 PAT was flat at INR82.2 crore. This was the first call with new CEO Natarajan Laxsmanan, who joined about a month earlier.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR44.3 crore (+22.3% YoY, +14.5% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR156.2 crore (+16.5%). Q4 segment margin INR19.5 crore (44%); FY26 segment margin INR66.6 crore (+28.9%). Processed 49.9 lakh employee records in Q4 and 191.5 lakh in FY26; added INR40.1 crore new ACV.

segments.name: BPM (CXM)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR110.4 crore (+0.4% YoY, flat); FY26 revenue INR442.4 crore (+7.3%). Q4 segment margin INR15 crore (about 13.6%); FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore (+16.8%). International share of BPM revenue 78% in FY26 (73% prior year). Added INR54.1 crore new ACV; international BPM revenue grew 8.7% YoY in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens, per the CEO, similar to the aspiration stated for FY26.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 1-2% in FY27 (management said 1-1.5% annual margin growth is typical), but no absolute margin number was given.
BPM segment margin expected to hold around 13-14%; the Q4 QoQ dip was a one-off linked to a leave policy alignment with the holding company.
T&D growth expected to be slightly higher than BPM growth; international mix expected to keep rising.
Depreciation for FY27 expected to rise only modestly (management said a couple of crore from the new Chennai office), with a sub-10% increase implied on the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.
Management expects no significant negative currency impact on revenue; a weaker rupee is expected to add to margin.
FY27 existing-customer headcount expected to be flat, with no major positive growth in employee records anticipated.
capex_capacity: Office upgrade underway in Chennai (new office being built) and Noida, with about INR20 crore of investment for the Chennai facility.
Admin and facility capex typically runs INR20-25 crore a year.
Current depreciation run-rate is about INR58.6 crore; management expects only a small increase beyond the new office.
SP4 platform migration completed for India-based customers, targeted at about INR3 crore a year in efficiency gains for T&D.
HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) to be released in FY27; PulseHR.ai to automate inbound query handling and cut turnaround time.
demand_pricing: HRO international order book was about 48% of total order book as of March 31, 2026 (no comparable domestic figure given).
T&D ACV wins have consistently been more than 60% from international clients.
Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place, but timing is uncertain: client decisions were on hold due to macro conditions and the war, impacting healthcare clients.
RCM (revenue cycle management) entry: processing began about a quarter ago and has doubled in FTE; further expansion with the same client is in progress.
FY27 BPM focus verticals: healthcare and RCM, international insurance, and international collections.
Existing T&D customers have plateaued; about 90% of FY26 record growth came from new customers.
Deal closure: about 30% of deals closed at CHRO/CFO level; smaller deals (under 1,000 employees) close at HR level; CEO involvement is rare.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HRO revenue grow faster than payroll-process volumes, and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is not directly proportional to employee numbers because of one-time change requests, year-end tax work, new wage code implementation, and currency benefits from international business. Higher revenue than headcount growth is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 growth was constant currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and 6.3% from company efforts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BPM headcount decline continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exit from low-margin business will continue through FY27; about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue CAGR below the mid-teens target, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the strategic exit from low-margin business and industry factors. It still sees mid-teens growth for FY27, which it said is slightly above industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a new large BPM client and how will margins change after the exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline, citing a large pipeline and deals delayed by macro conditions. It said the low-margin exit will have minimal impact because it is only about 10% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment margins (about INR129 crore) differ from reported EBITDA (INR162 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said segment margins are reported at PBT level after depreciation and finance costs, net of unallocable items, other income and expenses. He offered to reconcile offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company win deals and what is the sales structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price, scale, platform flexibility, operational accuracy and turnaround time. International sales are now run by geography-specific teams with rainmaker and technology partners.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and depreciation outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain guided to admin/facility capex of INR20-25 crore a year plus about INR20 crore for the Chennai office, with only a small rise in depreciation from the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.

risks_watch: BPM growth depends on landing one or two large clients; none was onboarded in the last about 12 months, and timing is not guided.
Continued headcount decline in BPM as low-margin exits proceed; about 10% of the portfolio remains low-margin.
Flat existing-customer headcount; no major positive growth in employee records expected for FY27, so growth relies on new clients and one-time revenue.
Currency tailwind contributed about 3.3% of FY26 growth; management declined to comment on future FX effects.
AI could cut client headcounts; management called this both a challenge and an opportunity.
Segment margin reconciliation to EBITDA was not clear on the call; Vaibhav Chechani's query was left for an offline discussion.
Q4 FY26 BPM margin dip was attributed to a one-off leave policy alignment with the holding company, which is yet to be quantified.
532633|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on T&D momentum, margins and the FY27 mid-teens growth target. Cautious and vague on BPM large-client timing, which management declined to pin to a timeline, and avoided giving absolute margin numbers.
key_quotes: And the good news is it has scaled up. It's doubled up now.
So, while there is one way of looking at it as a risk, it's also an opportunity for us.
We should -- it's -- I'm not giving you a time line, but I can give you an insight in terms of our pipeline.
So we're not anticipating any negative growth. But at the same time, we're not anticipating any major positive growth also for this year in terms of employee records.

rows.why: Management guided a 1-2% EBITDA margin improvement from the FY26 base of 27.1% (versus 23.7% in FY25), backed by SP4 platform savings of about INR3 crore a year and a weaker rupee, though BPM margin is guided to hold at 13-14%.

rows.why: Capex is held at admin and facility spend of INR20-25 crore a year plus the Chennai office, with utilisation not disclosed and no new plant, land or board-level expansion plan mentioned.

rows.why: Management held the mid-teens FY27 revenue guide and gave no absolute margin figure, with existing T&D customers plateauing and no large BPM client onboarded in about 12 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) is set for release in FY27, and the RCM service line has already begun processing with FTE doubling in a quarter.

rows.label: Large BPM client onboarding (healthcare / RCM, international insurance)
rows.why: Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place but no large client was onboarded in about 12 months and decisions are on hold, so the timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Currency tailwind and HRO revenue outpacing headcount
rows.why: 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and management expects a weaker rupee to add to margin, though it declined to comment on future FX effects.

rows.label: BPM low-margin exit continuing through FY27
rows.why: About 10% of the portfolio remains low-margin and the domestic FTE exit continues, which will lower BPM headcount while lifting mix (BPM FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore, +16.8%).

tone.note: Management was confident on T&D momentum (+22.3% YoY in Q4), the mid-teens FY27 revenue target and a 1-2% margin gain, but was vague on BPM large-client timing and gave no absolute margin figure; analysts pushed on the segment-to-EBITDA reconciliation, which was deferred offline.

532633|2026-09.headline: Alldigi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4% YoY to INR153.3 crore, while EBITDA grew about 29% to INR46.3 crore at a 30.2% margin.
532633|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR153.3 crore (+4% YoY, +2% QoQ), with H1 revenue at INR303.6 crore (+4.2%). Profitability grew much faster than revenue: Q2 EBITDA rose about 29% YoY to INR46.3 crore and PAT rose about 51% YoY to INR26.6 crore. Growth was held back by a deliberate reduction in low-margin domestic BPM, which fell 33% YoY in Q2, while international revenue rose 15.1% and now makes up about 70% of revenue. Management also announced a buyback of up to 4.8 lakh shares at INR1,000 per share (about INR48 crore), and new-business ACV for H1 more than doubled to INR82.6 crore.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR111.6 crore (+1% YoY, +1.8% QoQ); H1 INR221.3 crore (+1.4%). International BPM grew 12.6% YoY in Q2 and is about 83% of BPM revenue (75% a year ago), while domestic BPM fell 33% YoY.

segments.name: BPM segment margin
segments.commentary: Q2 segment profit INR17.5 crore at 15.6% (11.6% a year ago, 11.9% in Q1); H1 INR30.6 crore at about 13.8%.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crore (+12.9% YoY, +2.7% QoQ); H1 INR82.3 crore (+12.4%). Employee records processed were 51.1 lakh in Q2 (+7.2% YoY) and 101.3 lakh in H1.

segments.name: T&D segment margin
segments.commentary: Q2 segment profit INR18.3 crore at 43.9%; H1 INR35.7 crore at about 43.4%, helped by higher volumes and international mix.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the employee cost-to-revenue ratio to keep falling, with headcount reduction continuing; full effect of Q2 headcount reduction (started mid-Q2) expected in Q3.
BPM margin is expected to keep improving as domestic BPM is run down, but management gave no quantum; the domestic exit continues only where clients remain profitable.
Management declined to give revenue guidance for the next few quarters. BPM deals are expected to ramp in about 3-4 months; T&D ramp takes longer, possibly 2-4 quarters.
T&D guided to early double-digit growth over the next three years.
Lease payments expected to stay in the same range as FY26 (about INR35 crore base), potentially lower with resource optimisation.
Buyback of up to 4.8 lakh equity shares at INR1,000 per share (about INR48 crore), subject to approvals. Dividend policy is cited as consistent with the buyback.
capex_capacity: New BOT (build-operate-transfer) captive service started with one client: over 1,000 FTEs now, with the client targeting 2-3x growth; a separate BOT deal is valued at about INR16.8 crore on a contract of about 2 quarters, with potential to reach 3,000-4,000 FTEs.
Manila operations were significantly optimised; management called Manila a high-cost location.
Office was replaced with a new one on a longer lease commitment, raising ROU assets from roughly INR50-60 crore to about INR140-150 crore.

Products launched: Buzzily 2.0 (May 2026); Alldigi 360 (HCM suite incl. payroll, SaaS or technology-only) and Alldigi 360 Analytics (AI analytics, standalone or on top of existing HRIS) in October 2026.
demand_pricing: Q2 new business ACV INR37.2 crore: one Europe T&D deal of about INR7 crore (multi-year, auto-renewing, about 60%+ gross margin) and one BPM BOT deal of about INR16.8 crore.

Payroll pricing is under pressure: management said clients expect gain-share on efficiencies, so per-transaction prices tend to fall over time, while growth is sought through cross-selling HCM, SaaS and analytics.
Workday Silver certification held; design batch to finish mid-November 2026. Management sees about 4 clients in the pipeline for Workday connector implementations.
TaxSpanner partnership live since last year; management expects a bigger push this year, with more than 10-12 lakh employee records in India as the addressable base, but gave no revenue guidance.
Sales organisation rebuilt: new CBO for BPM, BPM-background leaders for US sales, SMB and enterprise sales teams in T&D, and a Southeast Asia BPM sales effort that has produced early Q2 ACV wins.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about INR5 crore (about 7%) QoQ while headcount fell less?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower replacement costs from tighter hiring rates, Manila optimisation (a high-cost location), and a retiral-benefit true-up. The full headcount reduction, which began mid-Q2, will show in Q3, and the employee cost-to-revenue ratio should keep falling.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic BPM rationalisation complete?
qa_highlights.answer: It is ongoing. Management decided to exit some large client relationships and will not add new domestic clients, but will keep profitable existing ones, so the domestic book shrinks continuously rather than being fully exited.

qa_highlights.question: How far can payroll price erosion go, and how much revenue per employee can be extracted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price points fall as efficiencies are shared with clients through gain-share, but premium services hold price. The focus is on selling additional HCM, SaaS and analytics services rather than defending transaction prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and timing prospects for the new ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide quarterly revenue. BPM ramp-up is about 3-4 months from go-live, while T&D takes longer, possibly 2-4 quarters, depending on client implementation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR69 crore to about INR80 crore while DSO fell from 77 to 74 days?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said receivables are billed plus unbilled, and the rise reflects unbilled balances being converted into bills after project milestones, along with business acceleration. DSO is expected to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: How does the segment profit total of INR35.8 crore reconcile with reported EBITDA of about INR46 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said segment profit is measured before finance costs, depreciation and unallocated costs, so it is not comparable with EBITDA and no clean bridge was given.

risks_watch: Revenue growth remains low at about 4%, with domestic BPM still declining, so the margin story depends on international ramp-ups converting to revenue.
Q2 receivables rose and standalone receivables were up about 46% in six months; management attributes this to timing, so DSO and unbilled balances need tracking.
Payroll price erosion through gain-share, which is structural per management's own answer.
Cash fell to INR127.2 crore after the dividend; the buyback (about INR48 crore) will reduce it further.
Execution risk on BOT and large deal ramp-ups (1,000 FTEs now, targeted 3,000-4,000) and on T&D implementation timelines.
Workday certification and NPS integration are at an early stage with no revenue quantified.

Management declined to give quarterly revenue guidance and gave no quantum for BPM margin uplift; NPS and Workday revenue are described as too early to quantify. The receivables answers were defensive and attributed the increase to timing and unbilled-to-billed conversion.

532636|2026-03.headline: IIFL Finance Q4 FY26: consolidated PAT of INR623 crore (up 24% QoQ) and loan AUM of INR1,08,180 crore (up 38% YoY), with gold AUM up 150% YoY to INR52,581 crore.
532636|2026-03.overview: Management reported consolidated PAT before minority interest of INR623 crore, up 24% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit of INR1,173 crore, up 80% YoY and 9% QoQ. Loan AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, growing 10% QoQ, with gold the primary growth engine at 62 tonnes of tonnage. Asset quality improved, with GNPA about 1.5% and NNPA 0.7%, while the housing finance arm stayed flat and weak on profitability. Management guided to FY27 AUM growth of 20-25% for gold, 18-20% for housing, a credit cost fall to 1.5-1.7%, and a 100-120 bp cost-of-funds reduction on a rating upgrade. The income tax special audit outcome remained pending, with management expecting orders within days and saying it would appeal any demand.

financial_highlights.metric: Core loan AUM (home, gold, MSME, microfinance)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA down 77 bp YoY, NNPA down 32 bp YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Ind AS provision coverage on NPAs

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR52,581 crore, up 150% YoY and 11% QoQ on 62 tonnes tonnage; management guides 20-25% AUM growth in FY27 if gold prices stay at current levels, and says the new RBI gold rules are fully complied with.

segments.name: Housing finance (IIFL Home Finance)
segments.commentary: AUM was flat QoQ with subdued profitability, partly due to stress in the legacy micro-LAP book (since exited); FY27 guidance is 18-20% AUM/book growth and 25-27% disbursement growth, with yield at about 12%+ on new affordable business versus about 10.55% blended.

segments.name: Microfinance (Samasta)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency is recovering and asset quality is stabilising; management is growing cautiously, targeting about 20% growth with average microfinance ticket of about INR68,000 and micro-LAP ticket of about INR4.8 lakh, and aims to return to AUM levels of March 2024.

segments.name: Off-book (DA and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Off-book share is 34-36% of AUM, with a target of 40-45%; co-lending book is INR14,384 crore, targeted to grow about 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated AUM growth of about 20-25% if gold prices stay at current levels (gold business guided at 20-25%).
FY27 credit cost guided at about 1.5-1.7%, down 120-130 bp from the FY26 guidance of 2.7-3%; management expects ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%, depending on growth.
Housing finance guided to 18-20% AUM/book growth and 25-27% disbursement growth in FY27, with about 100 new branches planned in phases.
Off-book (DA + co-lending) to rise to 40-45% of AUM from 34-36%; co-lending to grow about 20%.
Comfortable leverage up to about 4.5x; management said capital could be raised through debt periodically and equity when the time is right.
A credit rating upgrade from AA (stable) to AA+ could lower cost of funds by 100-120 bp.
capex_capacity: Gold branch expansion: RBI freed branch expansion; management plans to add branches this year, but 'not aggressively'.
Housing finance: about 315 branches (94 emerging, 221 affordable), with about 100 new branches planned this year in phases.
Leverage: net gearing about 3.8x at consolidated level; management says up to 4.5x is comfortable, with the regulatory maximum at about 6-7x depending on capital adequacy.
Liquidity: INR28,165 crore raised during the year plus INR7,046 crore via direct assignments; cash and equivalents including committed lines INR6,638 crore.
demand_pricing: Gold: management said loan demand is independent of gold prices, so tonnage can move sequentially even with AUM growth; Q3 tonnage growth was stronger than Q4.

Housing: prime segment exited on margin grounds; focus on affordable and emerging, where management says 7-8 large players operate and about 80 smaller players have small books. Management said PMAY 2 subsidy with a 5-year lock-in should cut borrower attrition.
Housing competition: management cited Bajaj Housing and PNB Housing entering affordable and near-prime ticket sizes of INR15-25 lakh and said IIFL does not see a challenge to growing its book.
Interest rates: management said money-market rates spiked in March and early April on war-related liquidity tightness, and are now normalising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax special audit and the likely impact (rumoured INR300-400 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on speculative reports. The special audit (mainly gold loans) is complete and the assessment order is expected within days or about a week; the company will appeal any demand and does not expect a material adverse outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a demerger of IIFL Home Finance and Samasta?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an option to demerge into three entities (for ADIA's exit from home finance), but this is a Board decision with no timeline and no active process.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 credit cost and ROA expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is guided to 1.5-1.7% (against 2.7-3% in FY26) and ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%. Credit cost applies only to the on-balance-sheet book (about 10-20% of AUM), not to assigned loans.

qa_highlights.question: How will IIFL adapt to new gold-loan rules (cash-flow assessment for loans above INR2.5 lakh) and branch expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Detailed credit assessment is in place for all loans above INR2.5 lakh and the branch model already does cash-flow assessment. Gold AUM growth is guided at 20-25%, with more branches in underserved areas.

qa_highlights.question: What are the leverage and capital plans, and is equity needed for 20%+ growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can grow without equity if co-lending and DA reach 40-45%; it is comfortable with leverage up to 4.5x and will raise debt periodically and equity when the time is right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was housing AUM muted in FY26, and why are home finance ROE and ROA weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the exit of micro-LAP (overlapping with MFI borrowers) and reduced leverage after an equity raise 2-3 years ago. Growth is expected to lift ROE back toward double digits, and LAP is being focused on at about 18% of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rating upgrade roadmap and its impact on cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, GNPA is 1.5%, and profitability is improving; the remaining gap is capital adequacy, which needs more off-book growth or equity. A move to AA+ could cut funding cost by 100-120 bp, but management would not quantify the rating-upgrade impact.

risks_watch: Outcome and quantum of the income tax special audit and assessment orders for IIFL Finance and group entities; management expects appeals.

New RBI gold-loan norms (cash-flow assessment above INR2.5 lakh) and rising competition from new NBFC entrants and branch expansion.

Capital adequacy as leverage rises; off-book (DA and co-lending) must reach 40-45% or equity raised; rating upgrade depends on capital, not only on asset quality.

532648|2026-03.headline: YES Bank Q4 FY26 net profit rose 44.7% YoY to INR 1,068 crore, with ROA of 1.0% and GNPA at a record-low 1.3%.
532648|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered 44.7% YoY net profit growth to INR 1,068 crore and a 1.0% ROA, in line with guidance. NIM rose 10 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY to 2.7%, helped by RIDF and mandated-deposit rundown and CASA outperformance. Asset quality improved sharply, with GNPA at 1.3% and NNPA at 0.2%, while INR 341 crore of one-time standard-asset provisioning was taken in Q4. Advances grew 11.1% YoY to INR 2.73 lakh crore, with management signalling faster momentum and FY27 growth targeted at 13-15%.

segments.name: Corporate and Commercial Banking
segments.commentary: Corporate book growing ~20% and Commercial Banking ~18%, per management. Commercial Banking is described as a preferred growth area.

segments.name: Deposits

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth targeted at 13-15%, in line with or above industry; management said the book should grow in double digits.
RIDF and mandated deposits to fall from ~6% of total assets to below 5% by FY27. RIDF rundown in FY27 is at least INR 6,500 crore and could reach INR 9,000 crore from ~INR 28,000 crore at FY26 end.
Target ROA of 1% exit rate maintained; internal aim to add 25-50 bps of core ROA improvement over 2-3 years, excluding JC Flowers ARC write-backs.
Structural NIM target of 3.25-3.5% over 2-3 years; no near-term NIM guidance given.
SR recoveries of INR 800-1,000 crore expected in FY27; about INR 1,500 crore face value of SRs remains to be redeemed over the next few quarters.
Branch expansion of ~80 per year, about 400 over 4-5 years; 82 branches opened in FY26.
capex_capacity: 82 new branches opened in FY26, in line with guidance; plan of ~400 branches over 4-5 years (~80 per year).

Management aims to invest across people, product, processes and technology; new rule engines and platform to support unsecured lending.

demand_pricing: Average deposit repricing front-loaded in April 2025; savings account rate cut by over 150 bps over the year to well below 4.5%, with another rate action in April 2026.
Yield on advances at March 2026 exit about 9.2%.
Management said it expects some mix compression as Retail grows slower than Corporate and Commercial, but mix to stabilise.
Management said MSME and larger clients are managing well with no signs of stress despite West Asia conflict; monitoring continues.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 15%+ next year, and how will CASA grow in line with loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 CA and SA each grew ~4% QoQ on average balances; CASA ~11% YoY on average. FY27 growth is guided at 13-15%, with sequential momentum accelerating from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift between Retail, Wholesale and Commercial after the SMBC induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail disbursements are above 20% YoY and normalising at 20-25%; Retail book growth expected at 10-11% in FY27. Corporate is growing ~20%, and mix is expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: How did the bond yield spike affect treasury and AFS reserves?
qa_highlights.answer: The trading book is small. AFS reserve is about negative INR 100 crore at March 31, with a swing of ~INR 200 crore. Most of the SLR book sits in HTM, and CET-1 absorbed ~10 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 340 crore one-time standard-asset provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 341 crore of provisioning was taken in Q4 under evolving and prudent policies, not linked to any credit issue. It was funded by SR recoveries of ~INR 450 crore and a INR 288 crore write-back from one corporate account.

qa_highlights.question: What is the next ROA milestone, and how sustainable is 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank exited FY26 at 1% ROA. Internal aim is 25-50 bps core ROA improvement, with some JC Flowers ARC write-backs still to come in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were credit card and personal loan slippages in INR crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card slippage was about INR 133-140 crore and personal loan slippage about INR 160-180 crore; the figures were corrected during the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion and branch share of disbursals change?
qa_highlights.answer: The plan is about 80 branches a year, aligned to deposit growth, credit growth and credit quality in each pin code. Branches supply ~60% of the ~50% of disbursals sourced internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff profile beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 and FY29 will see equal reductions, similar to FY27, with thinner runoff in FY29-FY30 as maturities taper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT1 case status?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter is sub judice, with Supreme Court hearings complete and judgment reserved. Management declined to comment on the likely outcome.

risks_watch: Pace of RIDF and mandated-deposit runoff, which drives the margin tailwind; FY27 runoff of INR 6,500-9,000 crore.

AT1 bond Supreme Court judgment, with a potential impact on the balance sheet; the outcome is unquantified.
Second-order effects of the West Asia conflict and rising G-sec yields on MSME credit and the HTM book.

532648|2026-06.headline: YES Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crore, with NII up 17.5% and cost-to-income down to 62.8%.
532648|2026-06.overview: Net profit grew 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crore and operating profit rose 25.5% to INR 1,704 crore, even with lower Security Receipts gains (INR 86 crore vs INR 338 crore) and lower treasury income. Reported gross slippages fell to 1.4% from 1.6% QoQ and 2.4% YoY, with retail slippages at a 10-quarter low. Advances grew 18.3% YoY to INR 2.85 lakh crore, with management stating underlying average-balance growth of 15-16%. Management reiterated its aim of a full-year ROA around 1% and a NIM above 3% over the next two years, and a board enabling resolution for capital raising was flagged.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Grew strongly in advances; management said part of the growth is transitional and shorter-tenure in nature.

segments.name: Commercial Banking (largely MSME)
segments.commentary: Advances grew 17% YoY; management said the portfolio quality remains high with controlled Q1 slippages.

segments.name: Retail Banking
segments.commentary: Advances grew only 6.9% YoY, but retail disbursements grew 27.5% YoY; retail slippages were at a 10-quarter low.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 ROA: aspiration around 1%; management expects core ROA to expand 15-20 bps in FY27, with the reported 1% ROA dependent on resolutions and bond/trading gains.
NIM: near-term aim of 3%+ over the next 2 years; management later said north of 3% is achievable in FY28, with expansion described as a steady climb rather than quarter-to-quarter.
Advances growth targeted at 15-17%, a little above industry; underlying average-balance loan growth of 15-16%.
SR recoveries: guidance of INR 800-1,000 crore for FY27 maintained, dependent on J.C. Flower's execution.
Capital: 14% CET-1 seen as sufficient for about the next 4 quarters of growth; enabling approval for capital raise remains in place until the AGM. Future raise would be targeted in the 13% handle.
Retail: management expects double-digit retail book growth in about 3-4 quarters; mid-teens loan growth is the stated goal.

qa_highlights.question: What net advances target do you have for the year, and is the board capital-raise resolution a signal of need?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances growth is targeted at about 15-17%, a little above industry. Capital resolution is an enabler to stay ready; 3-4 quarters of growth cushion is available for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the FCNR(B) deposit and leverage product progressing and what constrains it?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is strong and leverage limits are being filled, capped at 9x for now. Pace is slowed by higher overseas borrowing spreads and uneven global liquidity; limits are being set up with international banks including SMBC.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins improve and what is the FY28 view?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are runoff of low-yield RIDF and priority-sector deposits, deposit repricing and CASA mix. Management said north of 3% NIM is achievable in FY28, with a steady climb rather than quarter-to-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SR recoveries fall QoQ and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 SR redemption was INR 86 crore versus about INR 450 crore in Q4. SR face value outstanding is INR 1,500 crore with NAV above INR 2,000 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 800-1,000 crore is maintained but depends on J.C. Flower execution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital-raise timeline and does the AT1 court case link to it?
qa_highlights.answer: The approval is an annual enabling resolution, valid till the AGM and not tied to the court case. CET-1 of 14% is seen as enough for about 4 quarters; any raise would target the 13% handle. No provision has been made for the court case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail growth plan and how will disbursements translate into book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail book is flat to 7% growth due to run-off; disbursements grow 25-30% and book growth should follow in about 3-4 quarters. Secured mix of about 75% is the guardrail, with LAP, personal loans and franchise products.

qa_highlights.question: Did MSME slippages rise and is there West Asia war exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Commercial Banking slippages were controlled in Q1, with limited impact from the West Asia conflict and portfolio quality remaining high.

532648|2026-09.headline: Yes Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 65% YoY to INR 1,080 crore, but a Supreme Court ruling reinstating INR 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds cuts pro forma CET-1 to about 11.4%.
532648|2026-09.overview: Net profit was INR 1,080 crore (up 65% YoY) with operating profit up 29.4% to INR 1,678 crore and NII up 22.7% to INR 2,822 crore. The quarter was dominated by the Supreme Court's 15 October 2026 judgment upholding the Bombay High Court's setting aside of the March 2020 AT-1 write-down of INR 8,415 crore. Management said the indicative pro forma impact is about 240 bps on CET-1 (including profits), taking CET-1 to about 11.4% and overall Tier 1 to about 13.7%. NIM fell 12-14 bps QoQ to 2.6%, attributed mainly to FCNR(B) mobilisation that was not yet deployed, and management guided to a stable Q3 and a positive bias in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: vs 0.6% in Q2 FY26 and 0.9% in Q1 FY27

segments.commentary: Advances grew 20.2% YoY.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Advances grew 31.4% YoY. An analyst noted CIB was flat QoQ, and management said FCNR-linked funds would be deployed mainly in Q3 with some spill into Q4.

Q4 FY27 NIM expected to show a positive bias. A 25 bps repo hike (October) is expected to add a high single-digit bps margin benefit in Q4, subject to market forces.
RIDF balances to fall by about INR 8,000 crore in H2 FY27: about INR 4,500 crore in Q3 and INR 3,500 crore in Q4.

FY27 ROA target of 1% for the full year is reiterated but relies partly on non-core items (Security Receipts). Management is confident of 1% ROA in FY28 with less reliance on non-core income, to be firmed up at FY27 end.
ECL transition: opening-balance-sheet CET-1 impact of about 50-60 bps, which management expects to be largely offset by the new credit risk circular, so not a material hit.

Growth can be sustained without a capital raise: management said ROE accretion and the DTA benefit allow about 11% growth without consuming capital, and 15% RWA growth would consume about 30-40 bps of CET-1. Capital actions are under evaluation, with no timing given.

Mobilised INR 18,575 crore of FCNR(B) deposits and extended INR 15,215 crore of foreign currency term loans through the GIFT City IBU.

Security Receipts: face value about INR 1,500 crore (transcript says 15 billion), NAV about INR 2,000 crore, zero carrying value. Management cited this as a potential capital lever, without committing to action.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT-1 accounting and cash impact if the write-down is reversed, and is the coupon payable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reinstatement is in substance a balance sheet reclassification from reserves to Tier 1 borrowings, with no cash outflow on principal. The timing and manner of reinstatement and any coupon payment are still under assessment, and coupons will follow the information memoranda.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM sensitivity to repo changes, and how should Q3 and Q4 margins be framed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% of the book is floating (repo or T-bill). A 25 bps repo increase could lift margins by a high single-digit bps, subject to market forces. Q3 should be similar to Q2, and Q4 should see a positive bias from repricing, RIDF runoff and FCNR deployment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff plan, and is there quantitative NIM guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 RIDF reduction is about INR 8,000 crore: INR 4,500 crore in Q3 and INR 3,500 crore in Q4. Management asked that the benefit be baked into the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 ROA exceed 1%, and how much capital can growth absorb without a raise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of 1% ROA in FY28 with less reliance on non-core items, and said 11% growth is possible without consuming capital given DTA and ROE accretion. Growth at 15% would burn about 30-40 bps of CET-1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank raise capital, and what is the rating agency view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a pro forma CET-1 of 11.4% leaves headroom, but 11-11.5% is not ideal, so capital actions will be assessed. Agencies have called it a credit-neutral event, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CD issuance rise, and what is the ECL impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CD issuance was tactical, driven by the rating upgrade to above AA (long term), with LCR and NSFR considerations. ECL transition is expected at 50-60 bps of opening CET-1, largely offset by the new credit risk circular.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 2.6% (down 12-14 bps QoQ) with Q3 guided flat, and Q4 guided to a positive bias from a 25 bps repo hike (high single-digit bps benefit), RIDF runoff of about INR 8,000 crore, and FCNR deployment, with about 65% of the book floating.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 23.7% YoY (17.6% ex-FCTL), deposits 19.5% YoY and retail disbursements 35% YoY, with management saying about 11% growth is possible without consuming capital and 15% RWA growth costs 30-40 bps of CET-1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Pro forma CET-1 falls to about 11.4% after a roughly 240 bps AT-1 hit, and management called 11-11.5% not ideal, so capital actions are under evaluation with no timing; this is a capital raise rather than capex, and the brief gives no plant or branch numbers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 ROA of 1% is reiterated with H1 at 90 bps, and management is confident of 1% ROA in FY28 with less reliance on non-core income, to be firmed up at FY27 end.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 NIM may be flat to slightly negative from the full-quarter FCNR effect, and FY27 ROA of 1% partly relies on Security Receipts non-core gains (INR 395 crore recognised in Q2).

rows.label: AT-1 bond reinstatement and possible capital raise
rows.why: The Supreme Court upheld reinstatement of INR 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds, cutting pro forma CET-1 about 240 bps to 11.4%, and management is assessing capital actions with no timing given; the timing of reinstatement and coupon payments is still under assessment.

rows.label: RIDF runoff of about INR 8,000 crore in H2 FY27
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (INR 4,500 crore) and Q4 FY27 (INR 3,500 crore)
rows.why: Management has given a firm schedule for the RIDF reduction, and it is expected to add to Q4 NIM as the benefit is baked into the following quarter.

rows.label: ECL transition CET-1 hit offset
rows.why: Opening-balance-sheet CET-1 impact of about 50-60 bps is expected to be largely offset by the new credit risk circular, though details are still being firmed up.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating metrics, growth, NIM direction and ROA, but cautious and non-committal on the AT-1 reinstatement, coupons, capital actions and legal options; analysts probed the CET-1 headroom and the Q3 NIM path.

532652|2026-03.headline: Karnataka Bank Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40% QoQ to INR408.19 crore; FY26 PAT record INR1,310.50 crore, GNPA down to 2.78%.
532652|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp sequential improvement: NIM rose to 3.07% from 2.92%, cost-to-income fell to 50.47% from 58.72%, and GNPA fell 54 bps QoQ to 2.78%. Business reached INR192,118 crore with gross advances up 8% QoQ to INR83,340 crore, and CASA rose to 33.61%. Management said FY26 guidance was met on most metrics, but advances (INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000–85,000 crore guidance) fell short. Much of the Q4 earnings lift came from lower employee cost, higher fee and technical write-off recovery income, and accelerated provisioning, which analysts questioned on sustainability.

segments.name: Mid-corporate
segments.commentary: Mid-corporate advances grew about 13% QoQ in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: IBPC and food credit book
segments.commentary: Brought down to INR1,707 crore at 31 March 2026 from INR4,057 crore at 31 March 2025; about INR2,350 crore replaced in FY26 with higher-yielding loans.

segments.commentary: Aggregate deposits INR108,779 crore (+4% QoQ). Retail term deposits INR67,648 crore (+2% QoQ, +5% YoY). Bulk deposits fell to 4.2% of total deposits from 4.8%.

guidance_outlook: Business growth around 15%; deposit growth 10% to 15%; advances growth 15% to 20% for FY27.
CASA to be maintained at 33% plus; CD ratio around 80%.
ROA to remain 1% plus, with management saying improvement is expected.
Cost-to-income to be 52% to 53% going forward, from 50.47% in Q4 and 56.34% in FY26.
PCR to rise about 1% every quarter; Q4 rise was larger than that.
Management said NIM margin floor has been reached ("I feel it has bottomed out"), with ongoing focus on 3% plus NIM; NIM had fallen to as low as 2.72% in earlier data.
Business growth phasing: H1 about 39% and H2 about 61% of annual growth; management also cited a monthly target path.
ECL transition impact estimated at 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over about 4 to 5 years (roughly 25 to 30 bps of credit cost per year).
Management targets recovering 50% of NPA and technical write-off books; called it ambitious and gave no figure.

FY27 product launches: tobacco agri input loans, programmable CBDC, NFC-based QR/Tap and Pay, surrogate-based housing lending, MSME dropline OD and LAP; major IT solutions due in FY27 include loan origination revamp, HRMS, treasury and BHIM 3.0.
capex_capacity: Around 31 branches opened in FY26; management said branch expansion plans may be revised in view of West Asia-related uncertainty.
Employee count fell in Q4 with about 350 to 400 retirements per month and no recruitment in Q4; some recruitment planned for IT and expansion.
Technical written-off portfolio about INR2,500 crore.
IT spending rising; major IT solutions planned for completion in FY27 include loan origination system revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.
demand_pricing: Advances fell from about INR78,000 crore to about INR71,000 crore in FY25 before recovering to INR83,340 crore in FY26; management said retail and mid-corporate growth is the focus and bulk advances will be reduced.
About INR2,000 crore of sanctioned loans were pending disbursal as of March 2026; management said disbursement began post April.
Loan repayments were about INR26,000 crore in FY26; management estimated total disbursements at about INR31,000 to 32,000 crore.
Around 60% to 65% of the book is EBLR linked to T-bill rates (about 55% per management figures), 2.31% EBLR linked to G-sec, MCLR 5.59%, base rate 0.31% at March 2026.
Management said EBLR is at its lowest and any upward move in market rates would help interest income; ALCO will respond as required.

qa_highlights.question: Why did advances rise sharply in the quarter and how does it fit funding and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR was strong so it prioritised advances; funding came from available resources and some short-term borrowings, and funding was not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 across advances, ROA, credit cost, GNPA, NNPA and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Business growth around 15%, deposits 10% to 15%, advances 15% to 20%, CASA 33%+, ROA 1%+, cost-to-income 52% to 53%. Credit cost was not given a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 employee cost fall while other opex rose, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any one-time shift. Employee cost cannot be cut but was held down through staff utilisation; attrition of about 350 to 400 a month and selective recruitment for IT and expansion. No FY27 employee cost figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income driven by core fees or treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income rose on fee income (processing charges, one-time ATM card fees, guarantee commission) and recovery from the technical write-off book; treasury gain about INR13 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield pressure from growth squeeze margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBLR is at its lowest and margins have bottomed; upward rate moves would help; ALCO will manage.

qa_highlights.question: Why were gross slippages so low in Q4 and what is the interest reversal impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited SMA and CMA stress controls and recovery efforts; slippage was 0.20% in Q4 vs 0.47% in Q3. It did not quantify interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Will PCR keep rising, and what are the FY27 provisioning and technical write-off recovery expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is to rise about 1% a quarter; Q4 rose more. Recovery targets are ambitious (50% of NPA and technical write-off books) with no specific figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G-sec versus EBLR book mix and the gratuity impact on employee cost?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said both figures would be shared later by email; the call gave only the rate-linked mix (EBLR linked to T-bill about 55%, G-sec 2.31%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on net worth and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ECL impact is about 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over four to five years, with about 25 to 30 bps of credit cost each year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East deposit exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East and NRI deposits are a small share; the majority of deposits are domestic.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q4 earnings lift: PAT jump was helped by lower employee cost (management did not give a FY27 employee cost figure or gratuity impact), higher fee income and technical write-off recoveries, and accelerated provisioning; track whether these recur in Q1 FY27.

Advances shortfall vs guidance: gross advances INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000-85,000 crore guidance; FY27 advances growth guidance of 15-20% depends on converting INR2,000 crore pending disbursal and on shifting mix from bulk/IBPC to retail and mid-corporate.
Margin path: management said NIM has bottomed and ALCO will respond to rate moves, but ~55% of book is T-bill linked EBLR and rate direction is market-driven; watch NIM vs the 3% plus target.

Slippage and recovery sustainability: Q4 slippage of 0.20% vs 0.47% in Q3 is well below prior run rate; the 50% NPA and technical write-off recovery target (technical write-off book ~INR2,500 crore) was called highly ambitious with no figure given.

Macro and external risks: West Asia conflict, energy prices and supply-chain pressure; branch expansion plans may be revised; ECL transition impact of 1-1.5% of capital, spread over 4-5 years (about 25-30 bps credit cost per year), not yet quantified in FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we have witnessed meaningful improvement in all the ratios and have delivered on the guidance given during my previous interactions with the investor community
Growth for the business is also target, there is a target for recovery also.
What quantum, what number, our aim is always to recover 50% of the book of NPA, 50% of the technical written-off.
I feel it has bottomed out. There may not be any chance it is coming down further.
We want to increase 1% every quarter. That number still I'm holding on.

Management repeatedly described the outlook as measured and prudent given West Asia and macro uncertainty.

532652|2026-06.headline: Karnataka Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 43% YoY to INR418.95 crores, NIM widened to 3.20%, and Gross NPA fell to 2.58%.
532652|2026-06.overview: Karnataka Bank reported a strong Q1 FY27 with PAT of INR418.95 crores (up 3% QoQ, 43% YoY), NII up 11% QoQ to INR938.29 crores, and NIM at 3.20% versus 3.07% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality improved on both gross and net NPA, with credit cost at 0.03%. Business reached a record INR1,97,007 crores, with gross advances up 4% QoQ and 17% YoY, and CASA and CD ratio both improving. Management guided to around 15% overall business growth in FY27 and an ROA of 1.35% to 1.40%, but gave limited detail on SMA-2 rise, mid-corporate growth and the ECL transition.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank expanding branches and what is the sanctioned and pipeline book to support growth, given guidance looks conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans 31 to 32 branches in FY27 (one opened, 12 to 13 before end-H1) and reiterated about 15% overall business growth, with 10% to 15% liabilities and 15% to 20% advances growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank provide more provisions given SMA-2 rose to INR750 crores from INR635 crores and special mention accounts are at INR3,435 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on controlling SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2, attributed the Q1 rise partly to holidays and single-day defaults before 30 June, and said no additional provisioning is required for slippages going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What will the ECL transition require in additional provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR is comfortable and a dedicated team has been working since 1 April on Stage 1, 2 and 3 impact; it does not foresee a problem from ECL.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost increase and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost has not gone up, citing yield-movement-related gratuity and retirement benefit provisions, and expects it in the same range next quarter onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA sustain at 1.35% to 1.40% for the full year, and what are the FY27 and FY28 ROA and ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for ROA of 1.35% to 1.40% from 1.29% in Q1 and said it will keep improving, without giving a full-year ROE target or FY28 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 'other' (non-RAM) advances segment growing faster than RAM, and when will RAM outgrow corporate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail growth requires better turnaround time and that retail hubs in 15 regional offices are driving business; it said large corporate is restricted to protect yield and bulk advances will reduce in percentage terms.

qa_highlights.question: Is mid-corporate growth returning after several quarters of YoY decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mid-corporate moderated in Q3 FY26, grew in Q4 and further in Q1 FY27 (INR16,636 crores from INR15,721 crores), and it expects growth to continue.
