ROA target raised to 1.35% to 1.40% from the earlier 1% plus framing, versus 1.29% in Q1 FY27.
NIM expected to keep improving on higher-yielding RAM and retail advances, lower bulk deposits and card-rate renewals; management said NIM would continue to improve.

Governance and CEO tenure questions were raised by investors and management gave no clear answer on tenure status.

key_quotes: We have delivered on our investor guidance and achieved meaningful improvements across all major financial ratios, proving the power of disciplined execution and operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: What pipeline of accounts could cross the US$4 million run-rate threshold in FY27, given customer count rose from 79 to 93 and top-five concentration rose to about 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the 60x4x3 target (US$4 million run-rate for 93 active customers within three years) is still the goal; the three-year timeline is metaphoric and may stretch one or two more years. Specific FY27 target accounts were not named, and sales bandwidth is being added.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Product Solutions gross margin drop from 12.8% to 5.9%: memory pricing or something else?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said memory cost pass-through removes incremental margin even though costs are passed on, and the silicon business shifting toward productization changed mix. Some products ship through the year, so margins should be read on a full-year basis and are expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two hyperscaler engagements with the same hyperscaler or different ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody confirmed they are different hyperscalers.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount rose about 9% QoQ while cost rose only about 3%; how will sales and senior analog/RF leadership headcount evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said at least five to six more sales heads will be added in the rest of the year, with some growth delivery-led. Priyaranjan said cost mix includes lateral and fresher hires and Q4 had non-recurring bonus catch-up; utilisation improved. Anup Savla said the teams are independent and senior niche analog/RF/mmWave skills are grown in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 60x4x3 target of US$4 million run-rate be reached if extended by a couple of years, and at what growth drivers, with growth at the expense of margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the company may take one more year, not a commitment to a number, and cited silicon, specialised silicon, devices (China-plus-one and Make in India) and full-stack software services as the three vectors. On margins, he said Software Services margins went from about 2-3% to 11.5-12% EBIT over six quarters and the company will maintain margins while growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue stay flat for years and then grow suddenly in software services?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan cited four changes: working closer to customers, empowering teams to own growth, investing in capability, and filling white spaces such as the Borqs and silicon acquisitions for end-to-end engagement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating cash flow been negative for two years despite profit growth, and will FY27 be cash-flow positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said cash outflow reflects investment in working capital and fixed assets, not collection problems; a large cash consumption is expected this year, Q1 included inventory build for memory shortage. Funding will come from internal accruals and external funds, and the cash-flow positive timeline is work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Borqs break-even point still hold at the earlier US$60-70 million top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said break-even is now about US$12 million of quarterly revenue, after which the business adds to the bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of GlobalFoundries and Intel IP certifications and the formal TSMC relationship?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said all three are in progress with substantial progress, leading to more design activity, but no announcements can be made yet due to the non-public nature of the work.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RF and mmWave projects and when will revenue from these niche technologies show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said projects span connectivity, automotive interfaces and power, and revenue mix already reflects such implementation, though project details were not disclosed. Hareesh Ramanna said the Borqs instrument-cluster module is ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive, so no commercial order is yet in hand.

532663|2026-09.headline: Sasken Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.6% YoY to Rs.321 Cr with EBITDA margin up 330 bps QoQ to 12.9%, driven by software services.

Margins improved: gross margin 26.8%, EBITDA margin 12.9%, EBIT margin 8.9%, and PAT Rs.26 Cr (8% margin). TCV signed was $47 Mn, with $25 Mn new bookings, and management said the 60x4x3 target is delayed by about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable margins should be expected for software services and product solutions?

532667|2026-03.headline: Suzlon delivered a record 830 MW in Q4 FY26 and 2,456 MW for the year, with FY26 revenue up 54% to INR16,679 crore.
532667|2026-03.overview: Suzlon reported record Q4 FY26 India deliveries of 830 MW and FY26 deliveries of 2,456 MW (up 58%). Consolidated Q4 revenue was INR5,468 crore with EBITDA of INR964 crore (up 39% YoY) and reported PAT of INR1,114 crore, while FY26 PAT of INR3,153 crore includes a INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition. Management highlighted a shift toward EPC and development (DevCo) contracts, with EPC share of the order book rising to 28% from about 20% in Q2, and a 2.1 GW Andhra Pradesh development right extended by 24 months. Order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW at the start of the year, while commissioning reached 332 MW in Q4 and 744 MW for the year, with 971 MW erected but not yet commissioned.

532683|2026-09.headline: AIA Engineering Q2 FY27 sales flat at ~61,500 t; Q2 EBITDA ~INR361 crore on freight cost spike, management guides 25,000-30,000 t volume growth as internal goal for FY28-29.

Management said the new value-added strategy (liners and NGDS grinding media) remains intact, with trials delayed or redesigned at some mines, and that it is internally targeting volume growth of 25,000-30,000 t a year from FY28, explicitly not as formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How do FOCO economics work for PVR INOX on the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the management fee (10-14% of top line) is booked; the landlord keeps the property P&L, and PVR INOX incurs no capex or opex on FOCO screens, per management.

risks_watch: Occupancy stuck near 26% (26.2% FY26) despite the target of rising levels; management says 27-28% can restore pre-COVID margins.
Advertising growth subdued; big films shifting dates cut growth by about 7-8%, with dependence on H2 releases.
Macro risk from West Asia crisis and possible fuel price hikes on urban discretionary spend; management says no direct impact seen.
Q4 PAT includes a one-time divestment gain (4700BC to Marico), so underlying earnings are not clear from the call.
Execution of 138 signed capital-light screens over about 18 months and first smart screen pilots by mid-July 2026.
Timing of net-cash status and capital allocation (dividend or buyback) yet to be decided.
Lease and rent cost trend as capital-light share rises; no quantified rent-to-revenue guidance given.
532689|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pipeline and balance sheet, but evasive on capital allocation (buyback/dividend) and on quantifying rent savings and timing of net cash. Management brushed off macro and advertising concerns with qualitative reassurance rather than numbers.
key_quotes: FY26 was a d efining year for PVR-INOX. We delivered our best ever financial performance, brought net debt to a negligible level and pivoted decisively to a capital-light growth model even as the Indian box office reached an all -time high.
And we are yet to see 1 full year of operations.
And the entire P&L is consolidated.
Not for the heck of it, we should just put screens everywhere.

532689|2026-06.headline: PVR INOX Q1 FY27 PAT of INR71 crore vs loss of INR34 crore a year ago; net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026.
532689|2026-06.overview: Revenue on an Ind AS 116 adjusted basis rose 12% YoY to INR1,642 crore, with EBITDA nearly doubling to INR230 crore at a 14% margin. Footfalls rose 8% to 36.6 million, with ATP at INR273 (+8%) and SPH at INR161 (+9%). The company turned net cash of INR80 crore, and management said growth can now be funded from internal cash flows. No new screens opened in Q1 because completed sites were awaiting regulatory licences; openings are expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR34 crore in Q1 FY26
company describes it as debt-free; peak debt cited as INR1,450 crore
up from about 63-64%; convenience fee income +29% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Film hire cost and F&B COGS

segments.name: Exhibition (cinemas)
segments.commentary: Footfalls 36.6 million (+8%), ATP INR273 (+8%), SPH INR161 (+9%). Premium formats are 16% of the circuit (IMAX, 4DX, ICE, ScreenX, recliners, Insignia, Director's Cut, LUXE).

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management said ad revenue is still below its post-COVID peak and expects about a year to fully recover. Growth is expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 with large titles; it did not give a figure.

segments.name: Alternate content and F&B
segments.commentary: Alternate content (live sports, concerts, events) ATP is about INR409; artist cost ranges from 35% to 65-70% of ticket. Food court JV with Devyani has 3 outlets open, with more in the pipeline. Web and app monetisation launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gross screen additions of 90-100 in FY27 (about 80 net after closures); Q1 had no openings and few closures are expected for the rest of the year.
FY27 capex now about INR350 crore, down from the earlier INR400 crore, including the food court JV and a higher renovation share.
Film hire cost guided at 45% to 45.5% of revenue for full-year FY27; F&B COGS expected to fall YoY.
Near-term target is a return to pre-COVID ROCE levels; no FCF target was given.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 expansion: about 300 cities identified, first opening in Muzaffarpur shortly, with asset-light and FOCO models; growth expected to accelerate from FY28.
Management expects margins of pre-COVID levels even at 27-28% occupancy.
capex_capacity: Screen count about 1,790 today, up from about 1,650 at the merger; about 120 net screens added over the last 4 years.
FY27 screen openings were held back by pending regulatory licences; openings expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.
Closed screens in Q1 were loss-making and more than 18-20 years old; bulk of FY27 closures done in Q1.
Around 600 screens are in South India; southern concentration is about 34%, according to an analyst's estimate.
Asset-light and FOCO models are the main route for new sites; the 15 million sq ft of leased space is being offered for sublease where it is not needed.
demand_pricing: India box office grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY27 across metros, Tier 2 and Tier 3, and across languages.
North America box office was up 14% YoY at $4.8 billion in H1 2026, per management.
Hollywood share of box office is about 60% overall, about 50% for big films, and up to 80-90% for mid and smaller films.
ATP growth was driven by dynamic pricing plus premium mix; discounts are offered on Tuesdays, morning shows and front seats.

Management sees no INR500 crore-plus film so far in the year, but says mid-scale films are performing; it views the upcoming slate (Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Three) as strong.
Management said the occupancy trend is recovering as release windows return to 8 weeks, but did not disclose a current occupancy figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the screen closures and asset-light mix affecting the FY27 screen and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross screen additions are still 90-100 and net additions about 80. Capex is now about INR350 crore versus INR400 crore earlier, because FOCO and capital-light demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revisit asset-light models now that it is net cash, and is more real estate monetisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO will continue and will not limit growth of 100-120 screens a year. Capital will be deployed where needed without borrowing. Real estate monetisation is not planned at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why have footfalls stayed flat at 14-15 crore over rolling 12 months despite southern screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the southern skew reflects where opportunities are; 150 million admissions last year was the post-COVID high. It said occupancy is recovering and that margins at 27-28% occupancy can match pre-COVID levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 FCF target and what is the plan for surplus cash, including buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Sharma said there is no FCF target. The immediate goal is pre-COVID ROCE. Shareholder returns, including buyback, are being evaluated and will be disclosed when the Board decides.

qa_highlights.question: What are the unit economics of properties on the capital-light models?
qa_highlights.answer: Properties take 12-18 months to mature. FY24 and FY25 vintages are at margins above company level, and first-vintage performance will be shared by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did online penetration rise and what is the app/web monetisation revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Online penetration rose to about 69% on marketing and content mix. Growth will slow from here. The app/web ad product launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did film hire and COGS fall about 200 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Film hire fell because Dhurandhar was in its lower-rate third and fourth weeks, and there was no mega-blockbuster to trigger bonus payouts. F&B COGS have fallen YoY for two years.

risks_watch: Release calendar: no INR500 crore-plus film so far in FY27; the slate depends on Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic and Hollywood tentpoles.
Licence delays pushed Q1 openings into Q2 and Q3; the 90-100 gross screen target depends on this bunching.
Advertising has not yet recovered to post-COVID levels; management expects about another year.
Online penetration growth is slowing near 70%, so convenience fee growth will depend on ATP and admits.
Capital allocation is undecided: buyback or other shareholder returns may be announced, and the company says it is evaluating all options.
Occupancy is still below pre-COVID levels; management has not disclosed a figure.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 was a strong start to the year.
We can now fund our growth from our own cash inflows, continue on our capital-light path and do so without the weight of leverage on our balance sheet.
So we are evaluating all options, including growth as well as allocating this capital, which is best for the long-term shareholder value creation.
Yes, it would take another maybe a year before we get to the post-COVID and go ahead of that.

532689|2026-09.headline: PVR INOX Q2 FY27 adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to INR 475 crores at a 22.3% margin, with PAT more than doubling to INR 273 crores.
532689|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was described as the best-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by a record industry box office of INR 4,433 crores (up 23% YoY) and footfalls up 4% to 46.3 million. Ind AS 116 adjusted total income grew 17% to INR 2,133 crores, with operating leverage lifting EBITDA margin about 420 bps. Management turned net cash (INR 141 crores at September-end), executed a maiden INR 300 crore buyback, and adopted a capital allocation policy targeting around 30% of annual surplus cash flow returned to shareholders. Screen growth is guided to accelerate, with 90-100 openings in FY27 and a new capital-light SMART Cinema format piloted in Muzaffarpur.

segments.name: Movie exhibition
segments.commentary: Footfalls 46.3 million (+4% YoY), occupancy 30.4%. Company says it under-indexed industry growth (18% vs 23%) because content was spread across single screens in Tier 2-4 towns.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.commentary: F&B spend per head INR 153 (+14% YoY). Popcorn and Pepsi make up about 60% of F&B sales; management says gross margin rose from about 74% to 77-78%. About 85% of footfalls buy F&B.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films. Management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War; a pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

segments.name: Network and expansion
segments.commentary: Network at 1,797 screens across 114 cities (India and Sri Lanka). H1 added 24 screens across 6 cinemas and exited 25 mostly loss-making screens.

guidance_outlook: Open 90-100 new screens in FY27, mostly in H2 and mainly capital-light formats.
Next year (FY28) screen openings guided to about 150-175 per year, with about 60-70 possibly SMART screens; roughly 500 screens over three years was accepted by management.
Overall FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores (H1 spend INR 132 crores); FY28 capex likely above INR 350 crores, plus or minus.
Depreciation to fall by INR 35-40 crores a year after a useful-life change for projectors and IT equipment.
Capital allocation policy: keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x after distributions, invest for growth, and return about 30% of annual surplus cash flow via dividends or buybacks.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to benefit from a strong film slate; said it was 'very hopeful and optimistic' about H2 but did not give a Q3 footfall number.
Target payback of 3-4 years per unit; SMART Cinema capex 25-30% below normal screens and opex about 25% lower.
capex_capacity: Network 1,797 screens across 114 cities; 24 screens added and 25 exited in H1 FY27.

First SMART Cinema opened in Muzaffarpur, Bihar in September 2026 (capex 25-30% lower, opex about 25% lower, ATP about INR 190); two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur) and about 100 more signed for opening in the next 12-18 months.
300 cities identified for SMART Cinemas; expected two or three more SMART openings this fiscal.
Expansion mix is asset-light, FOCO and lease; for FOCO, only management fees are booked; for asset-light, full P&L is consolidated.
Around 35-40% of new screens in the last 2-3 years opened in South India.
demand_pricing: Industry box office INR 4,433 crores in Q2 (record, first quarter above INR 4,000 crores); H1 INR 7,618 crores (+22%).
English cinema INR 1,024 crores (+87%); Spider-Man: Brand New Day INR 608 crores; Odyssey INR 233 crores.
Hindi led by Hanuman Ansh (INR 351 crores) and Mirzapur: The Movie (INR 267 crores). Management argued Hindi growth is understated due to dubbed English films being reported under English.
Value offers: weekday morning shows at INR 99, Friday first shows at INR 149, front-row seats from INR 79.
South India average ticket price about 25% below the rest of India; management said higher occupancy more than offsets this.

qa_highlights.question: How are SMART Cinemas priced, what is the capex, and what is the 2-year opening plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower than normal cinemas; ATP around INR 190 at the pilot. About 100 more are signed for 12-18 months. Management said growth will not be compromised while keeping paybacks within 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hindi incremental box office so small in H1 versus regional and English?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 had a high Hindi base; Hollywood was recovering. It added that dubbed English films (about INR 200 crores from Spider-Man) count as English, so Hindi growth is understated.

qa_highlights.question: Will screen additions accelerate after the cleanup of underperforming screens?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Past closures were of dilapidated mall screens. Management guided to 150-175 openings a year from next fiscal, with about 500 screens over three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are FOCO and asset-light revenues and costs accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light is fully consolidated. FOCO books only management fees, with operating costs at the franchisee. Lease screens are traditional leases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROU assets and lease liabilities decline despite openings?
qa_highlights.answer: About 23-24 loss-making screens closed in H1, which offset new openings. ROU assets and liabilities also decline through depreciation and repayment under Ind AS 116.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion in F&B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a high-margin mix (popcorn and Pepsi are about 60% of sales), supplier renegotiation, a 4PL logistics migration that cuts wastage, and volume growth from weekend and weekday promotions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PVR's box office growth (18%) lag the industry (23%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to content mix: Hanuman Ansh, Mirzapur and regional films did well in Tier 2-4 towns where single screens dominate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the depreciation and capex numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year from the useful-life change. FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores; FY28 above INR 350 crores.

risks_watch: Ad revenue recovery depends on the Q3-Q4 tentpole slate (Ramayana, King, Avengers, Love & War) and the digital pay-per-eyeball platform, due in 8-10 months.
SMART format is a pilot with only about two months of data; the 150-175 screen FY28 target depends on the pipeline converting.
Lower rent-to-revenue in Q2 is tied to revenue-share terms on legacy screens (minimum guarantee or revenue share, whichever is higher); rent rose about 11% YoY in Q2.
Q2 other income includes INR 7 crores of one-off provision reversals.
Pending southern state ticket-price issues: management said no conversations are underway.

rows.why: SMART ATP is about INR 190 against INR 298 company-wide, with capex 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower, and about 100 more signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.why: Net cash of INR 141 crores at end-September after H1 FREE cash flow of INR 604 crores, with a policy to return about 30% of surplus cash flow and keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x.

rows.label: Ad revenue recovery on tentpole films
rows.why: Advertising was weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films, and management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, but no ad figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, F&B gross margin, the SMART format's paybacks and H2 films, and stayed evasive on Q3 footfalls and disputed the Hindi box office data. Analysts pressed on the lag versus industry growth, the SMART pilot's short data history and the 150-175 screen FY28 target.

532698|2026-03.headline: Nitin Spinners Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR859.8 crore (+7.4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin rose to 15.17%, with management guiding to a 16-20% normalised margin in FY27.
532698|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR859.8 crore, up 7.4% QoQ and 2.2% YoY, driven by better demand and yarn prices. EBITDA rose 16.9% QoQ to INR130.4 crore, with margin up 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, and PAT reached INR57.4 crore. For full FY26, revenue fell 2.8% to INR3,213.9 crore and EBITDA fell 4% to INR452.8 crore, while PAT rose 1.2% to INR177.6 crore. Management said the capex programme (fabric and spinning expansion, renewable power) is on track for H2 FY27 commissioning.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Yarn was 74% of FY26 revenue; spinning capacity ran at over 98% utilisation in Q4 FY26, with management guiding 97-98% going forward. Average yarn spread (realisation over cotton cost, around 33-34 count) is about INR120-125/kg, up from about INR110/kg last quarter.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric was 21% of FY26 revenue (woven about 18%, knitted about 4%, per the Q&A corrections). Woven capacity ran at over 90% utilisation in Q4; woven realisation rose about 2-2.5% QoQ and knitted about 5% QoQ. Knitted utilisation is below normal, with a 65-70% normal level expected to return in 1-1.5 years.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Others contributed 5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 63% of Q4 FY26 revenue (61.9% for FY26); domestic was 37% in Q4 (31.8% for FY26).

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin range of 16-20%, which management expects to reach in FY27.

Fabric capex adds 35 million metres, taking capacity to 75 million metres (errata to 70 million metres as stated), and spinning adds 22,000 tonnes to about 130,000 tonnes. Commissioning in H2 FY27: fabric from October-December 2026 and spinning from January-February 2027.

Capex of about INR1,000-1,100 crore is expected to add more than INR1,000 crore to top line. Normalisation of yarn prices may add 5-7% to existing turnover. Management expects 30-35% revenue growth on the existing base over time.

Renewable power: about 75 MW added including PPAs, reaching close to 100 MW installed. A 10 MW hybrid PPA is due by Q3 FY27. Expected savings of INR50 crore per year at full run-rate, with INR30-35 crore in the current year.
Total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crore after commissioning, including working capital. Average borrowing cost about 5.6%, working capital under 7%, blended about 6.5%.
Asset turn of about 1.2-1.3x at company level; new capex expected at about 1:1 excluding renewable capex.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion adds 35 million metres (to about 75 million metres, errata). Spinning adds 22,000 tonnes (to about 130,000 tonnes). Commissioning in H2 FY27.

Over INR300 crore spent so far, including about INR140 crore in capital advances, about INR55-60 crore capitalised from modernisation and balancing, and capital WIP of about INR100 crore. The balance is to be funded by internal accruals and debt.
Additional energy capex of about INR230-240 crore, not planned before last year. Renewable power capex is on schedule for H2 FY27.

Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme incentives include capital subsidy (about 20-27% of eligible investment, paid over 10 years), interest subsidy (5% of term loan or 2.5% of eligible fixed investment, whichever is lower, for 5 years), plus electricity duty and mandi tax rebates. Management did not quantify the total.
demand_pricing: Demand improved in Q4 FY26 in both domestic and export markets, driven by US tariff removal, downstream restocking and longer transit times. Management said exports of about 100 million kg of yarn a year are steady, with a possible 5-10% increase.

Yarn spread (realisation over cotton) rose to about INR120-125/kg from about INR110/kg last quarter. Management called INR120-125 the median and said it should be sustainable, with a minimum of INR100/kg against an earlier floor of INR90/kg.
Polyester prices rose more than 20% after the West Asia conflict, but synthetic yarn spreads stayed flat. Blended yarn margins improved marginally.

Cotton: domestic prices were INR52,000-55,000 per candy in the lowest period, around 4 years low, and have been rising since recent weeks. Duty on imported cotton was removed Aug-Dec 2025; the industry is asking for a repeat removal.
Fabric prices lag yarn: the company has already raised fabric prices, and management expects further improvement. The India-UK and India-EU FTAs are expected to add European and UK orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised yarn spread and margin, excluding inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spread was about INR90/kg at the low end historically and about INR140-150/kg at the high end; a minimum of INR100/kg is now the floor, and INR120-125/kg is sustainable. Last year's margin at INR110 was about 11.5-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the freight and gas cost impacts from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sea freight is up 75-80% and other regions 15-20% versus February, but freight is normally passed on under FOB terms and has normalised since March. Gas-based yarn is a very small share, with under a day of disruption and gas costs up about 1.7x since February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the duty removal on cotton and the top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty removal is up to the government, with a possible permanent fix in 5-6 months. Top-line growth is expected from the INR1,000 crore+ capex, yarn normalisation (5-7%) and recovery, for 30-35% growth on the existing base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the fabric and knitted utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Knitted utilisation is expected to recover to the normal 65-70% within 1-1.5 years, as US tariffs were reduced from 50%. Some customers were lost to competing countries and are being regained.

risks_watch: Cotton import duty status and cotton availability. The industry wants duty removed; government has not committed to a timeline.
West Asia conflict: transit times up about 2 weeks, sea freight volatile, and polyester and gas costs rising. Management says these are passed on, but synthetic spreads have not widened.
Capex execution: commissioning slips from H2 FY27, and ramp-up of new fabric and yarn capacity. Management said it can increase the reach of fabric to European and UK buyers under the FTAs.
Knitted fabric utilisation is well below normal, at the 65-70% benchmark, and customers were lost in the US tariff period.
Future capex plans are not yet quantified. Management declined to give future capex or fabric margin targets.

532698|2026-06.headline: Nitin Spinners Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR875 crore (+10.3% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 17.78%, with PAT up 83.6% to INR75.3 crore.
532698|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR875 crore was the company's highest ever quarter for a second straight quarter, up 10.3% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, driven mainly by yarn realisations. EBITDA before other income was INR155.6 crore (+39.85% YoY), with margin at 17.78% versus 14.02% a year earlier and 15.17% in the prior quarter. Management attributed the margin gain mostly to yarn price realisation outpacing cotton cost, with smaller contributions from power cost savings and efficiency. Management guided that the new capacities (fabric +35 million metres, spinning +74,000 spindles) will add INR200-300 crore revenue in the near term, though the commissioning timeline has since been reset.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Running at 98% utilisation. Yarn spread (yarn price less cotton) reported at about INR130/kg currently versus about INR110 in the prior quarter. Management said yarn price increases outpaced cotton, and a fall in outside yarn sales was due to higher in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit.

segments.name: Woven fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation above 92%. Fabric margins have not expanded like yarn; pass-through is only of actual cotton increases. Fabric revenue was about INR700 crore plus in FY26 and is about 20-21% of revenue, targeted at about 30% after expansion.

segments.name: Knitted fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 55-60%, below the pre-US-tariff norm of 60-65%, because of US tariff uncertainty; the US had been a major market for knit fabric.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay in the company's 16-20% band; management said it aims for the upper end but gave no firm guidance on reaching it. Management said it expects current margins to be maintained, and declined to comment on improvement.

Renewable power capacity expected operational by end Q3 FY27; management estimates about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit, with about INR1.2-1.5 crore already in Q1 and an analyst assumption of about INR12.5 crore per quarter from Q4.
Blended power cost expected around INR5.50/unit once solar covers about 60% of requirements.

New capacity: weaving starts in about two months, processing in about 1.5 months later (around Diwali), spinning on stream by about December; utilisation to ramp to 31 March 2027, with fabric 100% ramp taking a quarter or two into FY28.

Expansion adds about INR1,000-1,100 crore of turnover at full run-rate, of which about INR500 crore is fabric (FY28 fabric revenue targeted at INR1,200 crore) and yarn about 40% for external sale; management said incremental fabric revenue is 'not factoring in' the price volatility.
Management said no new capex is planned until after FY28 beyond the announced expansion.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion of 35 million metres (weaving plus finishing; solid and yarn-dyed fabrics; no printing capacity added).
Spinning expansion of 74,000 spindles; about 22,000 metric tons of new yarn capacity, of which 16,000-18,000 MT goes into fabric and some to yarn dyeing.
Capex of about INR1,100 crore; Rajasthan textile scheme incentives apply, with capital subsidy booked in other income.
Renewable power expansion on schedule for end Q3 FY27.
Spinning utilisation 98%; woven fabric utilisation over 92%; knit fabric 55-60%.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about 8-10% in Q1 on lower global output and West Asia-related logistics issues; India removed cotton import duty.
Indian cotton had been priced above the Cotlook index in 2023-24 (about +5-7%); it now trades at about -1 to -2% versus Cotlook, a delta of about 7-8 points.
Indian yarn exports to China rose to about 110-115 million kg in CY26 from 90-100 million kg in 2025; management sees China's import demand continuing.
Management said spinning capacity exits in the last 1-2 years and the post-US-tariff demand slump have rebalanced supply.

Volumes: management said yarn outside sales fell because of in-house consumption by fabric units and about some stock held at quarter-end due to vessel shortages; these were said to have dispatched in July.
Price pass-through: yarn price increases exceeded cotton increases (management cited about 120-125% pass-through on a 100% cotton increase); fabric pass-through is only 1:1 on cotton.
India crop: about 318-320 lakh bales for 2025-26, versus 326-327 lakh bales in 2024-25; 2026-27 acreage about 0.5-1% lower; rainfall over the next month is the key factor.

qa_highlights.question: What are the yarn spreads in Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about INR110 in the last quarter of FY26 and are now about INR130, and management said this is sustained at current conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Are current margins of 17-18% sustainable for the next one to two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to maintain the current level, with cost savings helping, but declined to comment on any further improvement or on a decline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 EBITDA expansion is from power savings, realisation, and inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Power savings contributed about 0.5% of EBITDA and a similar amount from solar; the gross margin rise to about 40% came mainly from yarn realisation. Inventory gains were described as very small, and the working capital cycle is broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What share of new capacity revenue goes to fabric, and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600-plus crore of the expansion's turnover is fabric, with yarn ramp-up complete by 31 March 2027 and fabric taking a quarter or two more into FY28; fabric revenue is expected at INR1,200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, as it is in a growth phase funding capex through internal accruals and loans, so a buyback would not be prudent now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning garmenting or home textiles as the next growth leg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said garmenting is only an idea with nothing firmed up, and home textiles and garmenting are both seen as equally good opportunities, with Europe the key opening for home textiles after the US slump.

risks_watch: Commissioning timeline: weaving in about two months, processing about 1.5 months later, spinning by about December; fabric ramp-up may take a quarter or two into FY28 (management also cited 6-8 months for fabric ramp-up in one answer).

Cotton price volatility and pass-through: fabric margins expand only 1:1 with cotton, while yarn spread (about INR130/kg) is sustained only under current conditions; management declined to commit to margin levels beyond maintaining current ones.
US tariff uncertainty keeps knitted fabric utilisation at about 55-60% versus 60-65% pre-tariff norm; knit fabric exposure to the US remains a drag.
Monsoon/rainfall over the next month will determine the 2026-27 Indian cotton crop size; quality outlook depends on the same.
Yarn outside-sales volumes fell QoQ and YoY due to in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit; shipment logistics (vessel availability) to be monitored for July dispatches.

Renewable power capacity due by end Q3 FY27; about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit is management's estimate, and the blended power cost target of about INR5.50/unit depends on solar covering about 60% of requirements.
key_quotes: So there is no issue at all for absorbing the yarn capacity.
Improvement I cannot comment upon at this point of time.
We are expecting same. In view of the cost initial cost saving initiatives going forward which is also going to kick in and also the margins looking reasonable.
It is always the endeavour of the management to go to the upper level of the band which we have discussed and that is a continuous effort.
We are not able to improve upon the margins as we are able to improve upon the margins in the yarn business.

532698|2026-09.headline: Nitin Spinners Q2 FY27 revenue rose 29.6% YoY to INR985.2 crore and EBITDA margin hit 17.8%, with capex commissioning slated for December 2026.

EBITDA rose 76.3% YoY to INR175.5 crore, with margin at 17.8%, flat QoQ and up 471 bps YoY. Management said trial production of about 41 lakh meters of fabric contributed roughly INR21 crore of revenue at a small EBITDA loss, so ex-trial margin was about 18.5%. Expansion commissioning is on schedule for end-December 2026, with renewable capacity rising from 41 MW to about 95 MW.

guidance_outlook: Commercial production in all divisions expected by end-December 2026; spinning utilisation to reach 95%+ by end-March 2027; finished fabric capacity to take 8-9 months more to reach full levels (around August-September 2027).

Depreciation to rise from about INR37.5-38 crore per quarter to INR53-54 crore per quarter after expansion, and to about INR200 crore plus in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue will the new fabric capacity add?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR300-350 crore in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore a year from FY28, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise about 40% since March?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly export receivables from higher exports; no extra credit given, and fewer bill discounting limits were utilised. No major overdues, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is knitting utilisation low?

Rising receivables (about 40% since March, mainly exports) and higher working capital and debt (total about INR1,950 crore by March 2027).
Bangladesh wage-agitation shutdowns and US tariff uncertainty affecting knitting and export orders.

Management is in discussions with the government on radio reforms and expects them, linked to the new frequency licence investment question.

Radio effective rates were flat YoY; volumes were down about 5%.

Gaana acquisition costs rose as AI search reduced referral traffic and Google performance marketing became more expensive.

532725|2026-06.headline: Solar Industries to acquire Omnia Holdings (South Africa) on an all-cash, 100% basis, funded by debt; ~$1.35bn deal value cited, FY28 leverage target below 2x EBITDA.
532725|2026-06.overview: This was a business update call on the proposed acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings Limited by Solar SA Investments (wholly owned step-down subsidiary), held as a transaction-only call, with no questions on core Solar operations taken. Management framed the deal as creating an integrated global explosives and blasting platform, adding mining (BME brand) and agriculture/agritech businesses, with benefits expected to be visible from FY28. Funding will be all-cash, through debt at Omnia level plus Solar-group debt and internal accruals, with no equity issuance planned. Management guided to combined FY28 revenue of about INR30,000-32,000 crore and EBITDA of INR6,800-7,000 crore, and said net debt/EBITDA will stay below 2x. Many figures are management estimates pending shareholder and regulatory approvals, and structuring is not finalised.

Guided Pinaka negotiations are at the final stage; management said the Pinaka family could total about INR9,000 crore across variants.
Missile programs: management expects RFP and contract timelines of roughly 1.5-2 years after trials, so new missile orders are unlikely before about 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected from the non-defense business for the rest of FY27 and into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better growth in H2 from domestic coal and mining demand; no specific volume number was given for the non-defense business.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhargavastra orders come this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment. Internal trials should finish in calendar 2026, followed by field trials; commercial orders are years away.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be beaten, and will EBITDA margin go above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will surpass the INR14,000 crore revenue guidance and expects H1 margin of about 28.45% to average about 29% for the year. Domestic is about 27-28% of revenue and should grow in H2. Management did not commit to margins above 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic explosives volume growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth is about 6-7%; Solar targets 10-15% volume growth annually, with management declining to give FY28-29 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Guided Pinaka and other defense orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Guided Pinaka (about INR3,000 crore) is expected to be finalised before FY27 end. Management declined to name other programs in negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Omnia acquisition close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no closing timeline and said it would update the market once approvals are received.

risks_watch: Omnia acquisition: closing timeline and agri business contribution are still unclear, and approvals are pending.
Defense order conversion: Guided Pinaka (about INR3,000 crore) and missile programs depend on RFPs and contract timelines, which management pegs at months to years.
Commodity and supply-chain volatility, including ammonium nitrate prices and geopolitical disruption, could affect margins.
International explosives share fell to 43% from 46% in Q2, and domestic share fell to 27% from 29%, so mix is shifting toward defense.
Management withheld FY28-29 defense and domestic guidance, so visibility beyond FY27 remains limited.
532725|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on FY27 top-line and margin trajectory, with management stating it will beat revenue guidance. Cautious and evasive on specifics: it declined to size or time Bhargavastra, Omnia, other defense programs, and FY28-29 targets, citing confidentiality and uncertainty.
key_quotes: Based on results, what we achieved, the strength of the order book and the opportunity available for us, we expect to surpass our stated annual guidance, which we have given at the start of the financial year FY27.
And as far as Bhargavastra is concerned, like we have said that we are likely to conclude all our internal trials in this calendar year.

532726|2026-03.headline: Gallantt FY26 consolidated revenue INR 4,418.92 crore (+3.95% YoY) with EBITDA per ton up to INR 8,785 from INR 8,300; net debt-free.
532726|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described by management as a consolidation year with volume growth of 1.7%, while EBITDA margin reached 17.56% and PAT margin 10.81%. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 1,204.81 crore, up 12.93% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 16.99% versus 15.5% in Q3. The company reported net cash of about INR 360 crore after INR 440 crore of borrowings, mostly working-capital lines. Management outlined a INR 3,000 crore capex plan (steel capacity 1.0 to 1.3 million tonnes, mines, solar) funded from internal accruals, with a medium-term growth plan to be presented in Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 168.69 crore and 15.5% in Q3

segments.name: Sales volumes (FY26)
segments.commentary: Pellets sold 49 kt, sponge iron sold 125 kt, billet sold 81 kt, TMT bar sold 766 kt. Most upstream output is consumed internally; management aims to lower the share sold externally.

guidance_outlook: Capex plan of INR 3,000 crore: steel capacity expansion from 1.0 to 1.3 million tonnes at about INR 1,200 crore, due H2 FY27 (management said completion in current FY).
Solar capex about INR 225-300 crore: 18 MW at Gujarat (Sidhpur) by Q2 FY27, 60 MW at Gorakhpur/Prayagraj by Q4 FY27; expected annual savings INR 30-40 crore.
Captive mines in Rajasthan and UP (four mines allotted) with about INR 1,500 crore capex, targeted by FY28; expected EBITDA gain about INR 2,000 per ton.

Medium-term growth plan to be presented in Q2 FY27.

Gujarat upstream de-bottlenecking capex in current FY expected to lift EBITDA per ton.
demand_pricing: Raw material cost held at about 72% of net realisation in both FY25 and FY26 despite coal and iron ore volatility.
Company claims about 25% market share in its UP and Gujarat selling areas and a brand-driven premium over peers.
Iron ore sourcing: Gorakhpur uses fines from Odisha, MP and some Maharashtra; Gujarat uses pellets from Rajasthan, NMDC long-term offtake, and imports when viable.
Management sees no near-term case for exports unless export realisations are clearly better than domestic; no geographic expansion beyond UP and Gujarat in the short-to-medium term.
Management described softer realisations during FY26 with EBITDA/ton still improving.

qa_highlights.question: Where do you see the company in 2-3 years, in terms of top-line and bottom-line growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Post the INR 3,000 crore expansion to 1.3 million tonnes, revenue should rise to about INR 5,300-5,400 crore with lower costs; a second phase medium- to long-term plan to be announced around Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What margins do you expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 15-17%; with project completion and mining integration, management expects around 20%.

qa_highlights.question: How is capex funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely internal accruals; management later clarified there is no equity component in the INR 3,000 crore programme, though it said it would consider debt and equity where appropriate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY26 volume figures and capex timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Production and sales volumes were given by product (see segments). Steel capacity expansion in H2 FY27, solar by FY27 end, mines by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is done with the cash surplus of about INR 800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus is treated as temporary; about INR 360 crore net cash, part deployed in intercorporate deposits at 12% payable on demand within three months; cash to go mainly to capex and partly dividends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak utilisation and optimum capacity level?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation has risen to 88% from about 80% earlier; management targets 90-92%.

Execution risk on INR 1,500 crore mine development targeted for FY28, pending approvals; management acknowledged Indian mining approvals are slow.

Implementation of the INR 3,000 crore programme and the later medium-term plan; management flagged balanced funding (equity and external borrowing) as a possible requirement, which conflicts with the 'internal accruals only' statement.
Raw material and iron ore cost volatility, currency impact on imports, and dependence on coal and iron ore pricing.
Reliance on UP and Gujarat markets; no near-term geographic diversification.

532726|2026-06.headline: Gallantt Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 203 crore (18% margin) from INR 254 crore a year ago, though flat sequentially, on coal costs and a pellet plant shutdown.
532726|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 2% year-on-year to INR 1,146 crore but fell from INR 1,205 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA was INR 203 crore (18% margin) versus INR 209 crore in Q4 and INR 254 crore in Q1 FY26, and PAT was INR 124 crore (11% margin). Management attributed the year-on-year decline to higher raw material costs (up 9%), the planned pellet plant shutdown, a seasonal monsoon-driven TMT price correction, and higher employee costs. The 1.23 million tonne capacity expansion and captive iron ore mines remain on schedule for H2 FY27 and FY28 respectively.

segments.name: TMT / long products (Gorakhpur and Gujarat)
segments.commentary: TMT sales volume was flat YoY at about 192,000 tonnes and down about 8% QoQ against a strong Q4 FY26. Gorakhpur rolling mill utilisation is 93%, while Kutch is at about 66%.

segments.name: Pellet and sponge iron
segments.commentary: External sales fell YoY and QoQ due to higher captive consumption for DRI and steelmaking, plus the planned pellet plant shutdown, which is now complete.

segments.name: Billets
segments.commentary: Billet volumes grew 13% YoY and 38% QoQ, running ahead of internal plans for the year.

guidance_outlook: Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes (0.23 million tonnes) under the INR 3,000 crore capex programme is expected to commission in H2 FY27, with benefits flowing from H2.
Pellet plant returns to normal captive utilisation in the coming quarter now the shutdown is complete; management expects no substantial EBITDA erosion through the year.
Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted because of the monsoon; management expects Q3 and Q4 to pick up.
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 7-9% this year; management referred to 8-9% in the Q&A.
Captive iron ore mines (UP and Rajasthan) are targeted to commence production in FY28; UP exploration expected to finish in 2-3 months and Rajasthan in about six months.
Solar: 18 MW in Gujarat due for Q2 FY27 and 60 MW at Gorakhpur due for Q4 FY27 (the call also cites 67 MW elsewhere, so the split is unclear).
Debottlenecking at Gujarat unit to complete within FY27.
capex_capacity: Total capex programme about INR 3,000 crore, of which about INR 800 crore spent over FY26 and Q1 FY27; INR 137 crore spent in Q1 FY27. Funded by internal accruals with no term loans planned.
Roughly half of capex goes to mining: three iron ore mines (two in UP, one in Rajasthan), with beneficiation plants in UP and a beneficiation-cum-pellet plant in Rajasthan. Production from FY28.
Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes, commissioning in H2 FY27.

Pellet plant installed capacity about 8 lakh tonnes against raw feed need of 9-9.5 lakh tonnes a year.
demand_pricing: TMT and rebar prices corrected meaningfully during the quarter from a firm start; management said the correction was seasonal and sector-wide, with flat products holding up better.

Management claims a market share above 25% in its addressable UP market and cites brand marketing with celebrity endorsements (Ajay Devgn, and now Janhvi Kapoor).
Export: management said exports are not a focus. Gorakhpur is inland, and Gujarat billet exports happen only occasionally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the iron ore and pellet sourcing strategy, and who are the top suppliers?
qa_highlights.answer: Gorakhpur sources iron ore fines from Odisha Mineral Corporation, multiple Madhya Pradesh concentrate suppliers and Lloyds (Maharashtra), mixed on price and quality. Gorakhpur coal for power is 100% Indian linkage coal; DRI coal is 60-70% Indian with the rest South African via Itochu. Gujarat uses Indonesian coal via Mundra/Kandla for power and South African coal for process.

qa_highlights.question: Does high-phosphorus iron ore from Lloyds pose a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Lloyds supplies only low-phosphorus material, about 15-20% of the mix, roughly 15,000 tonnes a month. Pellet plant capacity is about 8 lakh tonnes against 9-9.5 lakh tonnes of raw feed a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and funding, and how will UP market share and adjacent expansion be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 3,000 crore, with about INR 800 crore spent so far; half goes to mining, with 85 MW solar and the 0.23 million tonne capacity addition in H2 FY27. All funded by internal accruals with no term loans. Management claims over 25% share of the addressable UP market and uses celebrity branding (Ajay Devgn, now Janhvi Kapoor), with other markets to follow as capacity grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are exports a realistic avenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a focus. Construction steel is logistically hard to export and Gorakhpur is inland; Gujarat billets are exported only occasionally.

qa_highlights.question: What drives margins and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have stayed around 17-18% across FY26 quarters, driven by pellet-to-TMT integration and no term debt. Management says margins are sustainable, with solar and FY28 captive mines expected to improve them.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flat-product import pressure affecting long products, and what is the demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat-product price pressure spills over to long products to some extent. Management expects 8-9% steel demand growth, sees Q1 and Q2 as muted by monsoon, and expects pick-up from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the captive iron ore mine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Exploration in UP is expected to finish in 2-3 months and in Rajasthan in about six months. Management reiterated that all three mines should commission in FY28, not FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact and outlook on iron ore and coal?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs rose 9% YoY, about half of which relates to the pellet plant shutdown; 4-5% is price-driven across iron ore and coal. Coal is the main driver, with iron ore impacted mainly by sea freight; management sees no substantial EBITDA erosion for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per tonne fall, and is it one-off or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in line with the historical 17-18% range. FY26 EBITDA per tonne was about INR 8,800 and it is about INR 8,700 now, so the decline is attributed to pressure rather than structural change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue growth slow, and will volumes return to double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the YoY revenue decline as marginal, about 2-2.5%. It expects volumes to be much higher once the H2 FY27 capacity comes in.

risks_watch: Coal and freight cost inflation (Middle East conflict, fuel prices) could keep raw material costs elevated; watch whether the 4-5% price-driven increase reverses.

532726|2026-09.headline: Gallantt Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR111 crores (9.64% margin) from INR185 crores in Q1 on Gorakhpur shutdowns and power outage, with revenue flat at INR1,146 crores.
532726|2026-09.overview: Revenue held at INR1,146 crores, up 13% year on year and flat quarter on quarter, as realisations offset lower volumes. TMT sales fell to 1,65,000 tons from about 1,92,000 tons in Q1 because of a planned Gorakhpur shutdown, and an unplanned extension of a captive power plant outage raised power costs. EBITDA margin compressed to 9.64% from 16.19% in Q1, and PAT fell to INR61 crores. Management attributes the hit to one-time factors and expects recovery from the Gorakhpur capacity ramp-up, power plant restart and higher steel prices in Q3. Coal block allotment in Singrauli and a medium-term greenfield growth plan (to be presented in Q4 FY27) were the main strategic updates.

segments.name: Gorakhpur (UP) integrated plant
segments.commentary: Planned shutdown to integrate expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tons; enhanced capacity expected operational around 10 November 2026, with 85-90% utilisation targeted by end-December. The captive power plant (78 MW, plus 22 MW being added) had an extended turbine-related outage, restart expected within a week.

segments.name: Kutch (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Rolling mill utilisation 68% in Q2 vs 66% in Q1, a 2 percentage point rise. Management expects further structural improvement in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Captive power and renewables
segments.commentary: 18 MW solar at Siddhpur, Gujarat, complete and due to resume by November 2026; 60 MW solar at Prayagraj for Gorakhpur due Q4 FY27. Together expected to save INR30-40 crores per year in power cost.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 recovery expected from Gorakhpur capacity, power plant restart and firmer steel prices; management says price increase of about 20-21% (TMT, September vs a year ago) only reflected from September, so benefit lands mainly in Q3.
Working capital (inventory) expected to normalise in Q3 once new Gorakhpur capacity is operational within 15-20 days.

Remaining FY27 capex of around INR500 crores, split INR400 crores Gorakhpur, INR240 crores mines, INR170 crores solar and INR100 crores Kutch, all to be funded from internal accruals. Note the split sums to more than INR500 crores as stated on the call.
Iron ore blocks targeted operational in FY28; captive mines expected to add about INR2,000 per ton to EBITDA once fully utilised, with partial feed in the first one to two years.
Medium-term greenfield growth plan, built around iron ore and coal blocks, to be presented in Q4 FY27; funding mix (internal accruals vs debt/equity) not yet decided.
Management expects utilisation to improve by 3-5% next year as shutdowns are synchronised and capacity is added.
capex_capacity: Gorakhpur expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tons; enhanced capacity expected operational around 10 November 2026. Management also referenced a 1.3 million ton annual target. Gorakhpur capacity addition at every stage except sponge iron, including 22 MW additional generation to the 78 MW captive plant.

Singrauli coal block allotted August 2026; due diligence under way with a one-month decision window. Operations would take about 2-3 years after a decision; Gorakhpur intended to move fully to this coal, replacing imported South African coal.
Iron ore blocks in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan: exploration in progress, environment and forest clearances underway, FY28 target.
Gujarat: captive power debottlenecking completed in the last month (results in Q3); sponge iron (DRI) plant to commission in Q4 FY27, with benefits from next financial year.
Power outsourcing after the 22 MW addition is about 5-7 MW, to be covered by the 60 MW Prayagraj solar plant in Q4; until then 5-6 MW bought from grid and exchange.
demand_pricing: Management says India finished steel consumption grew 7.5% to about 85 million tons in H1; construction steel demand up about 7% per management. India remained a net importer of finished steel.

TMT prices in September were about 21% higher than a year ago; management says finished product prices rose about 20% while raw material cost rose about INR3,000 per ton in Q2 (coal about INR2,500 per ton, iron ore about 1%).
Brand premium: management says it commands 5-6% over unbranded TMT in UP and 3-4% in Gujarat; Ajay Devgn endorsement (four years) and Janhvi Kapoor recently added.
Gallantt Advance submersible: more than 25% share of the submersible market in UP, per management.
Management expects prices to stay firm into the November-December construction peak, though part of the price gain is being passed on to energy costs.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Singrauli coal block mean strategically and how does it change cost position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the block was only just allotted and is in due diligence; iron ore blocks are targeted for FY28, and securing both raw materials is a basis for the next growth phase.

qa_highlights.question: How will the medium-term growth plan be funded: internal accruals or debt and equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Vice Chairman Dindayal Jalan said the mix is undecided and depends on project size; the company historically relies on internal accruals and limited external borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are TMT prices into the construction season, and what is seen in October?

532734|2026-03.headline: GPIL FY26 consolidated EBITDA flat at INR 1,253 crore, but Q4 EBITDA rose 91% QoQ to INR 439 crore; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%.
532734|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and PAT were broadly stable, with consolidated PAT at INR 802 crore and EBITDA margin at 23%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 41% QoQ and PAT reached INR 280 crore, driven by higher pellet volumes, a one-time carry-over pellet inventory gain (about INR 20 crore) and March mining uplift after environmental clearance for Ari Dongri. Consolidated PAT was below standalone because Ardent Steel was de-recognised as an associate after the stake sale. Management guided FY27 revenue above INR 6,000 crore and EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels, while flagging price softness of about 10% in late April and early May.

segments.name: Iron ore mining (Ari Dongri / Boria Tibu)
segments.commentary: FY26 mining achieved 92% of target; FY26 mining was about 2.7-2.8 million tons versus 2.35-2.4 million tons in FY25. FY27 usable ore guidance is 3.4 million tons (4-4.25 million tons mined, including about 0.5 million tons from Boria Tibu).

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: FY26 pellet output reached 95% of target. Pellet capacity rose from 2.7 to 4.7 million tons after the 2 million ton gas-based grate-kiln plant commissioned in December 2025; FY27 pellet guidance is 4 million tons, with about 3 million tons for merchant sales.

segments.name: Sponge iron
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26. Capacity is being expanded from 0.59 to 0.65 million tons under a CTO received from CECB.

segments.name: Structural rolled products / RR Ispat
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26 and rose sharply from Q4 after mill modifications finished at end-Q3; order book is about six months. Total FY27 rolled output is guided at about 3.7-3.75 lakh tons.

segments.name: Ferroalloys
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26; no further figures given on the call.

segments.name: Galvanised / fabricated products and billets
segments.commentary: Billets reached 96% of target in FY26; sales volumes for galvanised fabricated products increased over the year.

segments.name: BESS (20 GWh project)
segments.commentary: Commissioning targeted March 2027, with long-term supply tie-ups with EVE Power (628 Ah LFP cells) and Shanghai Shenyi Roche. Phase-1 ramp is 5-6 GWh in FY28 (30-40%), about 12-14 GWh in FY29 and 17-18 GWh from FY30. Management guided a 7-8% margin, but said current margins are about 12-13%.

segments.name: CRM complex (0.7 million tons)
segments.commentary: Targeted commissioning March 2027; FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation, or 3-3.5 lakh tons. Management expects about 90% from FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to cross INR 6,000 crore, driven by the new pellet plant running at 80-90% of capacity.
FY27 EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels; management said it expects to maintain about 25%.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant (6 million tons) to be commissioned by Q3 FY27; full-scale mining of 6 million tons in FY28, with about 4.5 million tons of usable ore.
Capex guidance: about INR 1,500-2,000 crore in FY27, and about INR 3,000 crore each in FY28 and FY29, mainly for the steel plant.

Vision 2031 (per the presentation): steel, BESS (Phase-1) and CRM revenue are included. Management said PAT of about INR 3,000 crore implies a margin of about 10%, reflecting lower-margin BESS and CRM. Phase-2 BESS is excluded.

Steel plant: INR 7,000 crore 1 million ton integrated plant (blast furnace route, 50% pellet and 50% sinter feed); construction is expected to start in October 2026 and management expects EBITDA above 20% at full run-rate.
capex_capacity: Ari Dongri mines: EC and CTO received in February 2026 to expand from 2.35 to 6 million tons; phased ramp under way, full scale from FY28.
Pellet plant: 2 million ton natural gas-based plant commissioned in December 2025, running at about 70% in its first quarter; total capacity 4.7 million tons.
Captive solar: from 165 MW to 540 MW; 25 MW commissioned on 21 May 2026, with 100 MW more due by July 2026.
Waste heat recovery power capacity to reach 49 MW after a 7 MW addition; HB wire capacity to rise from 0.1 to 0.115 million tons.
EV fleet: 10 EV dumpers, 24 EV loaders and 15 EV excavators added in FY26. Plans for about 300-350 EV trucks, costing about INR 350 crore including charging infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Benchmark 62% Fe iron ore traded at $95-110/t recently; management expects prices above $100/t for the full year.
Pellet prices softened about 10% from late April/early May 2026 across the supply chain, citing war, summer heat and a weak steel finished-product market.
Domestic pellet price is about INR 9,500-10,000/t ex-plant; management said export pricing is now only about $10 apart from domestic and it may start exporting.
Q4 pellet realisations were held back because the EC delay forced production of 63% commercial-grade pellets instead of high-grade pellets, which earn a premium above INR 1,000/t.

Coal: Q1 FY27 average cost is about INR 12,000-13,000/t. Imported coal is up 15-20% from Q2 because of freight and currency; the company is about 100% on imported coal and may switch to domestic coal.
Mining-to-pellet conversion cost is about INR 2,000/t. Mining landed cost is about INR 3,000-3,200/t in FY27; transport cost is about INR 900/t, potentially rising to INR 1,150-1,200/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY27 mining guidance (3.4 million tons) fallen versus the earlier 4.5-5 million tons?
qa_highlights.answer: 3.4 million tons is net usable ore after beneficiation. Mining will be about 4-4.25 million tons, including about 0.5 million tons from Boria Tibu, with about 0.8-1 million tons of ore bought from the market until post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry-over pellet inventory of about 89,000 tons sold in Q4, the new pellet plant ramp to 70% and about 2-2.5 lakh extra tons of mining in March after EC approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS margin and the lithium cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was planned at 7-8% but is now 12-13%. Cell pricing with EVE is index-linked, so cost changes pass through to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance for 24-25% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects current market levels and the early stage of the year; pellet margins should widen from Q3 as high-grade mix rises after monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steel plant capex rise to INR 7,000 crore from the earlier INR 4,000 crore estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised for an earlier estimation error. The increase reflects a coke oven plant (now needed after import curbs) and a value-added structural mill; EBITDA above 20% is expected at full capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CRM and FY28 utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The first line is expected by end-Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation (3-3.5 lakh tons), with about 90% from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company export pellets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports may start soon if the domestic market stays weak; freight to China is about INR 3,000/t, and domestic prices are about INR 9,500-10,000/t ex-plant.

Diesel-linked transport cost (INR 900/t, potentially INR 1,150-1,200/t) and imported coal price rise of 15-20% from Q2 FY27.
BESS supply chain and competition: the first market entry is expected around September 2026, and components rely on tier-1 suppliers; the lithium price link is index-based.
Steel project funding: about INR 7,000 crore capex with heavy spend from FY28; management said it is self-funded for now, and consent to establish is still pending.
Consolidated versus standalone PAT gap from Ardent Steel de-recognition; INR 36-37 crore write-off of the Godawari Energy pre-operative cost.
Pellet and CRM margins on lower-margin BESS and CRM revenue expansion: management guided about 10% PAT margin in 2031.

532734|2026-06.headline: GPIL Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin 19.1%, PAT margin 12.7%, both flat YoY but softer QoQ on costlier merchant iron ore and imported coal.
532734|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew both YoY and QoQ on higher volumes and better realisations, while EBITDA and PAT were broadly flat YoY and down sequentially on input costs. Iron ore mining volume fell because dumping space was constrained by pending tree-cutting approval on additional land, forcing market ore purchases for pellets. One of the new 2 mtpa pellet plants was shut from around mid-June/July on gas price and iron ore economics, with Q2 pellet output guided to roughly 500 kt. Management shelved the 1 mtpa integrated steel project over water allocation delays and moved the 0.7 mtpa CRM complex to Maharashtra, with commissioning now targeted December 2027.

financial_highlights.metric: Pellet plant (4.7 mtpa expanded capacity) utilisation

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance is said to be on track, with Q1 at 16-29% of full-year guidance. Management said FY27 pellet output will be slightly lower, and a revised figure will come later.

Q2 FY27 pellet production is expected at about 500 kt if the plant stays shut for the whole quarter. Q3 is expected at full pellet capacity, with merchant ore purchases at 25-30%, falling below 10% in Q4 and to zero (fully captive) in FY28.

Mining ramp-up is expected from Q3 FY27 once government land approval comes through (targeted end-September), reaching full capacity by end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Beneficiation plant commissioning is expected by Q3 FY27.

Margin improvement is expected from Q4 FY27 once the beneficiation plant enables higher captive pellet use. Management said CRM incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from the earlier 7-8%.
Vision 2030 target (4x revenue, 3x EBITDA and PAT) was restated without the steel plant. Management said the steel plant is on hold and no timeline is set.
capex_capacity: CRM complex (0.7 mtpa, relocated to Maharashtra near Sambhajinagar): capex raised to INR1,100 crore from earlier INR900-950 crore, including working capital margin money; INR80 crore spent so far; land about INR50 crore for 35 acres; construction from October 2026; commissioning December 2027; funded by INR550 crore debt and internal accruals. Land allotment approval is expected by end-August 2026.
BESS (20 GW... as stated in transcript, battery storage project in Maharashtra): about INR500 crore spent; remaining INR700-800 crore to be spent over FY27 and FY28; commissioning targeted Q1 FY28.
Mining and other capex: about INR2,000 crore for the remaining FY27 and the whole of FY28. No FY29 projection has been given.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant: INR218 crore spent till June 2026; ramp-up from Q3 FY27 and full-scale operation from FY28.

Captive solar: 25 MW commissioned in May 2026; 100 MW under construction, targeted September 2026; 150 MW project in abeyance. Solar storage of 45 MW targeted for Q3 FY27 (management corrected 'Q3 27' to 'Q3 26' and then said Q3 FY27 was intended). Captive solar would reach 290 MW.
Boria Tibbu mine (0.7 mtpa now) expansion to 4 mtpa targeted for FY31, with a 4 mtpa beneficiation plant yielding 1.5-2 mt concentrate (about 40% yield). TOFR filing pending.
demand_pricing: Iron ore prices (global) expected to hover around USD90-100/t; management said it does not expect prices to fall below USD90 soon. Domestic ex-mine iron ore about INR5,500/t.
Pellet prices: ex-Raipur about INR10,000/t now, versus a July low of about INR8,700-9,000/t. Management expects long-term range INR9,000-10,000/t.
Pellet exports: two vessels exported in June-July at about INR9,000/t ex-plant, roughly at par with domestic. Exports have now stopped due to the plant shutdown.
Industry pellet utilisation is about 65%, held back by lower exports, limited high-grade supply and margin pressure. Indian pellet production was about 120 mt in FY26, up from 109 mt in FY25.
Cost: iron ore accounts for about 75% of the raw material cost increase and imported coal for about 25%. Q2 FY27 costs are expected to stay high.
Sensitivity: each INR100/t fall in pellet price reduces annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt of pellets (per management).

qa_highlights.question: Milestones needed before the board revives the 1 mtpa integrated steel plant, and should it now be treated as optional growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Water allocation is the gating item: an LOI was received but the confirmation letter has stalled, delaying the ~9.4 MCM allocation by 6-8 months. Management said to treat the steel plant as an option for medium-term growth, and that Vision 2030 was restated without it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mining production shortfall continue into Q2 and Q3, and when does merchant ore purchasing fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Government land approval for dumping (tree cutting) is expected by end-September, with Q2 mining at the same level as Q1. Mining ramps from Q3 and reaches full capacity by end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28. Merchant ore purchases stay at 25-30% in Q3, fall below 10% in Q4, and reach 100% captive in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the pellet plant shut, and is the gas issue expected to normalise after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas is fully supplied, but the PNGRB guideline has pushed gas purchase value up about 40-45%. Combined with market ore purchases, this made the plant commercially unviable, so one 2 mtpa plant was shut. No clarity on normalisation was given; GAIL has no guidelines, and August is expected to remain a shutdown month.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for iron ore and pellet prices, and what is the sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global iron ore is expected to hover at USD90-100/t, with management not expecting a fall below USD90 soon. Pellet prices were about INR10,000/t after a roughly 10% recovery from the early-July low of about INR8,700/t. Each INR100/t fall in pellet price cuts annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA benefit per tonne do beneficiation, EV fleet and mining cost cuts deliver from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining cost is INR3,000-3,500/t now, with a target below INR2,700/t from FY28. Each INR100/t saving on about 5-6 mt of ore is worth about INR45-50 crore EBITDA. Pellet output is expected to reach about 4.5 mt in FY28, and selling surplus ore is not planned in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised CRM capex, and what incentives and margins are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: CRM capex rose to about INR1,100 crore from INR900-950 crore, which includes working capital margin money. The land is about INR50 crore for 35 acres. Management said incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from 7-8%. Commissioning is December 2027.

The pellet plant shutdown: restart is uncertain, with August expected to stay shut and September possible for the third plant. Gas prices are up about 40-45% under PNGRB guidance and there is no supplier clarity from GAIL.
Full-year FY27 pellet guidance of 4.0 mt is under review and will be lower; the revised figure is pending. Q2 pellet output is about 500 kt if the plant stays shut.
Pellet price volatility: the early-July low was about INR8,700/t, and the sensitivity is INR40 crore EBITDA per INR100/t. Exports have stopped and utilisation across the industry is about 65%.
Coal costs: imported coal is about INR13,000/t vs about INR10,500/t earlier, and Q2 is expected to stay high. Water allocation for the steel plant remains pending with no timeline.
Capex visibility: no FY29 projection given, and the BESS (commissioning Q1 FY28) and CRM (December 2027) timelines have slipped in the past. The BESS commercial ramp depends on tender wins.

532735|2026-03.headline: R Systems Q1 CY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 20.1%, helped by rupee depreciation.
532735|2026-03.overview: Revenue grew 3.5% QoQ and 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore ($62.8 million), with Novigo consolidated for a full quarter and rupee depreciation supporting the numbers. Management said organic revenue was flat QoQ, citing fewer days and Q4 fixed-price true-ups, and that Novigo's restated revenue is about $21–22 million a year after accounting alignment versus the roughly $32 million quoted at acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 115.7 crore (20.1% margin), which management said is about 19% excluding the currency benefit. Utilisation was deliberately reduced to about 80.5% (from a peak of about 84%) to build AI and data bench and COE capacity. Trailing-12-month ACV wins rose to $82.5 million from $76.5 million last quarter.
